CSP uses local scripts/fonts/connect, no objects or frames; inline styles support the existing accessible primitives. Framing, referrers, sniffing and device permissions are restricted. HSTS is one year on this host (no automatic preload or subdomain policy). Ingress access and request-error logs are disabled because request-line diagnostics can contain OIDC codes; use content-free API diagnostics and readiness. The container healthcheck checks the built index and proxied API readiness; its loopback-only TLS probe does not establish external certificate trust.

Identity secrets, local operation and invitations

Create private host directories (0700), mount secret files read-only, and make files readable by the container UID without opening their parent directory. The image's app account owns the mail handoff directory; inspect its UID/GID with docker compose run --rm --no-deps context-api id before setting ownership. The operator needs privileged access to this private directory. Secret managers should supply unique MongoDB passwords/keyfile, TLS private key, MFA keyring, and approved confidential OIDC client registrations. Provider CA files are public trust anchors, mounted separately at /run/provider-ca/.

The versioned MFA file has the existing SeedVault format: an active key ID and keys mapping of IDs to URL-safe-base64 random 32-byte keys. Generate these through your secret manager, retain retired versions while ciphertext refers to them, and escrow a separate encrypted recovery copy. Never put a real example key in source or logs. Local passwords are Argon2id hashes in MongoDB, not mounted plaintext passwords. Browser sessions/challenges/recovery codes are stored as opaque hashes; there is no invented static browser-session signing secret. Installation cursor secrets and authority generations are database state.

For local-only operation mount an explicit [] registrations JSON file and use organizations whose policy is local_only. The SSO engine remains enabled for the Phase 5 policy contract, but there is no selectable provider or discovery request. Existing SSO-required organizations do not fall back when the file is empty or the provider is unavailable. Before retiring a provider, an operator must deliberately approve the policy transition while that registration is still available; a file change alone never changes organization policy.

Enrollment is invitation-only. Follow local identity, human management and management policy to provision an initial owner with explicit root/bootstrap approval. Starting the Compose overlay does not adopt legacy data, claim an owner or activate an org. The shipped delivery port is a private local mail sink, not a production SMTP sender. An operator hands the purpose-bound, expiring single-use code to the verified recipient over an approved channel; never publish/mount this directory through nginx or paste codes into issue trackers. A production delivery adapter can implement the existing MailDelivery port separately; this release makes no SMTP/deliverability claim. Clear expired handoff files under your retention policy. Do not send test invitations to real addresses during verification.

External OIDC and optional Keycloak

Use SSO identity for the exact approved registration schema, pinned provider IP/CA, issuer, client ID/secret and assurance rules. Register only: <origin>/api/v6/auth/oidc/callback and <origin>/api/v6/auth/oidc/logged-out as exact redirect/logout URLs. The provider must support Authorization Code + S256 PKCE. Equal emails never link identities; configured acr/amr assurance and exact provider membership remain required. Keep the confidential client secret in the mounted registry, never the frontend. After a registration/IP/CA/secret change, reapprove with the host operator CLI:

docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f deploy/console/compose.yml exec -T context-api \
  python -m app.cli.contextctl --org-id YOUR_ORG identity configure-sso \
  --registration-id APPROVED_PROVIDER --policy sso_preferred \
  --approval-reference YOUR_REVIEW_RECORD

local_only, sso_preferred and sso_required have their existing meanings; provider downtime supplies no implicit fallback. Explicit temporary break-glass recovery requires the existing operator command, local MFA and approval record. See SSO docs for actual provider/account revocation limits; no instant IdP revocation is promised.

deploy/keycloak/compose.yml is an optional separate single-node production mode Keycloak 26.8.1 + pinned PostgreSQL 16.15 setup. Set KEYCLOAK_ORIGIN, its exact TLS hostname/port, bind address, certificate/key files, unique DB password and initial bootstrap operator secret using its required variables. For initial commissioning add -f deploy/keycloak/bootstrap.compose.yml after the provider Compose file; ordinary operation omits that overlay and does not mount or read a bootstrap secret. It uses start, not start-dev, no public HTTP, no published database port and a persistent keycloak_data volume. Finish provider setup, remove the commissioning overlay/secret from the provider configuration, restrict admin access and configure realm MFA/clients explicitly. It is a starting topology, not an HA, availability or capacity claim. For a managed/external IdP, do not start this stack.

Back up PostgreSQL separately, using its supported consistent database backup and restore process, plus provider signing/encryption keys, TLS keys, client registrations and configuration. MongoDB backups cannot recover this provider. Realm JSON export is configuration handoff, not a complete live database backup. Rehearse provider recovery on an isolated database before relying on it. These choices follow official Keycloak production configuration, container, database and hostname documentation; PostgreSQL pins follow its supported minor releases. Routing follows nginx location/try_files and proxy forwarding.

Maintenance, backups and recovery

Whole-installation backup/recovery remains host-operator-only. Stop domain writers/jobs/MCP, block ingress, and record the old/new image digests, source revision, schema head and all actual worker versions before adoption or restore. Follow the staged migration/recovery procedure, tenant adoption and isolation cutover; explicit organization selection, preservation manifests, reference closure and current evidence are required. Do not bypass activation by changing flags or moving unknown data. Extra orgs stay sealed until their reviewed activation. All old/unscoped workers must be stopped; never overlap worker generations against this database.

For console installations, export COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml:deploy/console/compose.yml in the operator shell and the scheduler's private environment file. This lets the existing backup/restore scripts use the same identity flags and secret mounts; a bare one-off base container does not inherit the overlay. After the reviewed cutover, start with docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f deploy/console/compose.yml up -d context-api console. Keep ingress stopped during restore and use the documented one-off operator container, rather than restoring through a running API.

Use a quiescent database for the count-and-dump backup/rehearsal: the archive is a database-level mongodump, not an online cross-collection snapshot claim. Every collection, including private global identities, memberships, sessions, MFA, OIDC challenges, policy anchors/grants/audit/outbox, machine issuance/jobs, summary coverage/reports and adoption preservation/quarantine is enumerated. Managed restore verification checks each collection, not just one combined count. Preserve mounted secret recovery copies separately from these raw private archives. Manifest key fingerprints are commitments to the random key bytes, not copies of the keys; restore checks reject a missing/mismatched keyring. Recover all retained key versions before starting identity services. Losing those keys cannot be repaired by resetting passwords or disabling MFA.

First restore into an isolated environment; verify exact records/references, validators/indexes, key decryption, current session/policy behavior and search. Treat a rollback to an older authority snapshot as security-sensitive: revoke sessions/keys/challenges and repeat the applicable operator cutover before opening ingress. Derived mongot indexes are rebuilt; neither index volumes nor embedding caches replace primary MongoDB state. Tenant CSV reports are bounded, policy-checked exports; they are never full backups, never expose raw archives, and never authorize database --drop or live restore.

Distribution and real acceptance gates

The public exporter includes dashboard/ source, lockfile, pinned toolchain, licenses/notices, component/browser test source and Docker/Compose/build scripts. It excludes generated builds, node_modules, browser traces/reports, caches, secrets and .private/ at any depth. The guide registry contains only shipped, maintained docs. No separate frontend repository/submodule is introduced.

python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_v6_dashboard_deployment.py tests/unit/test_v6_backup_management_state.py
bash scripts/test-v6-deployment.sh
npm --prefix dashboard run test:e2e -- e2e/hosting.spec.ts
python scripts/prepare_open_source_release.py --output /tmp/acp-reviewed-source.tar.gz

The deployment script builds the real distribution images, uses uniquely named Compose projects, fresh MongoDB/mongot, real TLS and production-mode Keycloak with separate disposable PostgreSQL. It runs the requested management-backup and hosting integration files. Playwright's hosting selector uses those same images, not the older test-only SPA handler. It checks local MFA/session/CSRF, real provider login/logout and console/API/MCP/asset boundaries. Backups are actually materialized and compared to original BSON, including decryption using a recovered keyring; mixed-worker startup is refused. No deployment .env, live database or running production service is used/restarted. Browser certificates, factors, people and secrets are synthetic. Record actual results/engine/runtime limits for every run; successful mock/component tests do not establish this gate. Extract the source archive, re-audit it and run locked frontend install/license/ static build there. Missing mirrors, images, wheels or browser infrastructure must be reported as incomplete evidence, not a passing build.

Complete acceptance and hardening

Use scripts/test-v6-acceptance.sh for the complete Python unit/integration and real browser gate. Supply Node from the pinned dashboard toolchain on PATH, PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE, and V6_ACCEPTANCE_MODEL_CACHE containing the reviewed sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model. Set V6_REPORT_DIR to a fresh ignored private directory. The runner seals the public source inventory and refuses changed source or inherited development selectors. The runner creates authenticated disposable storage, copies MongoDB tools from its pinned image, builds the console/API images, and starts the production-mode reference provider. It disables installation dotenv loading in the integration process; never point these fixtures at an existing database or reuse live credentials. Run the frontend checks as well:

npm --prefix dashboard run lint
npm --prefix dashboard run typecheck
npm --prefix dashboard run test:unit
npm --prefix dashboard run build
bash scripts/test-v6-acceptance.sh

tests/v6_acceptance_matrix.json maps security scenarios to actual integration functions. The runner reconciles every integration source function with JUnit results, including old MCP/three-client suites. Each module uses fresh MongoDB/mongot storage; the complete large-corpus gate uses project-owned Docker volumes, removed at every module boundary and on exit. Smaller development selectors default to bounded tmpfs. A full vector corpus exceeds that tmpfs size; do not shrink the corpus to turn a storage failure into a passing gate. JUnit reports are retained and combined without hiding failed batches. Source fingerprints must agree across the complete run. The runner refuses empty reports, failures, errors, missing cases or skipped tests. Initial isolation rehearsal reports bind operator cutover to the current runtime and test fingerprints. Distribution fixtures also compare the running API image with the checkout runtime fingerprint and record the actual API/console image IDs. Browser JUnit checks reject skipped journeys, missing spec files and empty results; focused selectors and development workloads never produce a complete release manifest. The new credential issuance/offboarding race must leave no orphan credential or receipt. Plaintext delivery is checked across every persisted fixture collection. These checks supplement enforcement tests; an inventory match alone proves no runtime isolation.

The older V1-V5 integration scenarios now run in a fresh, explicitly adopted organization per test. Their initializer and standard-index assertions use the current tenant schema; domain actions and legacy client behavior remain covered. Operator provisioning has a trusted fixture context, while real API requests authenticate their issued credential after discarding that ambient context. The skill-router persistence journey also uses a real stored key. This adapter is test setup, not an unscoped runtime compatibility mode. The separate V6 two-organization and managed-sponsor suites establish the stronger boundaries.

Performance artifacts declare hardware, actual corpus, cold/warm conditions, latency sample counts, concurrency and response statuses. The default event benchmark seeds one million synthetic events, once with a 90/10 tenant skew and once with an even distribution. Other measurements cover 100 stored bounded policy assignments, native Argon2 work, bounded reports and sponsor offboarding with 500 verified clients. Hybrid measurements use 100,000 matching chunk IDs per tenant and the real 384-dimensional local model; the declared synthetic text prototypes repeat, so this is throughput/isolation evidence, not a relevance evaluation. Embedding, lexical, vector and merge durations are recorded separately. The remainder of the Phase 0 reference corpus must be measured and reported separately. A conflict/refusal is not a fast successful request. Passing correctness tests does not certify performance on a dedicated reference host. Keep measurements, logs, screenshots, exports and manual-review notes private. Inspect built assets and artifacts for synthetic secret leakage, and record unmeasured workloads or exceeded targets explicitly.

Automated browser checks require a separate manual review of keyboard order, visible focus and dialog return, true browser zoom, light/dark themes and 360/768/1440px layouts, delayed organization switching, empty/error/conflict and coverage states, and chart table alternatives. Record the tested browser and limitations. Automated accessibility scans alone do not establish WCAG 2.2 AA conformance. Completion of this gate never publishes a release or restarts an installation automatically.

docs/dashboard-foundation.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

V6 dashboard frontend foundation

The React console at /console/ uses bounded session-only shell/security contracts: GET /api/v6/me/console and GET /api/v6/me/security. Implemented management, knowledge, research, creator and monitoring workflows build on this foundation. The console starts disabled (V6_CONSOLE_ENABLED=false). Enable it only after the earlier tenant, identity, policy and managed-machine cutovers have passed and the managed schema-42 control is activated. Enabling the flag does not perform or bypass those cutovers. Schema head stays 42.

Same-origin deployment

Build dashboard/dist using the pinned Node version and npm ci. Deploy that static directory with its licenses.txt beside the existing API, behind one operator-configured HTTPS origin. The backend Docker production image remains API-only. Frontend source, lockfile, tests and licenses are included in public source releases; node_modules, private fixtures, browser traces and generated builds are excluded. This is a separate static deployment, not a Git submodule. Do not run the development server as a production identity boundary.

Set V6_BROWSER_ORIGIN to that exact HTTPS origin and V6_CONSOLE_ENABLED=true on the API (with the previously approved V6 flags and mounted identity secrets). Keep V6_OIDC_REGISTRATIONS_FILE on the backend only. Configure each approved provider's exact existing callback /api/v6/auth/oidc/callback and logout return /api/v6/auth/oidc/logged-out on this origin. For browser HTML requests only, successful callbacks now redirect to fixed local console paths; failures redirect to a neutral fixed error page. JSON clients retain their prior responses. OAuth codes/state never pass to SPA state, storage or frontend URLs.

A TLS reverse proxy should serve /console/assets/ from the build, use index.html only as the fallback for /console/ routes, and proxy /api/ to the existing API. Preserve the original HTTPS scheme using the installation's explicitly trusted proxy configuration. Use this response policy for console HTML and assets (the API keeps its stricter JSON policy):

Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
X-Frame-Options: DENY
Referrer-Policy: no-referrer
Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin
Cache-Control: no-store

Inline styles are limited to the style policy for Radix focus/scroll primitives; scripts remain local external files without unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval. Do not broaden connect-src to the provider: the server exchanges authorization codes. Do not cache identity HTML or /api/v6 responses at the reverse proxy or register a service worker. Use host-only Secure/HttpOnly __Host- session cookies. No API key, IdP token or browser credential belongs in frontend configuration.

Context and personal security

The bootstrap returns only the signed-in person's verified active memberships, organization display names/auth policies, current action-resource tuples and safe own security metadata. It never returns emails, issuer subjects, credential hashes, MFA seed ciphertext or recovery-code hashes. Counts of remaining recovery codes and verified issuer labels are deliberate own-security fields. Each store read is bounded to 101 rows, with up to 100 memberships/identities displayed. This foundation is intended for people with at most 100 organization memberships; expand the own-membership pagination contract before operating above that bound. No global directory is exposed by this contract.

All mutations use the current in-memory CSRF token, same-origin credentials and server policy context. Error recovery refreshes context but never replays a mutation. Session cookies cannot authenticate V1–V5/MCP and bearer tokens cannot authenticate these browser endpoints. Local MFA/recovery, invitation verification, password reset/change, identity linking and own human-session revocation call the existing real session APIs. SSO-required organization entry always rechecks its approved provider and assurance. The UI never offers a local fallback for it. An enrolled local factor may step up a current verified SSO session for a personal security action; it does not replace that session’s approved provider or its organization entry policy. Provider downtime has no automatic fallback. IdP revocation behavior remains the bounded contract documented in SSO identity.

Organization switches first cancel requests and clear React Query data, component state, selections, recovery codes and sensitive forms. A dirty form offers Keep editing or Discard and switch. The new session/CSRF and policy context replace the old ones; every query key includes organization, organization-policy version, policy-anchor revision, membership revision, session-context ID and local context generation. A late response is rejected even if its transport ignores abort. The server still authorizes every request: route guards are only presentation. Old organization URLs redirect to the current verified context without mounting old private content. BFCache restoration hides private DOM before revalidation. Unavailable session verification hides private views and requires reconnection. Cross-tab session changes broadcast only a content-free invalidation message. Nothing private is persisted in browser local/session storage or query caches.

Acceptance and budgets

The three focused component files exercise the real typed client with mocked transport responses; they do not establish cookie, OIDC or persisted replay security. The three focused Playwright files use the real HTTPS API and Keycloak. tests/integration/test_v6_dashboard_browser.py is the corresponding Python integration fixture/selector; without its explicit disposable infrastructure it skips and does not establish the gate. The npm browser command sets up that infrastructure automatically. No real invitations are sent.

The initial JavaScript budget is 300 KiB gzip across all emitted chunks; npm run build measures/enforces it. Targets for a representative cold navigation are LCP ≤2.5 s, CLS ≤0.1 and INP ≤200 ms at 4× CPU slowdown, 10 Mbps/100 ms RTT. These are acceptance budgets, not benchmark results. Provider latency is outside that client-navigation budget. Test at 360/768/1440 CSS pixels, both themes, keyboard-only focus and reduced motion. A real Chrome 200% zoom review supplements viewport/DPR reflow specimens; it does not establish screen-reader, forced-colors, OS-scaling or cross-browser interoperability. Current complete-release evidence and limits are recorded in verification. Automated axe checks supplement screenshot and focus review; they do not replace manual accessibility review. Controls target 44 px, visible 2 px focus, WCAG AA 4.5:1 ordinary text and 3:1 non-text contrast. Status always includes text.

The source/build uses the existing four-block SVG mark and local system fonts. The specimen surface explicitly labels all sample data. Unknown/empty/error and loading states remain distinct; no unfinished module displays pretend live data.

The local browser verification environment used Node 24.22.0, Playwright 1.64.1 and installed Google Chrome 147.0.7727.55 with real MongoDB 8.3.9 and HTTPS Keycloak 26.8.1. The Playwright Chromium download returned an HTTP 403 location restriction, so that bundled browser was unavailable. Results establish the installed Chrome profile; Firefox, WebKit and the unavailable bundled version are not covered. Fixture certificates are disposable self-signed test CAs, not production certificates. No production deployment or real mail delivery is part of this verification.

docs/dashboard-knowledge.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Knowledge workspace (V6 Phase 11)

The console provides a project directory/details/create flow, revision-aware project context, intentional shared memory, canonical skill metadata/versions, and budgeted unified search. It calls session-only adapters under /api/v6/organizations/{org_id}/knowledge. Existing V1 services/repositories remain the domain implementation. No internal HTTP request or machine credential is used to authenticate a human.

Every adapter requires the enabled console, a verified current human session, matching active organization, and an exact action. Mutations also require current MFA, Origin, CSRF, and the existing policy/session transaction fences. Repository queries, pagination/cursors and search candidates use the same tenant and per-action predicates used by managed machine paths. A directory/management role does not grant knowledge access. Read-A and write-B remain separate assignments.

Adapter Required action and resource
GET /projects, GET /projects/{project_id} projects:read + project_directory
POST /projects projects:write + requested project_directory
GET /context, GET /context/{context_id} context:read + exact project
POST /context, PATCH /context/{context_id} context:write + exact project; PATCH requires expected revision
GET /memories, GET /memories/{memory_id} memory:read + exact project or explicit organization knowledge
POST /memories, PATCH /memories/{memory_id} memory:write + same scope/resource; PATCH requires expected revision
GET /skills, GET /skills/{skill_id} skills:read + imported skill; optional exact version/chunk cursor
POST /search search:read intersected with each source's context:read, memory:read, or skills:read resource selector

List/chunk pages are bounded to 50 records, default 20. Status and supported skill filters narrow existing repository queries before pagination. Search uses the existing query/source/filter validation, 50-result maximum and configured token-budget clamp. A supplied project/skill filter needs that search resource. NONE never becomes ALL. Cursors retain tenant/filter/action-policy binding. Denied/foreign records do not contribute candidate totals or citations.

All four memory scopes retain their existing tenant/client addresses. The human workspace exposes global (organization-global) and project memory only. It never accepts a client identity or derives one from sponsorship, owner_id, team visibility or management rights. Requests for agent/project_agent memory fail closed; those scopes remain available through their verified machine identity and explicit memory policy. Memory creation is intentional. Supersession uses the existing same-scope service and preserves the prior record, content and links; archive uses optimistic concurrency. It retains the existing service's ordered-write/retry behavior, rather than claiming a new atomic history system.

Context preserves its current revision, actor and promotion provenance. Existing APIs do not store historical context text snapshots, so the UI does not advertise such history. On conflict, the draft stays in component memory. The user loads and compares the current revision, then explicitly chooses to save against it; there is no automatic overwrite or retry. Session/policy/org changes still clear the old context and sensitive drafts. Skill versions/chunks are stored imports of canonical Git; the workspace has no server file editor or skill mutation route.

Search reports actual source, trust (where the source has a trust classification), source path/version/hash, actor and revision where available, citation key, retrieval methods and returned token budget. Human search uses the existing retrieval pipeline without the opt-in query-text retrieval logger. Terms, prompts, transcripts and result bodies are not added to workforce monitoring or audit. Process-local retrieval counters remain operational observations.

Markdown is rendered with pinned react-markdown, without raw-HTML plugins. An explicit element allowlist excludes images/embedded content; links accept only absolute HTTP(S) URLs without credentials/control characters. Links have noopener noreferrer and no referrer. HTML, scripts, event attributes, unsafe schemes and relative/protocol-relative action links are inert. No remote image is fetched. Source content is never assigned to innerHTML.

Verification

The requested filenames are used directly:

python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_v6_knowledge_adapters.py
python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_projects_api.py tests/unit/test_context_api.py tests/unit/test_memory_api.py tests/unit/test_search_api.py tests/unit/test_hybrid_search_api.py tests/unit/test_memory_service.py tests/unit/test_retrieval_filters.py
V6_KNOWLEDGE_ADAPTERS_ONLY=1 bash scripts/test-v6-isolation.sh
npm --prefix dashboard run test:unit -- src/knowledge/search.test.tsx src/knowledge/memory.test.tsx
npm --prefix dashboard run build
npm --prefix dashboard run test:e2e -- e2e/knowledge.spec.ts

The disposable runner selects exactly tests/integration/test_v6_knowledge_adapters.py. It provisions a real MongoDB replica set and mongot, with matching logical IDs and different private sentinel content in two organizations. Synthetic deterministic 3D embeddings exercise the real production lexical/vector candidate pipelines; they are not a relevance or embedding-quality benchmark. Human fixtures use persisted browser sessions and independently approved operator bootstrap/recovery contracts, never a superuser HTTP token. A separate normal recipient-issued machine credential compares V1 behavior with the human adapters.

Browser verification uses the built SPA, real HTTPS API and disposable provider infrastructure described in the foundation. Its private filesystem fixture channel prepares data and concurrent edits; there are no fixture endpoints in the product. The tests cover safe Markdown, project creation, conflict recovery, memory supersession, skill history, delayed search across organization switch, direct API denials and both themes at 360/768/1440px, keyboard and text zoom. Screenshots and infrastructure logs are local verification artifacts, excluded from public release inventories. Browser engine/version limitations must be recorded with the actual run evidence.

docs/dashboard-management.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Dashboard management workflows (V6 Phase 10)

The management screens in dashboard/ use the session-only adapters over the existing identity, policy and sponsored-machine engines. Schema head is 42; this UI does not bypass activation, create an owner or grant corpus access by role title. Installation recovery stays an independently approved operator CLI operation. See the maintained organization guide and verification status. Knowledge/research/creator and monitoring interfaces are implemented in their separate console modules.

Workflows

People and teams provide authorized directory pages, details, invitations, verified team placement, lead assignments, suspension, offboarding and safe reinstatement. Display-name/team-name prefix filters run before pagination. Human roles, agent permission templates, creator profiles and machine clients have distinct names and purposes.

The policy editor defaults personal use, delegation ceiling and targets to NONE. Each row keeps its action and resource dimension together. Selected IDs, all_in_org, onward roles, depth and UTC expiry are explicit. Assignment previews use the real governance validator without writing a grant, audit or policy anchor. Issuance checks the reviewed target membership revision as well as parent/team generations. Previews reserve no authority. Existing assignments remain effective until separately narrowed, revoked, stale or expired.

Signed-in recipients can inspect their own invitation proposals and paste a single-use delivered secret in My invitations. New local enrollment uses the Phase 9 enrollment/verification screens. Acceptance rechecks the issuer and proposal. Requests use an independent current parent, exact policy and expiry; decisions bind both request and policy revisions. Stale proposals require resubmission. Self-approval and self-elevation are refused by the backend.

Owners can offer a bounded handover from a verified person's detail page. The distinct target accepts the ten-minute offer in Ownership & recovery. The existing root ceiling transfers, the former owner is demoted, and descendants of the old root become stale. A title creates no corpus entitlement. The UI explains when independently approved operator recovery is necessary.

Machine-client approval previews the intersection of current sponsor, team, parent, template and client limits. Recipient/custodian key generation is a separate authenticated operation. Key receipts expose safe metadata; managers cannot retrieve somebody else's token. Explicit rotation revokes the replaced key atomically. Client, key and service-custody revocation stop future authorized work without undoing committed work.

V5 agent permission templates support catalog, create, edit, disable and actual assignment-count impact. V5 requires at least one catalog scope; this ceiling alone grants nothing. Client/credential resource assignments still start at NONE. Template changes leave assigned grants and issued credentials unchanged. rate_limit_profile is descriptive, not an enforced quota. V4 machine sessions have a separate authorized lifecycle from human browser sessions. Project bindings reuse the V4 normalized mapping model, conflict constraints and reviewed revisions. New binding/session governance actions are explicitly declared in the content-free activity projection.

Session adapter enforcement

All adapter paths are under /api/v6/organizations/{org_id}/management and use CurrentBrowser, the existing organization/context check and no-store response middleware. They require activated human/machine governance. V1–V5 bearer routes and MCP continue to reject browser-cookie authentication.

Adapter Selection and policy gate
GET /context Own active assignment envelopes; only independently usable request handles; authorized/current own teams. No foreign ceiling/ancestry graph.
POST /policy-preview Same parent, role, target, same-org resources and expiry validator as issuance; read-only transaction; recent MFA.
GET /members/{id} Existing directory prefilter; safe tenant DTO; visible team links; action-specific current affordances.
GET /own-invitations Exact current organization and authenticated recipient before projection/pagination; no secret/hash.
GET /catalog/{clients,services} Current own/team/org client-read tuples before pagination; verified sponsorship fields; no descriptive owner_id inference.
GET /catalog/templates Explicit current client-management capability; tenant-only safe template fields.
GET /templates/{id}/impact Organization client-management grant; same-org exact template/revision and actual assigned-client count.
GET /catalog/sessions Explicit visible managed client plus action-specific permitted project associations; safe operational fields only.
POST /clients/{client}/sessions/{session}/end Current client management and project-write rights, session/client/org/revision match; shared governance/session fence and transactional audit.
GET /catalog/bindings Action-specific project-read prefilter.
PUT /bindings/{id} / POST /bindings/{id}/delete Current project-write rights for old/new references, same-org project existence, normalized V4 model, exact revision and uniqueness; governance transaction/audit.
GET /ownership-transfers Exact organization and current owner/target participation; bounded metadata.

All cursor pages bind organization, subject, query/filter and policy revision. Foreign filters produce no foreign totals. The screens show page size, not an invented total. Existing governance mutations retain their shared policy-anchor CAS, current browser/membership fence and atomic audit/outbox contract. Missing MFA, revoked authority, conflicts and service failures produce explicit refusal or retry states; failed commands are never automatically replayed.

Secret and browser behavior

Machine plaintext is excluded from query/mutation caches, browser storage, metadata, idempotency and outbox. It is shown only after recipient issuance, for up to two minutes, and copied only by a Copy machine key click. Dismissal, page hide, route/context change or session loss discards the transient view. A retry returns a receipt; lost delivery requires revocation/replacement. This is a state-lifetime guarantee, not a claim of JavaScript memory zeroization.

Setup examples contain static placeholders and a private token-file path, never an embedded token. They use the existing local stdio launcher and explicit Codex/Claude Code/Gemini CLI configuration. Official client references checked on 2026-10-18: Codex MCP, Claude Code MCP, and Gemini CLI MCP. Use the client guide for remote HTTP setup. No new npm or Python dependency was introduced; pinned versions, license inventory and notices remain those reviewed in the foundation.

Reproduction and evidence boundaries

Use the Phase 9 Node/Python/HTTPS prerequisites in dashboard/README.

python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_agent_client_api.py tests/unit/test_client_profile_api.py tests/unit/test_project_bindings_api.py tests/unit/test_agent_session_service.py
python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_v6_management_adapters.py
V6_MANAGEMENT_ADAPTERS_ONLY=1 bash scripts/test-v6-isolation.sh
npm --prefix dashboard run test:unit -- src/people/people.test.tsx src/access/grants.test.tsx src/clients/credentials.test.tsx src/clients/templates.test.tsx
npm --prefix dashboard run build
npm --prefix dashboard run test:e2e -- e2e/management.spec.ts e2e/client-onboarding.spec.ts

The real integration selector is tests/integration/test_v6_management_adapters.py; the disposable runner maps to that exact target. Browser tests use the real API, replica set, HTTPS provider fixture and local test mail sink with fictional identities/credentials. The private filesystem fixture control channel is absent from product HTTP routes. Never point this runner at a production database or mail service. Screenshots, reports, Graphify output and private planning remain ignored and outside public release inventories.

Visual checks cover real populated/empty/refusal screens, both themes and 360/768/1440 CSS-pixel widths, keyboard dialog focus/restore, reduced motion and 200%-equivalent geometry. These do not establish other browser-engine coverage, OS display scaling or a manual screen-reader audit. Build acceptance retains the foundation's 300 KiB aggregate JavaScript gzip budget; no unmeasured latency or productivity result is claimed.

Recorded Phase 10 verification on 2026-10-18: 3,233 Python unit tests; five replica-set adapter integration tests; 19 dashboard component tests (eight in the focused Phase 10 selector); and six real HTTPS browser journeys passed. The requested existing Python selector passed 13 tests. Lint, strict TypeScript, Python type checks, license inventory and public release audit passed. The installed Chrome 147 fallback was used, with Node 24.22.0; browser-engine and manual assistive-technology limitations above still apply. Representative screens and the nested policy/credential dialogs were visually reviewed.

docs/dashboard-monitoring.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Monitoring and audit UI (V6 Phase 14)

Complete-source release acceptance remains pending. The final-fence natural expiry regression now passes its focused real MongoDB gate. See verification and known limits.

My workspace, Team overview and Leadership overview use the Phase 8 authorized read model. Navigation reflects explicit metadata grants; server policy remains authoritative. An owner role grants no automatic monitoring/corpus bypass. Personal views require activity:read:self for the person and its project selector; team views require activity:read:team for the current delegated team and projects. Organization metadata uses explicit activity:read:org. audit:read:org independently authorizes governance. Team leads cannot widen these views by changing a URL, filter, hidden control or organization header.

Visible organization, event-time team, project, client, time window, timezone, bucket and outcome filters are sent to the server. Instants use inclusive start and exclusive end; positive windows are at most 31 days within the served 90-day horizon. IANA timezone changes server bucket boundaries, not stored event times. The browser draws only authorized server buckets, spacing them by time. It does not aggregate an unrestricted event dataset or fill missing periods with zeros. Every chart has a textual summary, sample population and table alternative, with filtered drilldowns. Current own grant expiry is a separate effective-access snapshot, not a historical or team-wide count.

Measure Declared source and denominator
Recorded calls and outcomes Permitted persisted agent_activity gateway reports; not every REST/MCP call
Observed clients Distinct verified event-time machine client IDs; sample population is permitted verified reports, not current inventory or presence
Mean reported latency Finite nonnegative gateway-reported milliseconds; missing/invalid samples excluded; sample count and permitted-report denominator returned
Older unattributed events Retained reports without verified event-time sponsorship; no retrospective identity/team inference
Access review decisions Separately authorized governance access_request_decided events, divided against permitted committed governance events; not all corpus reviews
Grant expiry Own current effective-access source explanations, with effective/ineffective status and recorded expiry; no broad policy graph inferred

Gateway review counts remain unavailable: this stream has no declared corpus review history. No process-local last-observation metric becomes a historical series. A collector's missing, unavailable, stale, partial, complete and absent_history states remain distinct. Declared missing intervals, watermark, collection/retention start, declaration check time, generated time, population and timezone are visible. Zero observations with incomplete coverage are not a complete zero. Coverage describes collection, not a person’s output.

Activity separates verified actor/client, human sponsor, service-account identity and event-time team. Own/team visibility uses the same Phase 8 predicate as counts, buckets and exports. Current worker membership never relabels old events; a team move does not reveal the previous team's history. Legacy actors remain unknown. Last seen is not employee presence or productivity. Leadership metadata grants reveal no corpus text or private agent memory. No prompts, transcripts, response bodies, search terms, guessed hours/model spend, productivity rankings or causal output scores are introduced.

The new session-only GET /api/v6/organizations/{org_id}/audit-diff accepts the bounded governance filters plus event_id. It rechecks audit:read:org, current policy and served retention under the shared policy fence. Its before/after view allowlists status, fixed role, revision/generation, expiry, delegation depth, fixed allowed roles, selector modes and action/resource grant shapes. Resource IDs, target identities, names, approval references and arbitrary payloads are withheld. Missing or unsafe fields say “not recorded / withheld”; legacy or unsupported snapshots are unavailable. Current policy never substitutes for a historical snapshot. Existing event lists and CSV still exclude raw changes.

Summary, timeline, diff and CSV reads aggregate within a bounded snapshot, then recheck the current visibility and perform an atomic majority write against the unchanged policy anchor before delivery. Aggregation holds no long-lived anchor write lock. Revoke/narrow wins if it commits before that final confirmation; governance mutations retain their transactional shared-anchor fence. A new or narrower served-retention boundary also changes the anchor revision. This uses MongoDB's documented conditional single-document atomicity and transaction conflict behavior. Up to three attempts refresh session/policy after a transient database conflict. An exhausted/bounded query returns an error, never invented observations. Detail/report operations have three-second database deadlines; a cold overview has a ten-second ceiling and can reuse a bounded source-invalidated aggregate cache. Its displayed generation time remains the original observation time. Every reuse still rechecks current policy. No-disk-spill bounds remain; these limits are not measured production throughput promises. There are no new dependencies, collections, migration versions or background collectors.

Reports require a separate reports:export organization grant and recent MFA. Preparation records bounded filters; download rechecks recipient, current membership/policy revision, retention and five-minute expiry. After rendering, delivery independently rechecks reports:export as well as activity visibility; longer-lived activity rights cannot replace an expired export grant. Expiry is checked synchronously after the final database await. Reports are at most 5,000 rows and 2 MiB, with server-side spreadsheet-formula neutralization. Narrowing served retention invalidates earlier report receipts; request a new report under the current boundary. The browser fetches using its opaque session/context, validates the same-org report path, bounds bytes, guards late responses by context generation and releases the temporary Blob URL. It stores no CSV, report descriptor, token or persistent data cache in browser storage. Expired/revoked downloads fail; previously authorized saved files cannot be remotely erased. Raw shared metrics and whole-database backup/restore remain installation-operator operations.

Verification

python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_agent_activity_api.py tests/unit/test_content_metrics.py tests/unit/test_search_observability.py
python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_v6_dashboard_read_models.py tests/unit/test_v6_report_visibility.py
V6_SUMMARIES_DEVELOPMENT_ONLY=1 bash scripts/test-v6-isolation.sh
npm --prefix dashboard run test:unit -- src/overview/charts.test.tsx src/activity/activity.test.tsx src/audit/audit.test.tsx
npm --prefix dashboard run build
npm --prefix dashboard run test:e2e -- e2e/monitoring.spec.ts e2e/audit.spec.ts

The integration selector reuses the requested Phase 8 aggregation/report files, extended with actual latency samples, client cardinality, safe diffs and concurrent read fences. Browser fixtures reuse Phase 8 preparation with identical logical IDs and different private sentinels in two organizations. They compare API counts, outcomes, latency samples, permitted event IDs and UTC/Asia-Tehran/ New-York bucket boundaries against independently inspected raw fixture events, not screenshot text or page lengths. Governance totals also reconcile with raw committed events. The second-organization fixture preserves its legacy-retirement anchor and revoked keys, prepares an explicitly empty test root and obtains metadata-only grants through the actual operator approval transaction. This is fixture setup, not a new owner claim or bootstrap endpoint. Journeys exercise real persisted sessions/API/MongoDB, safe diffs, formula-safe CSV, expiry and revoked export authority. Screenshots, local Graphify graphs and planning remain ignored artifacts. Record the actual browser engine/version and outcomes for each run; no other engine coverage is implied.

docs/dashboard-research.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Evidence-backed research console (V6 Phase 12)

The organization console provides research projects, source registration, bounded ingestion, retained snapshots/documents/chunks, working notes, claims and citation relations, structured briefs, candidate/skill-patch review, controlled promotion and advisory freshness. It reuses the existing research services through session-only adapters under /api/v6/organizations/{org_id}/research. Human requests never borrow a machine credential or make an internal HTTP call to a privileged legacy route.

Every adapter requires an enabled console, current verified membership/session, matching active organization and action-specific research-project and linked project resources. Unlinked research requires explicit organization-global knowledge permission. NONE stays NONE. Lists are limited to 50 records (default 20), with tenant/filter/policy-bound cursors. Skill proposal lists prefilter the intersection of research and canonical-skill read access before pagination.

Operation Current authority
Projects, sources, notes, documents, snapshots, evidence, briefs, decisions, freshness research:read for the research project and all linked resources
Project/source/note/claim/citation/brief/candidate/proposal creation and ingestion research:write for each affected resource
Claim assessment, candidate or skill-proposal decision research:approve, readable evidence, reviews:decide, independent verified authorship and exact expected revision
Candidate promotion research:promote, readable provenance and separate context:write or memory:write for the target
Skill proposal/patch Above research action for the skill plus skills:read; approval never applies Git changes
Job inspection/download Current read authority plus revalidation of the original initiating session, membership and write policy

Mutations require recent MFA, Origin/CSRF and the shared session/policy write fences. Decision gates also apply at the repository boundary to existing machine/REST/MCP operations. A normal managed machine cannot decide using content:write; independently approved service-reviewer custody rules still apply. Human provenance uses real human identities, without synthetic API-key IDs. Review events have no promoted-object reference until promotion creates that object. Original authorship is retained by the existing immutable review history. Rewriting a reviewed artifact cannot erase the self-review boundary.

The console accepts at most 8 KiB of submitted text or decoded file bytes, within the existing 16 KiB browser-request cap. Files use submitted bytes only; file URIs are source identifiers, not paths fetched from the server. Supported browser acquisition types are manual, URL, file, Markdown and PDF. Repository, GitHub and RSS acquisition are unavailable in the console. URL acquisition accepts only the registered source and retains the existing provider's public address checks, per-hop redirect checks, byte/time/content limits and disabled environment proxy discovery. DNS resolution is not pinned to the connection; the existing residual limitation in research and security remains. The dashboard adds no arbitrary URL proxy.

Ingestion uses the actual persisted pending/running/completed/failed lifecycle; it does not introduce a background queue. The jobs panel is restricted to jobs started in the current browser session. A JSON download retrieves a freshly authorized, bounded page and releases its temporary browser Blob URL; it is not a permanent server download link. Revoking the initiating authority denies future job-result access without undoing committed domain records. Job failures are projected to fixed, content-free messages, without raw exceptions or initiating session/credential metadata.

Evidence shows citation IDs, exact source/snapshot/chunk locators, retrieval time, source class and relation. Confidence is an explicit authored assessment, not a score inferred from citation counts or source class. Claim evidence is marked bounded at 50 citations; absence does not establish complete coverage. Briefs preserve their stored references, unknowns and contradictions and make no claim of automatic prose synthesis. Freshness compares retained snapshot versions and review deadlines; it never silently replaces promoted knowledge.

Candidate decisions and promotion use exact current revisions. Conflicts keep the draft in component memory; the review dialog requires an explicit reload and reinspection before another decision. Promotion revalidates same-org provenance and uses the existing V1 context/memory services. Their documented ordered-write/idempotency behavior is retained; this phase does not claim a new transaction across every promotion side effect. Skill patches remain inert, generated proposals even when approved, for separate reviewed Git changes and canonical import. There is no filesystem editor or auto-apply endpoint.

All untrusted Markdown reuses the Phase 11 allowlisted renderer: raw HTML, scripts, images/embeds and unsafe link schemes are inert. Patch/locator text is escaped. No research bodies, prompts or search terms are added to workforce monitoring. No dependencies or schema versions are added in this phase.

Verification

python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_v6_research_adapters.py
python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_research_ingestion_api.py tests/unit/test_research_notes_claims_api.py tests/unit/test_research_evidence_api.py tests/unit/test_research_brief_api.py tests/unit/test_knowledge_candidate_api.py tests/unit/test_skill_update_proposal_api.py tests/unit/test_revalidation_api.py
V6_RESEARCH_ADAPTERS_ONLY=1 bash scripts/test-v6-isolation.sh
npm --prefix dashboard run test:unit -- src/research/evidence.test.tsx src/research/review.test.tsx
npm --prefix dashboard run build
npm --prefix dashboard run test:e2e -- e2e/research.spec.ts

The integration runner selects exactly tests/integration/test_v6_research_adapters.py, using disposable real MongoDB and existing domain services. Fixtures reuse logical project/source/skill IDs across two organizations with different private sentinel content. Browser tests use the built SPA and real HTTPS API/provider infrastructure, persisted sessions and fictional recovery factors, via the existing private fixture channel. They produce actual revision-bound decisions and promoted provenance, rather than mocking a review response. Screenshots, Graphify output, infrastructure logs and planning remain ignored local artifacts. Record actual browser/version and results with each run; no other browser-engine coverage is implied.

docs/dashboard.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Organization console

The console at /console/ provides human access to organization management, knowledge, research, creator workflows and authorized monitoring. Its source, tests, lockfile and dependency notices live in dashboard/. It uses the same domain services and policy engine as the agent APIs.

Console serving is disabled by default. An operator must complete the tenant, identity, policy and sponsored-machine cutovers before enabling it. Enabling a flag does not perform those cutovers. Release acceptance is a separate gate; see verification and known limits. The public marketing site is independently hostable and contains no console session or organization data.

Sign in and choose an organization

Local enrollment requires an invitation and verification. Use the delivered single-use code, establish your password and complete local MFA enrollment. There is no public signup or anonymous first-owner claim. An installation operator provisions the initial owner through the explicit reviewed bootstrap.

An organization can be local_only, sso_preferred or sso_required. Required SSO accepts that organization's approved provider and assurance; signing in to another organization's provider is insufficient. Provider downtime creates no automatic local fallback. See local identity and SSO and identity linking for recovery and revocation limits.

The organization picker lists your own verified active memberships. Switching reauthorizes the target membership and provider policy and rotates the browser session, CSRF token and policy context. A dirty form offers to keep editing or discard and switch. Requests are cancelled, private caches and selections are cleared, and late responses from the old context are rejected. Browser Back does not authorize entry to a previous organization. Server checks remain mandatory even when a navigation item is hidden or disabled.

Browser sessions use Secure, HttpOnly, host-only cookies. Passwords, bearer credentials and provider tokens are not stored in browser local/session storage or frontend environment variables. Human cookies do not authenticate V1–V5 or MCP, and agent bearer keys do not authenticate the session-only /api/v6 APIs.

Owner, lead and worker journeys

Person Typical journey Boundary
Owner/admin Inspect effective access, create permitted teams, invite a lead, approve bounded delegation, review offboarding and ownership handover Role titles do not supply corpus access; every operation needs an explicit current assignment
Team lead Work within delegated teams, invite workers, review exact access requests, approve bounded client policy and revoke permitted client metadata Cannot elevate to owner/admin, manage another team, self-grant or recover another worker's plaintext key
Worker Accept an invitation, inspect own effective access, request precise resources, generate an approved client credential once and use permitted knowledge Management visibility does not reveal private agent memory or another worker's credential

The organization-management guide explains each workflow, expiry, revision conflicts and independent approval. Choose NONE, selected resources or explicit all_in_org for each action/resource dimension. An empty managed assignment grants nothing. Read on project A and write on project B never authorize write on A. Organization-global knowledge and imported skills require their own explicit policy.

My security and agent setup

My security supports local password change, MFA enrollment and recovery, verified identity linking, and inspection/revocation of your own human browser sessions. Human sessions are distinct from machine execution sessions. Linking authenticates both identities with step-up and invalidates old sessions; equal email addresses never establish a link. A password reset neither removes MFA nor restores suspended membership. A local factor does not bypass required SSO.

For an agent, first obtain an independently approved bounded client grant. Sign in as the authorized recipient, complete the required step-up and generate the credential once. Copy is explicit. Use the client's safe environment/private-file instructions; never put the token in source, a shared configuration or a browser cache. A retry returns safe metadata, not the secret. Lost delivery requires revocation and replacement. See managed agents and the client onboarding guide.

V5 agent permission templates copy policy onto explicit assignments. Editing or disabling a template does not modify already assigned clients or issued keys. Creator profiles, permission templates, human roles and machine clients are different objects. rate_limit_profile is descriptive metadata, not an enforced rate-limit setting.

Knowledge, research and creator work

The knowledge workspace provides permitted projects, context, skill metadata and versions, memory and search. Context edits use current revisions; conflicts preserve unsaved text. Memories are intentional records in organization-global, project, agent or project-agent scope. Every scope stays within one organization; private agent scopes also retain client ownership. Canonical skills are reviewed in Git and imported per organization. The console does not edit arbitrary server files. See knowledge workspace.

Research shows registered sources, bounded ingestion jobs, snapshots, timestamps, locators, evidence, claims, contradictions and briefs. Reading, writing, research:approve, research:promote and managed review are separate rights. Decisions require an independent authorized reviewer and the exact current revision. Promotion checks every linked target and provenance reference. Skill patches remain proposals for reviewed Git changes and normal import. Untrusted evidence is rendered as inert data. Network controls and existing DNS-resolution limits still apply; see research console.

Creator studio supports profiles/pillars, ideas, novelty and repurposing plans, history, evidence-backed briefs, drafts, immutable versions, review, manual export, publication receipts and manually captured metric observations. The calling human or agent writes prose; the dashboard has no autonomous writer. Editing invalidates review. Publishing needs separate content:publish authority and records a manual receipt; it sends nothing to external publishing platforms. A second client with the same verified sponsor is not an independent reviewer. Ordinary machines cannot review with content:write; only a separately approved service-account reviewer exception permits automation. See creator studio.

Monitoring, audit and reports

My workspace, Team overview and Leadership overview use authorized server read models. Each chart has a textual summary and table, visible filters, source, population, sample count, timezone, coverage, watermark and last-update metadata. Zero recorded events, absent history, an unconfigured collector, missing intervals, stale declarations and partial coverage remain distinct states. Process-local metrics are not historical chart series.

Verified actor identity is separate from event-time sponsor/team labels. Unattributed legacy history stays labelled. A team move does not grant access to the previous team's events. Executive metadata rights do not reveal corpus text or private agent memory. Last seen is not employee presence or productivity. Prompts, transcripts and response bodies are not workforce-monitoring sources; the console does not estimate hours, productivity rankings or model spend.

Queries cover at most 31 days inside the served 90-day horizon. Physical storage retention is installation-managed and declared separately. CSV reports have a 5-minute lifetime and a 5,000-row/2 MiB cap; oversized requests must be narrowed. Download rechecks current authority and expiry, redacts bodies and neutralizes spreadsheet formulas. Reports are not database backups. See monitoring policy and authorized summaries.

Report delivery rechecks natural grant expiry after its final policy fence. Overview data may reuse a bounded, source-invalidated aggregate cache, with its original generation time; authorization is checked for every response. Complete release acceptance remains pending; see verification and known limits.

Operate and verify

Use the deployment and recovery guide for HTTPS, mounted secrets, invitation handoff, optional Keycloak and maintenance cutover. Logical tenant isolation does not isolate data from trusted installation database/backup operators. Organization roles do not authorize whole-installation archives, raw shared metrics or live database restore.

The frontend supplies lint, typecheck, component, build and Playwright scripts. Real MongoDB/mongot/OIDC/browser gates and their limitations are described in verification. Automated accessibility checks supplement keyboard, focus, zoom and visual review; they do not establish WCAG conformance.

docs/database.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Database contracts and migrations

MongoDB is the source of truth for the platform's runtime data. The database contains core knowledge, creator content, research evidence, client identity, sessions, credentials, and audit history. Search indexes are derived state; local model files live in a separate cache.

Collections and validation

The core knowledge collections are:

Collection Purpose Ownership
skills Versioned canonical-skill metadata Organization-owned Git import
skill_chunks Runtime chunks for one skill version Same organization as imported skill
projects Software-system boundaries One organization and explicit directory policy
project_context Durable technical decisions and context Same organization and one project
memories Intentional shared or client-operational memory One org; global/project/agent/project-agent, plus private client ownership
conversations Conversation records kept separate from memory One org/project; not indexed for retrieval
retrieval_logs Optional private query diagnostics without result bodies One org/caller/project; excluded from workforce monitoring

Creator/content collection contracts are documented in content-schema.md, research evidence and review workflows in research.md, and client-profile administration in client-profiles.md. The current validator inventory is app/db/schema.py; the collection and index appendix in codebase onboarding provides navigation to each domain.

Application models reject unknown fields. MongoDB also enforces strict $jsonSchema validators with validationAction: error, so a write that bypasses a repository cannot silently introduce a structurally invalid record. Records use BSON _id values, UTC timestamps, and revision metadata. Mutable operations use revision checks; immutable versions, citations, review events, and metric observations preserve their own historical records.

Embeddable records retain embedding, embedding_model, embedding_dimensions, and embedding_generated_at together. A vector is usable only with a compatible model and dimensions. See embeddings.md, retrieval.md, and content-retrieval.md for vector policy and derived indexes. Conversation records are not automatically embedded or promoted into memory.

Skills, context, and memory use active, archived, and superseded lifecycle states. A partial unique index permits at most one active version of a skill ID. Canonical skill Markdown remains in Git; MongoDB stores its validated runtime representation.

Ownership catalog

Every served domain collection has immutable organization ownership. The source catalogs are tenant inventory, identity ownership, policy, human management, managed agents and summaries.

Private global human identity includes users, exact login identities, local credentials, MFA, opaque browser sessions/challenges, OIDC transactions and identity audit. Organization memberships, provider policy, teams, grants, invitations, review provenance, sponsorship and governed events are tenant state. Schema/adoption/activation controls and cursor secrets are installation metadata. Private global users are not an organization-wide directory. Operator quarantine is outside served domain collections and retains preservation manifests; an unresolved record blocks compatible adoption, even after quarantine.

Strict validators, repository guards and compound indexes protect application writes, not against a trusted database administrator. Whole-database archives include all ownership classes and are installation-operator-only.

Overview aggregates use bounded process memory classified in the summary inventory. MongoDB change streams invalidate source changes before reuse; authorization is never cached. The data cache and observation cursors are recreated after restart/restore. An organization/time covering index supports cold activity aggregation; normal tenant index reconciliation creates it without changing stored identities or migration versions. See authorized summaries for limits and observation times.

Identity and idempotency

Namespaced natural keys produce deterministic BSON ObjectIds where the domain needs repeatable creation. Examples include skill ID/version, chunk ID/version, project ID, and optional context or memory external_id values. Tenant-first compound unique indexes enforce the same identities within one organization. Only explicitly adopted records retain legacy identity version 1; new version-2 identities include the organization. Requests cannot choose the legacy scheme. Adopted ObjectIds, revisions and actors remain unchanged, and validators/lookups support subsequent updates to those adopted objects.

All idempotency is first bounded by organization and current authority. Context idempotency is additionally bounded by its project. Shared memory idempotency is bounded by scope and project; agent scopes additionally include the authenticated client identity. Records without an external ID can use a generated ObjectId. A repeated create must still pass the same authorization checks as the first request.

Repositories and isolation

Asynchronous persistence adapters live in app/repositories/. The shared base owns validated serialization, CRUD primitives, cursor pagination, and revision checks; concrete repositories expose domain-specific operations.

Project context and conversation repositories are bound to one project. Memory repositories are bound to their resolved scope, project, and client where applicable. Content repositories are bound to one creator profile. Trusted tenant context is mandatory. Ownership and action-specific resource fields cover CRUD, counts/distinct, joins, search, references, jobs and exports. These ownership fields are present in query filters, rather than checked only after an unscoped read. API and MCP callers must also satisfy operation scopes and the relevant project/profile grants.

Client ownership is derived from authentication. A caller cannot select another client's operational memory by putting its ID in a request. Organization-global and project records retain their explicitly authorized shared meaning even when an agent authored them. See memory.md for the four supported memory scopes.

Mutable updates match the record and expected_revision, set a fresh updated_at, and increment revision. A stale match produces a conflict instead of silently overwriting another caller's work. Cursor-based lists use stable sort keys, usually (created_at, _id); metric captures use (captured_at, _id).

Migrations and startup

Migration source files define the durable schema changes. _schema_migrations records each applied version under a unique index. Startup applies pending migrations and reconciles standard indexes; Search/Vector Search indexes are reconciled separately through MongoDB's search management interface.

Migration range Contracts introduced or extended
1–5 Core collections, skill/context/memory embeddings, API keys, audit
6–12 Creator/content schema, profile grants, content embeddings, approval audit, publication receipts, metric provenance
13–21 Research schema and source registry, structured briefs, immutable review decisions, controlled promotion, skill proposals, evidence-backed content briefs, freshness
22–32 Agent clients, credentials, project bindings, caller provenance, agent memory scopes, sessions, gateway retry controls
33–35 Reusable client profiles, profile lifecycle, Gemini client type
36 Explicit tenant schema, preserved legacy identity and resumable adoption
37 Tenant isolation, search/cursor/job ownership and sealed activation
38 Private global local identity, MFA and hashed browser sessions
39 Exact issuer/subject OIDC, assurance and organization switching
40 Coupled policy, delegation, governance audit/outbox and shared fencing
41 Teams, invitations, access requests and membership lifecycle
42 Verified machine sponsorship, service accounts and one-time credentials

Migrations preserve existing records where a contract is widened. For example, migrations 2–4 add embedding metadata to core knowledge collections, migration 9 extends current content representations, and migration 27 adds client-scoped memory ownership. Migrations 18 and 20 preserve research provenance on promoted knowledge and content briefs. Migrations 33–34 add reusable client profiles without widening existing client grants.

The current schema head is 42. The identity/policy/management transitions are guarded operator cutovers, not an instruction to start a full console against an unadopted database. Follow staged migration/recovery. An API flag does not substitute for explicit adoption or worker exclusion.

Review the exact migration before an upgrade or rollback. Some migrations refuse automatic reversal because removing authored content, review decisions, credentials, or provenance would destroy durable state. A successful schema rollback is not a substitute for a verified backup.

Recovery and verification

Full-database backups include every durable collection and retain stored vectors. Search indexes are rebuilt from restored documents; they are not a second source of truth. Restore verification compares collection counts in an isolated temporary namespace. See backup.md for operational commands and recovery limits.

Run the real database checks against a disposable stack:

bash scripts/test-v6-isolation.sh

The integration suite writes fixtures. Give it its own database and volumes, following Contributing. It checks repeated initialization, required indexes, strict validation, CRUD, pagination, optimistic updates, and ownership boundaries against the actual replica set.

docs/deployment.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Deployment

For the implemented V6 console, use console deployment: its same-origin TLS overlay, mounted identity secrets and explicit cutover replace the older loopback-only API topology below. Authentication-disabled multitenant operation is refused. Do not expose the base API over public HTTP.

Authentication

Knowledge APIs and MCP require a scoped credential by default; health checks are public. Issue the first operator key through the database-backed CLI:

docker compose exec -T context-api python -m app.cli.contextctl --org-id YOUR_ORG --json keys create \
  --name codex --scope search:read --scope skills:read | jq -r .key

Inside the platform, because contextctl keys reaches MongoDB directly and MongoDB is on the internal network with no host port. python -m app.cli.contextctl because the image installs the application's dependencies but not the project, so there is no contextctl console script in it.

The operator key is shown once; the platform stores only a hash. Subsequent client credentials can be issued through authenticated gateway administration. API_AUTH_ENABLED=false is refused for tenant domain traffic. An application whose authentication decision was never made fails closed with a 500 rather than serving. Health endpoints stay open because Docker's healthcheck has no credential and readiness carries no knowledge.

AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED (default true) records who was allowed or refused what, and who wrote something — never what was read or written. API_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES (default 1 MiB) bounds a request body, refused from Content-Length before anything is read.

The containers built here run as a non-root user with no capabilities and a read-only root filesystem; the official MongoDB images keep their capabilities because their entrypoints need CHOWN, SETUID, and SETGID to start. Every service runs with no-new-privileges.

See security.md for scopes, project authorization, what a refusal says, what reaches the logs, and how to check a deployment.

Secrets

Development may use scripts/generate-dev-secrets.sh. Production deployment must provision unique root/application/synchronization passwords and a MongoDB keyfile through its secret manager, then point the corresponding *_SECRET Compose variables at those files. The mongot synchronization password file must be non-empty and must not end in a newline. Do not commit .env, secret files, or generated credentials, and do not pass administrative or synchronization credentials to context-api. For local Compose, the generator protects the containing secrets/ directory with mode 0700 and makes its bind-mounted files container-readable; every container mount remains read-only.

Changing the root username after the data volume has been initialized does not rename the existing root user. Credential changes should be performed as an explicit administrative rotation. The idempotent bootstrap job updates the application and synchronization users' passwords and roles to match the supplied secrets and least-privilege definitions.

Network and persistence

MongoDB, mongot, and bootstrap are attached only to the Docker network agent_context, which is marked internal. MongoDB and mongot declare their container ports for service discovery but publish no host ports. The API is dual-homed so it can reach MongoDB privately while publishing port 8000 to 127.0.0.1 by default. Put a separately managed TLS reverse proxy in front of the API if it must cross a host boundary.

Database and Community Search files live in the named volumes agent_context_mongodb_data and agent_context_mongot_data. docker compose down preserves them. Removing either volume is destructive and is intentionally not part of any Make target.

Local embedding model files live in agent_context_embedding_models, mounted at /var/cache/embeddings and owned by the non-root container user. The model is downloaded once into that volume; removing it only forces another download. On an air-gapped host, populate the volume out of band and set EMBEDDING_ALLOW_DOWNLOADS=false. Measure both disk and resident memory for the configured model, its dependencies, and corpus, in addition to MongoDB and search. Each API worker loads its own model instance.

Startup and readiness

The startup sequence is:

  1. The official MongoDB 8.3.9 image creates the root user on an empty data volume.
  2. mongodb-init authenticates as root, initializes rs0 when necessary, waits for primary election, creates the monitoring privilege, and creates/updates the application and dedicated mongot synchronization users.
  3. MongoDB's container health check requires authenticated primary status.
  4. mongot starts only after bootstrap succeeds and MongoDB is healthy. Its health endpoint becomes serving after replication/configuration initialization.
  5. FastAPI starts only after mongot is healthy. Its lifespan creates a timezone-aware PyMongo Async client, validates the database, replica set, and indirect coordinator path, applies pending database migrations, and idempotently reconciles standard indexes.
  6. The lifespan reconciles every Search index, then loads the configured local embedding model once and reconciles every vector index for the dimensions that model reports. An unusable model or an unreachable search coordinator is logged and reported by readiness rather than crashing the process, so the container is never reported healthy while it cannot embed or retrieve.
  7. Startup fails if database initialization or required index creation fails. The MongoDB client and the embedding model are released during shutdown.

GET /health/live reports process liveness. GET /health/ready returns HTTP 503 unless the application database is reachable, the configured replica set is primary, a non-mutating $listSearchIndexes coordinator request succeeds through mongod, the configured embedding model is loaded, and all six search indexes — two each over skill chunks, project context, and memories — are queryable, with each vector index matching the model's dimensions. The response reports the model, its dimensions, and its device, plus each index's name, status, and queryability. A newly created index reports BUILDING until mongot finishes it. Setting EMBEDDING_ENABLED=false removes the embedding and vector-search requirements from readiness; the Search indexes stay required because lexical retrieval does not depend on the model. The application never opens a direct connection to mongot.

The readiness body also carries an api block naming the running build and its uptime, and each check publishes acp_dependency_ready{dependency=…} as 1 or 0 so an alert can fire without anything parsing JSON.
