The container health check calls this endpoint every ten seconds, which is what keeps those gauges as fresh as readiness itself.

Application and Uvicorn logs are emitted as one JSON object per line on stdout. Set LOG_LEVEL to CRITICAL, ERROR, WARNING, INFO, or DEBUG (case-insensitive). HTTP access events carry a request_id, the method, the path, the matched route template, the response status, the duration, and whatever the call turned out to be about — the operation, the project, the query identifier, and the result count. The request ID is returned in the X-Request-ID response header, and an acceptable one supplied by a caller in that header is adopted rather than replaced, which is how an MCP tool call and the API request it became share an identifier across two processes' logs. Query strings are not logged. Embedding events log only the model name, dimensions, device, duration, and error type.

METRICS_ENABLED (default true) publishes GET /metrics in the Prometheus text exposition format to a caller holding system:read: request, MongoDB, embedding, retrieval, and per-index latency at p50/p95/p99, plus counters for API requests, MCP calls, memory writes, skill imports, and failures. Nothing is pushed anywhere, no exporter runs, and no second port is opened — a self-hosted scraper reads the API's own port. A scrape performs no dependency checks, so monitoring never lands on the critical path of what it monitors. Setting it to false removes the endpoint rather than serving an empty one, and stops the driver publishing a timing per MongoDB command. See observability.md for the full catalogue and the scrape configuration.

Hybrid ranking is tuned through RETRIEVAL_WEIGHT_*, RETRIEVAL_RECENCY_HALF_LIFE_DAYS, RETRIEVAL_DUPLICATE_OVERLAP, RETRIEVAL_TOKEN_BUDGET, and RETRIEVAL_MAX_TOKEN_BUDGET. Each is validated at startup, so an incoherent weighting or a default budget above its maximum stops the process from starting rather than surfacing on the first query. Changing them changes ranking only; no reindexing or re-embedding is required. Research packets use their own RESEARCH_RETRIEVAL_TOKEN_BUDGET (default 8000) and RESEARCH_RETRIEVAL_MAX_TOKEN_BUDGET (default 16000) so V3 research retrieval cannot retune V1 engineering or V2 content budgets.

Every search reports what it did to the structured log as retrieval_completed, carrying a generated query_id, the project, the retrieval method, the requested sources, the result count, and the latency. The query text is deliberately excluded, so shipping these logs never ships what somebody asked. RETRIEVAL_LOG_ENABLED (default false) additionally stores one retrieval_logs document per search, query text included; that is a retention decision, which is why it is opt-in rather than a default. Retrieved content is never logged or stored either way — a stored record references results by key.

The MCP server runs as its own process and is started by the client that talks to it: docker compose --profile mcp run --rm -T mcp, or python -m app.run_mcp locally. It speaks its protocol over stdin and stdout, so it publishes no port, and it writes its logs to stderr because a log line on stdout would corrupt the protocol stream. It reaches the platform through the Context API on the private network and is configured with no database credentials at all — the component an agent talks to directly is the one that can do the least. MCP_SCOPES, MCP_PROJECT_IDS, and MCP_PROFILE_IDS narrow what one server may do, which V1 projects it may reach, and which V2 creator profiles it may reach. Leaving a local allowlist empty removes that additional restriction; it never overrides the API credential or linked client's grants. When the API requires a key, point MCP_API_TOKEN_FILE at a mounted secret holding one — the server presents it as a bearer token and the API's own refusals reach the agent as tool errors that name a missing scope but never a refused project or profile. See mcp.md.

See search.md for the unified POST /api/v1/search interface, its retrieval metadata, and its logging hooks. See mongot.md for search-service operating requirements and database.md for persistence details. Canonical skill deployment and import operations are described in skills.md, the local embedding model in embeddings.md, vector, lexical, and hybrid retrieval in retrieval.md, project boundaries and their durable context in projects.md, and intentional memory in memory.md. Codex configuration, the startup order it depends on, and its troubleshooting are documented in codex.md, and the contextctl operator commands — importing skills, rebuilding search indexes, issuing keys, backup, and restore — in cli.md. API-key authentication, authorization, and container hardening are in security.md; the backup strategy, retention, verification, and the disaster-recovery procedure are in backup.md. Backups cover MongoDB alone: search indexes are derived state that contextctl skills reindex rebuilds, so a restore is followed by a reindex and a readiness check rather than by restoring an index. The vectors are inside the documents and travel with the backup; re-embedding is needed only when the model or its stored-vector compatibility changes.

docs/embeddings.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Local Embeddings

The self-hosted embedding layer provides an EmbeddingProvider abstraction, one local sentence-transformer-compatible implementation, model-tagged vectors on skill chunks, and readiness reporting for the loaded model. No hosted embedding API is used or supported in this mode. Lexical, vector, and hybrid retrieval are documented in retrieval.md; the MCP gateway accesses them through the API.

Components

Module Responsibility
app/embeddings/base.py EmbeddingProvider protocol: embed_text, embed_documents, load, health, close
app/embeddings/config.py EmbeddingConfiguration, the frozen contract built from settings
app/embeddings/local.py LocalEmbeddingProvider, device resolution, batching, retries
app/embeddings/types.py EmbeddingVector, EmbeddingModelInfo, EmbeddingHealth, shared limits
app/services/embedding_service.py Active-model policy and provider composition
app/models/embedding.py The persisted vector fields and their invariants

Callers depend on the protocol, never on the backend. build_embedding_service() is the only place that selects LocalEmbeddingProvider, so a different provider can be introduced later without touching services, repositories, or routes.

Configuration

Variable Default Meaning
EMBEDDING_ENABLED true When false no provider is built and readiness does not require one
EMBEDDING_MODEL sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 Model repository id or local directory
EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS 384 Expected output dimensions, validated against the loaded model
EMBEDDING_DEVICE auto auto, cpu, cuda, or mps
EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE 32 Texts sent to the model per encode call
EMBEDDING_MAX_BATCH_TEXTS 256 Hard limit on texts per embed_documents call
EMBEDDING_MAX_TEXT_CHARACTERS 20000 Hard limit on one text
EMBEDDING_NORMALIZE true Produce unit vectors, which cosine similarity expects
EMBEDDING_MAX_ATTEMPTS 3 Encode attempts before reporting the model unavailable
EMBEDDING_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS 0.5 Base delay for exponential retry backoff
EMBEDDING_MODEL_CACHE_DIRECTORY unset Where model files are stored; /var/cache/embeddings in containers
EMBEDDING_ALLOW_DOWNLOADS true Set to false for air-gapped hosts that already hold the model

Configuration is validated twice: Settings rejects invalid environment values, and EmbeddingConfiguration re-validates its own invariants so the provider is safe to construct directly from a CLI or test. The same environment always produces an equal, frozen configuration, so the metadata stored with vectors is deterministic.

Remote code execution from model repositories is disabled (trust_remote_code=False) and is not configurable.

Model loading

The model is loaded once per process, behind a lock, so concurrent first requests share a single load. Loading and encoding both run in worker threads through asyncio.to_thread, so a CPU-bound model never blocks the event loop. Encoding is serialized because one loaded model is a shared, non-thread-safe resource.

Dimensions are discovered from the model rather than assumed: the provider reads whichever dimension accessor the backend exposes and otherwise probes the model with one short text. If the discovered value differs from EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS, loading fails with EmbeddingDimensionError instead of producing vectors that could never be searched together.

A failed load is not cached, so the next readiness probe retries it. Transient encode failures are retried with exponential backoff up to EMBEDDING_MAX_ATTEMPTS before EmbeddingUnavailableError is raised.

Devices

EMBEDDING_DEVICE=auto prefers CUDA, then MPS, and falls back to CPU when no accelerator is present, so the platform runs on a CPU-only host. An explicitly requested accelerator that is not available fails with EmbeddingConfigurationError rather than silently running on CPU.

Stored vectors

Every vector is stored with the model metadata needed to keep it comparable:

{
  "embedding": [0.0123, -0.0456, "..."],
  "embedding_model": "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2",
  "embedding_dimensions": 384,
  "embedding_generated_at": "2026-01-01T12:00:00Z"
}

Three layers prevent incompatible vectors from being stored side by side:

  1. The document model requires the four fields together and requires the vector length to equal embedding_dimensions.
  2. EmbeddingService.verify() rejects any vector whose model or dimensions differ from the active configuration, so a vector from another model cannot reach a repository.
  3. The skill_chunks MongoDB validator accepts only arrays of doubles within the supported bounds, with complete metadata.

skill_chunks carries a standard (embedding_model, embedding_dimensions) index so a model migration can find the chunks that still need re-embedding. The Vector Search index over these vectors is documented in retrieval.md; its dimensions come from the loaded model, so it always matches the vectors described here.

Skill chunk embedding

SkillService accepts an optional chunk embedder. When one is configured, every chunk of a new skill version is embedded before the version is installed; if embedding fails, no version is written at all. Re-importing unchanged content stays a no-op and does not re-embed.

python -m app.cli.import_skills                  # embed with the configured local model
python -m app.cli.import_skills --no-embeddings  # store chunks without vectors

The importer reports Chunks embedded alongside the existing statistics.

Health

GET /api/v1/health/ready includes the embedding model:

{
  "status": "ready",
  "mongodb": true,
  "database": true,
  "replica_set": true,
  "mongot": true,
  "embedding": {
    "enabled": true,
    "available": true,
    "model": "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2",
    "dimensions": 384,
    "device": "cpu"
  }
}

Readiness fails with 503 when embeddings are enabled but the model cannot be loaded. When EMBEDDING_ENABLED=false, no provider is built and embedding never blocks readiness.

Startup verifies the model but does not crash the process when it is unusable; the failure is logged as embedding_model_unavailable with the model name and error type, and readiness reports it. Successful loads log embedding_model_loaded with the model, dimensions, device, and load duration. Log records never contain credentials or document content.

Changing the embedding model

Vectors from different models must never be mixed. To migrate:

  1. Re-embed every affected document with the new model.
  2. Rebuild the vector index for the new dimensions, which startup reconciles automatically.
  3. Verify retrieval quality.
  4. Switch EMBEDDING_MODEL and EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS together.
  5. Remove the superseded vectors only after the migration succeeds.

Because the active configuration is enforced on write, a mismatched EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS fails at startup rather than corrupting a collection.

Offline and air-gapped hosts

Model files are stored in EMBEDDING_MODEL_CACHE_DIRECTORY, which the Compose deployment maps to the named agent_context_embedding_models volume. Populate the volume once with an outbound connection, or copy the model directory in, then set EMBEDDING_ALLOW_DOWNLOADS=false and point EMBEDDING_MODEL at the local path. The platform needs no hosted embedding service at any point.

Verification

python -m pytest
RUN_EMBEDDING_MODEL_TESTS=1 python -m pytest tests/integration/test_local_embedding_model.py

The opt-in checks load the configured model on CPU, assert the discovered dimensions, assert normalized unit vectors, and assert that payment idempotency is closer to How do we prevent duplicate payment requests? than to unrelated text.

docs/human-organization-management.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Human organization management

Session-only member, team, invitation and access-request APIs use governance transactions and current verified organization context. The implemented organization console consumes them; verified machine lifecycle builds on managed agents. Public signup, anonymous owner claims and private global user-directory search are not exposed. This reference retains the explicit schema-41 stage of the staged cutover; current full head is 42.

Activation and storage

V6_HUMAN_MANAGEMENT=false is the default. Enabling it requires V6_MANAGEMENT_POLICY=true and the verified Phase 1–5 prerequisites. Migration 41, allocated after actual head 40, requires an explicit stopped-writer operator cutover. API startup cannot silently perform this cutover. Stop every API, stdio/HTTP MCP consumer and background writer, verify a restorable operator backup, then use the operator environment with the new flag enabled:

contextctl --org-id fictional-org management activate \
  --writers-stopped --worker-schema-version 41 \
  --approval-reference fictional-reviewed-cutover

Restart only schema-41 workers. The tenant control seal and local/SSO/policy markers reject schema-40 processes. Adopted-key adapter records are also upgraded to the legacy_adoption_v41 discriminator with an advanced revision, preserving exact reviewed envelopes/expiries. The old queued-job resolver checks the previous discriminator and refuses these records even without consulting a schema marker. The domain schema remains 37; worker compatibility is a separate recorded field. Repeating migration 41 is safe. Unknown populated reserved collections are refused. Rollback requires a sealed, verified operator restore; tenant restore is not exposed.

The following new collections are tenant owned and accessible only through the human management boundary: teams, team_memberships, management_invitations, access_requests, access_decisions. _human_management_control is installation metadata. Every natural-key index starts with org_id. Validators reject unknown fields. Existing memberships, ObjectIds, authored knowledge, actor history and governance events are preserved. Neither ordinary corpus search nor an installation backup changes ownership.

Phase 5 bootstrap deliberately did not assign team management capabilities. Activation creates no grants. To approve those capabilities, an independent host operator reviews a bounded JSON RootApproval document and runs:

contextctl --org-id fictional-org management approve-root \
  --user-id fictional-owner --policy-file reviewed-root.json \
  --writers-stopped --worker-schema-version 41 \
  --approval-reference fictional-independent-root-review

The file contains tuples, ceiling, targets, allowed_roles, and an aware expires_at no more than 365 days away. Use tuples contain only capabilities allowed to an owner by the fixed management catalog. The ceiling contains the exact reviewed capabilities/resources the owner may issue, including any previously approved corpus ceiling that should remain delegable. Existing owner corpus-use tuples remain unchanged. This is the explicit operator bootstrap/recovery exception, with approval reference and before/after policy in transactional governance audit/outbox. It is not a browser self-grant.

For example, creating teams needs an explicit teams:manage / organization / include [fictional-org] tuple. Reading them needs teams:read with that organization or named team IDs. Inviting a previously unknown person without a team needs independently reviewed members:invite and grants:delegate member selectors and parent targets that explicitly cover future members (all_in_org). Such an approval is consequential and explicit; NONE remains the default. A named-team invitation instead uses that exact team envelope, as described below. Included resource IDs must already exist; creating a team and reviewing its named ceiling can be separate operator steps.

Root approval replaces the management-use policy and full issuance ceiling, updates generation/revision, and permanently invalidates old descendants. It does not merge unrelated permissions into an implicit broad ceiling. An existing unique root is updated, so accepted ownership handover still transfers one exact governance root. Use-only personal corpus recovery is not transferred. Unbound Phase 5 lead assignments remain preserved but become ineffective under schema 41 until a new explicitly reviewed named-team assignment is issued. No team is inferred from a name, email, owner field or dormant broad selector.

Boundaries and team delegation

All endpoints require an opaque human browser session, HTTPS, current active organization and X-Session-Context. Every mutation also requires matching Origin, CSRF and recent MFA. Bearer REST/MCP cannot use these cookies. Submitted org/team/user identifiers select resources; they never establish authority.

Member directory DTOs expose only org_id, user_id, tenant display name, role, membership status and revision. Searches are bounded display-name prefix queries, qualified by org and permitted members/teams before pagination. There is no global email/user search, factor/login data or other-org membership lookup. Cursors are signed and bound to org, observer, filters and policy revision. A policy change requires a fresh page. Team member DTOs additionally expose the named team edge's status and revision for safe conditional edits.

Owner/admin role titles do not themselves grant team or directory access. Leads require explicitly delegated named-team tuples. In Phase 6, direct broad member management grants cannot bypass a lead's team boundary. Leads may read, invite, suspend/reinstate team members, inspect grants and approve requests only inside their currently delegated team and resource ceiling. Team structure creation/renaming/suspension uses the fixed teams:manage permission; the initial lead template does not receive it. Placing an existing person into a new team requires explicit team management and cannot be used by a lead to acquire control over arbitrary people. A lead cannot change their own team edge.

Team-scoped Issue commands add team_id and expected_team_generation. The server captures the subject's current team-edge revision. The complete assignment ancestry, membership revision, active team generation and active edge revision are checked on each policy resolution. A team suspension advances its generation. Suspension/removal of an edge advances its revision. Reinstatement advances rather than resets these values; old assignments/descendants stay dead.

A lead's parent assignment must itself be bound to the same named team and hold grants:delegate / team / include [that-team]. It can issue a leaf assignment to a currently verified member of that team even when the new person's user ID was not previously known. Such a leaf has depth zero, NONE targets and no allowed child roles. Its action/resource tuples must fit that same parent's ceiling, role and expiry. This explicit team envelope never substitutes a broad member target set or permits recursive widening.

Invitations and requests

An invitation stores the exact bounded reviewed policy, parent ID/generation, optional team generation, issuer, recipient membership revision and expiry (maximum seven days, within the assignment lifetime). The same parent must hold both invitation and delegation authority for the selected member/team. The secret is random, purpose-hashed and never returned by management APIs or audit. Delivery uses only the private test sink. The usual local invite/verification challenge is 30 minutes; a longer proposal expiry does not extend either challenge.

New local recipients use the existing invitation-only enrollment and browser- bound verification endpoints. Existing accounts authenticate their existing password and MFA; an invitation cannot reset credentials or MFA. An already verified active member may accept through POST /api/v6/me/invitations/accept using their own recent-MFA session and the delivered secret. The narrow self route can accept an invitation for another organization, but it cannot switch active org or satisfy that organization's SSO policy. Explicit switching still requires the target provider/assurance from Phase 4.

A local email selects only the exact local identity namespace. It never links an OIDC identity with the same email. SSO users need an explicitly linked local identity for local enrollment; no JIT registration or email-based account merge is introduced. Tenant management responses do not reveal whether a local login already existed globally.

Enrollment and verified acceptance recheck current issuer membership and parent ancestry, reviewed resources, role, target, expiry and team boundary. Verification, one-use consumption, active membership, team edge, assignment and governance audit/outbox commit atomically. A revoke/narrow/suspend racing acceptance touches the same org policy anchor. Losing transactions refuse or require a fresh retry; they do not issue from a saved snapshot. Revoked/expired proposals cannot restore suspended memberships or team edges. Renewing a pending invitation creates a new reviewed record, revokes previous pending proposals/challenges, advances the pending membership revision and preserves history. Old verification links cannot activate the renewed proposal. A lead cannot use a lower requested role to demote an existing higher-role member.

Access requests store the exact requested policy, membership revision, policy revision, deadline (at most seven days) and immutable identity of the requester. They grant no authority. Submission validates that the proposed independent parent and resources belong to the org and can cover the request. The returned policy_revision is the revision after submission. Approval/denial must present that exact revision and the current request revision. Any intervening org policy mutation makes the request stale; the requester cancels/resubmits rather than silently changing it. This is deliberately conservative.

Only the named parent's currently authorized subject can approve, inside that parent's current action/resource/role/team/expiry envelope. A requester cannot approve themselves; unrelated assignments cannot supply missing authority. Decision commands contain no replacement policy. A unique tenant/request index, conditional pending revision, shared-anchor CAS, assignment insertion and durable decision/audit/outbox transaction allow exactly one decision. No decision edit or deletion endpoint exists. Expiry is checked per operation, independently of cleanup. Histories remain available within authorized boundaries.

API surface

Paths below are relative to /api/v6/organizations/{org_id} unless marked self. The Phase 5 assignment/delegation and accepted ownership-transfer APIs remain available and use the same new team-aware policy evaluation.

Method/path Gate and behavior
GET /members members:read named member/team; bounded prefix and cursor
GET /members/{user_id}/effective-access grants:read subject/team; authorized sources only
POST /members/{user_id}/suspend members:suspend, expected membership revision
POST /members/{user_id}/reinstate members:reinstate, verified membership, new revision
POST /members/{user_id}/offboard members:suspend, preserved revoked membership
GET /teams explicit org/named teams:read; lead sees delegated teams
POST /teams explicit org teams:manage, immutable tenant/team ID
PATCH /teams/{team_id} org/named teams:manage, expected team revision
GET /teams/{team_id}/members permitted named team and member projection
POST /teams/{team_id}/members/{user_id} explicit placement/lifecycle authority; expected team and edge revisions; zero means a new edge
GET /invitations authorized member/team proposal DTO; no hashes/email
POST /invitations members:invite plus same parent's current issuance envelope
POST /invitations/{id}/revoke current invitation authority and expected revision
POST self /api/v6/me/invitations/accept exact verified recipient, one-use challenge, recent MFA
GET /access-requests own requests or explicit grants:read member/team boundary
POST /access-requests verified self; reviewed proposal, exact current revision
POST /access-requests/{id}/decisions independent current parent issuer; exact revisions
POST /access-requests/{id}/cancel requester only, pending revision

A verified active member can always inspect their own effective-access explanation and own assignment sources through the existing self routes, including when all use selectors are NONE. This diagnostic reveals their own parent IDs/generations needed to submit an independent request; it grants no delegation or corpus access. Other-subject inspection still requires explicit grants:read.

Team leads cannot inspect another team's assignments or effective-access sources merely because a person belongs to both teams. Other-subject effective-access explanations omit ancestor IDs outside the selected source. No endpoint returns a private global identity document.

Offboarding and verified machine relationships

Organization suspension/offboarding advances only that membership's revision and revokes its browser sessions in the same transaction as audit. It does not disable the global user, destroy knowledge, rewrite actor/audit history or affect another organization's membership/sessions. Leads cannot suspend an organization membership if that would reach another team outside their envelope; they can suspend only their authorized team edge instead. Owners cannot be suspended, revoked or demoted through these APIs. Ownership requires the independent accepted handover and current last-owner protections from Phase 5.

Pending human job authority records include verified user, membership revision, original opaque-session public ID and worker version. Execution, persistence and result replay recheck that session, membership, current auth policy and exact source resources; reinstatement or a fresh login cannot revive the old job session. SSO job checks receive the same mounted provider registry as browser sessions. A standalone checker without that registry refuses SSO authority.

Managed credentials with unknown sponsorship are refused through the shared REST/MCP/job resolver. No sponsorship is inferred from owner_id. At managed-machine activation every legacy key must be explicitly claimed to a verified sponsor or service account, or revoked. Current verified sponsorship and custody are checked in ordinary REST, active stdio/HTTP MCP sessions and pending job access; see managed agents for those relationships and evidence gates. The human-management selector alone does not prove a complete machine lifecycle.

Validation

Focused unit targets: test_v6_memberships.py, test_v6_invites.py, test_v6_access_requests.py. Real replica-set targets: test_v6_membership_lifecycle.py, test_v6_access_request_races.py. ./scripts/test-v6-management.sh runs all unit tests and disposable prerequisites (isolation/search, local identity, Keycloak/org switching and policy fencing) before the human management integration gate. Each new selector receives a fresh disposable replica set, with a default 3 GiB MongoDB limit for the larger fixtures. Each report records runtime and test-source fingerprints. Mocked repositories do not establish atomicity or revocation. Development-only selectors are not a complete acceptance gate.

No dependency or license change is introduced. The existing maintained crypto, OIDC and MongoDB libraries remain pinned. No dashboard performance or visual result is claimed by these API tests. There is a bounded evaluation capacity of 1,000 assignments, 1,000 teams and 1,000 team edges per organization; exceeding it fails closed rather than silently truncating authorization. Directory pages are at most 100 rows. Scaling those limits requires measured representative performance and a separately reviewed policy-resolution design.

Verified human-sponsored clients and service custody are documented in Managed agents.

docs/local-identity.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Local human identity and browser security

The invitation-only local identity engine underlies the implemented organization console. SSO and organization switching build on these sessions. A browser session alone grants no corpus access; explicit managed assignments supply action/resource policy. Existing V1–V5 APIs and MCP continue to require organization-bound bearer keys.

Complete the real Phase 2 isolation gate and its explicit operator activation first. Migration 38 refuses a sealed, mixed-worker or unclassified installation. It adds strict private collections without rewriting authored records, ObjectIds, historical actors or machine credentials. Older runtime configurations refuse an installation with migration 38 applied.

Installation boundary

Enable V6_LOCAL_IDENTITY=true alongside V6_TENANT_FOUNDATION=true, V6_TENANT_ISOLATION=true and API_AUTH_ENABLED=true. Configure:

Setting Contract
V6_BROWSER_ORIGIN One exact HTTPS origin, such as https://context.example.test; no trailing slash, credentials, path or wildcard
V6_MFA_KEYRING_FILE Read-only installation secret mount containing the versioned AES-256-GCM keyring
V6_MAIL_SINK_DIRECTORY Explicit writable private directory for local test/manual delivery; mode 0700, message files 0600

The keyring JSON shape is {"active":"key-1","keys":{"key-1":"BASE64URL_32_RANDOM_BYTES"}}. Generate key material with an operating-system CSPRNG, outside public source. For example, create a new file without printing or overwriting a key:

umask 077
mkdir -p secrets
python - <<'PY'
import base64, json, secrets
from pathlib import Path
with Path("secrets/local-mfa-keyring.json").open("x") as output:
    json.dump({"active": "key-1", "keys": {
        "key-1": base64.urlsafe_b64encode(secrets.token_bytes(32)).decode()
    }}, output)
PY

Mount the file read-only and grant only the runtime user access. Retain old key versions while any factor uses them; changing the active key affects new factors. Services load the keyring at startup; apply keyring changes through a controlled operator restart while retaining every key still needed by stored factors. Removing a required old key fails authentication closed. Encryption binds each seed to its user and factor ID, so swapping ciphertext between records fails. Back up keys separately from the database under installation operator controls. Loss of every applicable key requires documented operator recovery; password reset cannot decrypt, remove or bypass MFA.

The default deployment remains disabled. Supply an explicit Compose override with these environment values, a read-only keyring mount, and a private writable mail-sink mount when enabling this phase. A TLS reverse proxy must forward only through the existing trusted proxy configuration. The identity boundary checks the effective request scheme and accepts HTTPS only. No HTTP development cookie fallback is enabled.

The mail port is MailDelivery; the implemented adapter is LocalMailSink. It writes only to the operator-selected private directory and has no outbound transport. Messages contain recipient, purpose and challenge token; they are secrets, never logs or public fixtures. Consume/delete them under the local operator's retention policy. A production mail provider adapter is separate work.

Enrollment and owner bootstrap

There is no anonymous registration or first-login owner claim. An operator with private host/database access chooses the organization and approval reference:

contextctl --org-id ORG identity invite --email alice@example.test \
  --name Alice --approval-reference APPROVAL_REFERENCE

contextctl --org-id ORG identity provision-owner --email owner@example.test \
  --name Owner --approval-reference APPROVAL_REFERENCE \
  --root-delegation-file /private/reviewed-root-tuples.json \
  --approve-project-bootstrap

The root file is a bounded, nonempty JSON array of explicit tuples, for example {"action":"projects:read","resource_kind":"project","selector":"include","ids":["project-a"],"conditions":{}}. The operator reviews the complete delegation ceiling; no wildcard action or implicit corpus bypass is accepted. Owner provisioning separately records the approved projects:read and projects:write directory bootstrap policy and the root ceiling in a pending_phase5 intent. No permission assignment or effective grant record is created by identity provisioning. The policy engine activates these approved records through its engine; further self/corpus grants need independent approval or documented operator recovery. The initial-owner unique index prevents concurrent bootstrap claims. No web route can call this operator path.

An invitation names an exact local identity and an organization membership. Possession permits only that transition. Enrollment sets a local password and sends a separate browser-bound verification challenge to the same recipient. Verification activates only the invited membership. For an existing local identity, accepting another invitation also requires its current password and active MFA; it cannot replace that identity's credentials. Equal email/domain does not create authority, merge identities or activate another membership. Local login into an sso_required organization is refused.

Browser API contracts

Start with GET /api/v6/auth/csrf. It creates a short-lived pre-authentication cookie or returns the current session's CSRF token. Keep that token only in memory and send it as X-CSRF-Token; every POST also needs the exact configured Origin. Public authentication POSTs require a valid pre-authentication cookie. The login challenge is bound to that browser and is not a data session. After expiry or revocation, this endpoint clears invalid HttpOnly cookies and issues fresh pre-authentication state so re-login needs no manual cookie removal.

Endpoint under /api/v6 Boundary and result
POST /auth/invitations/accept Invitation token and password; existing accounts also prove MFA; sends verification through the configured sink
POST /auth/local/verify Purpose-bound, browser-bound verification token; activates only the pending invited membership
POST /auth/local/login Local identity, password and requested org; the selector is checked against verified active membership; returns a five-minute login challenge
POST /auth/local/complete Browser-bound login challenge plus TOTP/recovery when configured; issues a new opaque session
POST /auth/password-reset/request Generic 202 for known/unknown eligible local identities, with a minimum response duration and shared throttles
POST /auth/password-reset/consume Reset token and new password; atomically consumes token and revokes local sessions; does not log in, disable MFA or reinstate membership
GET /me Verified own user, minimal active membership, assurance and session ID; no credential/factor/provider data or effective corpus access
GET /me/sessions Bounded own-session metadata; no cookie/token hashes
POST /me/sessions/{session_id}/revoke Own public session ID, current session, CSRF/Origin and recent MFA
POST /auth/session/rotate Revokes the old token, rotates token and CSRF; preserves the original absolute deadline
POST /auth/logout Revokes the current session and clears the cookie; remains possible after the MFA step-up window
POST /auth/mfa/enroll, /auth/mfa/confirm Recent password proof; encrypted pending factor expires after ten minutes; confirmation consumes a TOTP step, rotates the session and returns recovery codes once
POST /auth/step-up Consumes a fresh TOTP/recovery code and rotates session/CSRF; ten-minute privileged window
POST /auth/mfa/recovery Recent MFA plus a fresh TOTP; replaces recovery hashes, revokes other sessions and returns new codes once
POST /auth/mfa/remove Recent MFA; disables the factor, clears recovery hashes and invalidates all local sessions
POST /auth/password/change Recent MFA and current password; changes Argon2id hash and invalidates all local sessions

Password-only sessions permit self-security setup and identification; they never create a corpus principal. Both session cookies use Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, host-only scope and Path=/. The authenticated cookie is __Host-acp-session; pre-authentication uses __Host-acp-login and lasts fifteen minutes. Human sessions have a thirty-minute idle deadline and eight-hour absolute deadline, checked on every request before touching idle time. TTL is cleanup only. User epoch, membership revision/status and organization login policy are checked live. Revocation/password/MFA changes serialize on the user fence; membership-sensitive transitions also touch the member fence. Sensitive state, challenge consumption and identity audit commit together in replica-set transactions. A failed audit aborts its security transition.

Browser cookies are rejected by V1–V5 and HTTP MCP, even when a bearer is also supplied. /api/v6 rejects bearer headers. Stdio MCP has no browser-cookie authentication path. No token belongs in browser local/session storage, URLs, frontend environment variables or logs. Validation errors on identity endpoints never echo submitted passwords, factors or challenge values. Verified human actors carry user ID, org, local auth method and assurance; historical actor shapes remain readable and no machine key/client ID is fabricated.

Private data inventory and enforcement

Collection Ownership and gate
users, user_identities, local_credentials Private global human identity; exact login/challenge lookup or verified self-security transaction only
mfa_factors Private global human identity; own verified session or bound login transaction; encrypted seed, replay counter, hashed recovery codes
auth_challenges Private global identity/security; fixed purpose, user, org/member, browser where applicable, epoch, expiry and atomic unused predicate
browser_sessions Private global identity/security; opaque-token hash lookup, live authority checks; self-only bounded session listings
auth_throttles Private global security metadata; hashed account/network bucket, fixed minute and atomic bounded admission
identity_audit_events Private global security history; internal transactional writer, installation operator only; no directory/audit export API
organization_memberships Tenant-owned governance; explicit operator org or verified own membership ID plus org/user/revision; minimal directory DTO
_local_identity_control Installation metadata; guarded schema/version marker, no public write path
MFA keyring, local mail sink Installation-mounted private storage; neither is a public download, ingestion/search source or tenant export

app/identity/repository.py is the narrow allowlisted raw-driver boundary. The identity package does not search/join/count/export corpus data, invoke jobs or create effective policy. Existing whole-database backups include private identity and remain installation-operator-only. Restore must reconcile session epochs, membership/policy revisions and key availability before serving traffic; an old backup must not silently resurrect access.

Libraries and verification

Passwords use argon2-cffi 25.1.0 with explicit Argon2id memory 65,536 KiB, time 3, parallelism 4, salt 16 bytes and output 32 bytes. A maximum of four native hash jobs is admitted, with no waiting queue; cancellation retains its slot until native work finishes. Passwords are bounded to 1,024 UTF-8 bytes and are never reversibly stored. Unknown users perform dummy Argon2id verification under the same limits.

PyOTP 2.10.0 supplies six-digit, thirty-second TOTP with a one-step clock window. The accepted time step is atomically monotonic; random recovery codes use purpose/user-bound SHA-256 hashes and atomic removal. cryptography 50.0.2 supplies AES-256-GCM, with fresh 96-bit nonces and user/factor associated data. Direct and transitive versions are pinned in requirements.lock. Their upstream license metadata is MIT (argon2-cffi, bindings and PyOTP), Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause (cryptography), MIT-0 (cffi) and BSD-3-Clause (pycparser); retain installed wheel license notices. These licenses do not change the platform's MIT license.

Network requests are limited to 120 per minute per direct peer; login/reset requests to ten per minute per normalized account; login challenge attempts to five per minute; session security mutations to ten per minute per user. Buckets are persisted and shared by API workers; forwarded client headers are not used as authority. Set deployment proxy/network limits for distributed abuse too. At most twenty live sessions per user epoch are admitted under the user fence.

python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_v6_local_auth.py \
  tests/unit/test_v6_browser_sessions.py tests/unit/test_v6_mfa.py
scripts/test-v6-identity.sh
python -m scripts.benchmark_local_auth --samples 20

The disposable runner retains the complete Phase 2 MongoDB/mongot gate and adds tests/integration/test_v6_local_identity.py. Real persisted challenge/session replay, transaction rollback, enrollment, verification, MFA/recovery, reset, expiry, CSRF and revocation use synthetic identities, factors and a private test mail sink. Logical clock advancement exercises expiry before TTL cleanup; the password benchmark uses the real host clock. The benchmark records hardware, policy, latency and process peak RSS without printing hashes or test secrets. Its warm synthetic measurements are not production throughput results. Private evidence, key material, message files and Graphify outputs stay out of releases.

docs/managed-agents.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Human-sponsored agents and service accounts

Phase 7 adds verified machine sponsorship to the existing V4 client/key/session interfaces and V5 template snapshots. It adds session-only management APIs; normal MCP tools cannot manage people, organizations or credentials. No dashboard or live deployment activation is included.

Cutover and legacy keys

V6_MANAGED_AGENTS=false is the default. Enable it only with authenticated tenant isolation and the verified Phase 3–6 identity/policy configuration. Migration 42 follows actual head 41 and requires an explicit stopped-writer operator cutover. Stop API, stdio/HTTP MCP and background writers. Verify a restorable installation backup, then prepare with the new runtime/configuration:

contextctl --org-id fictional-org managed-agents prepare \
  --writers-stopped --worker-schema-version 42 \
  --approval-reference fictional-independent-cutover-review

Preparation preserves domain ObjectIds, authored records, key hashes, actor and revision history. It adds strict authority storage and switches the persisted worker seal to 42. Older workers are refused. Earlier adopted-key policy adapters are explicitly revoked; an unverified admin adapter cannot continue queued work. Human organization management remains available. Machine authentication stays sealed until the separate installation-wide activation succeeds.

Inventory every organization's active keys with managed-agents inventory and the same required org, writer/version and approval flags. Each legacy key needs one of these explicit decisions:

  • Independently approve a client with a verified human recipient or organization service account. Then managed-agents claim-key --policy-file reviewed.json binds an adopted key to that reviewed client. The bounded claim contains key_id, client_id, expected_client_revision, exact tuples, and aware expires_at. It cannot expand the existing key, sponsor or parent policy.
  • managed-agents revoke-key --key-id PUBLIC_ID retires the credential. Expired but still active metadata must also be explicitly revoked.

The operator never gets a plaintext key from claiming. Descriptive owner_id values, equal emails and creator labels are never ownership proof. Claim cannot silently move a key already attached to another client. New credentials cannot choose legacy identity rules.

Run managed-agents activate with the same required flags after reconciliation. Activation checks every active key across the installation under shared policy anchors. An unclaimed, expired, stale or unresolved credential blocks it. This command creates no grants. Repeated migration preserves the activation marker; unknown populated reserved storage is refused. Rollback requires a sealed, verified installation restore. There is no tenant restore API.

Approval, custody and current permissions

A client approval records immutable organization, subject kind/ID and optional team, a verified human sponsor, sponsor membership/team-edge revisions, the independent issuer's exact assignment ID/generation, bounded action/resource policy and expiry. An organization service account has a verified current human custodian, named team, bounded lifetime and independent approval. Old owner_id is retained as descriptive history and never consulted by authorization.

Client policy approval requires an independent authorized manager and a current delegating parent with sufficient depth, target/team envelope and issuance ceiling. Leads can approve only their delegated named team's clients. They cannot approve their own policy, move a client to another subject/team, or widen beyond that parent. Explicit owner/admin capabilities are still required; titles confer no corpus access.

Every REST authentication and MCP preflight re-evaluates the current sponsor, team/edge generation, service custody, complete delegation ancestry, client snapshot and key policy. Intersection preserves each action/resource pair: read-A plus write-B never permits write-A. NONE remains empty. Organization-global knowledge and skill imports require their own explicit tuples. No null-org or shared-corpus fallback is introduced.

Policy updates advance the client approval revision and invalidate its previous credential approvals. Revoked/suspended membership, team, parent, client, key or service custody denies future work. Reinstatement does not restore old captured revisions. Reapprove and issue a replacement explicitly. A service custody change requires a new independently approved account/relationship; there is no implicit handover from an old owner label.

Recipient-only one-time delivery

Approval contains policy only. A recipient signs in with their own recent-MFA browser session and explicitly delegated credentials:issue:own capability. For unattended service accounts, the authenticated current custodian performs issuance within the approved service policy, with transactional governance audit. A lead may inspect/revoke permitted metadata and cannot issue or recover another worker's token.

The recipient submits an issuance_id, current approval revision, exact narrowed key tuples and expiry. The server reuses the existing random key minting and SHA-256 verifier for high-entropy machine secrets. The token is returned once, after the key/receipt/audit transaction commits, with Cache-Control: no-store. Only its hash goes into api_keys; the delivery receipt, governance event and outbox contain safe identifiers/policy metadata. Browser storage and frontend environment variables are not token destinations.

An identical retry returns safe metadata with delivered=false, without a token. A changed command under the same receipt ID is refused. Lost response delivery requires explicit revoke/replacement; it never causes plaintext replay. Rotation uses a new issuance ID and replaces_key_id, atomically revoking the old key and issuing its replacement. Expiry is checked on each request, not by cleanup. Ordinary MCP idempotency also refuses machine credential material in retained results. No credential issuance tool is added to MCP.

Templates, previews, sessions and limits

An explicit template assignment selects an active V5 profile and exact revision, and can only narrow its scopes. The copied scopes/profile revision are recorded with the approved client. Later template edits/disable do not update assigned clients or issued keys. An explicit reassignment is reviewed again and invalidates old credential approvals. rate_limit_profile remains descriptive; it changes no limit. Preview returns current intersected tuples, copied scopes, source revision and policy revision; it is not a promise of future authority.

MCP preflight and capability summaries carry complete action/resource tuples. Generic project/profile lists are empty for managed summaries to avoid suggesting one broad grant. Named resource preflight uses the tool's action; the API still checks every actual resource/reference and every search candidate. Summaries never substitute for authorization.

V4 agent sessions are bound to the org/client/key/subject/policy fingerprint. A change to its effective policy requires a new operational session. Copied template edits and unrelated org metadata do not invalidate its policy context. The live shared org anchor still fences every authorized persistence step. HTTP MCP transport sessions remain bound to their original key/org and reauthenticate every request; stdio preflight reauthenticates each tool call. MCP rate reservations carry verified subject/policy context and single-use leases. Quotas aggregate by org/client so rotating credentials or changing policy cannot reset a client's budget. Limits remain process-local as documented; no distributed quota enforcement is claimed.

Ingestion captures the exact initiating key and schema version. Workers and job reads/downloads recheck the same current sponsorship and action/resource source closure. Revocation denies pending work/results. It does not undo work committed before the revocation fence won. Operator backups/raw metrics remain host-only.

Service-account reviewer exception

Ordinary clients cannot review with content:write, even if their copied policy mentions review. A service account additionally needs a separate bounded approval from an independent verified reviewer. That approval names the reviewer's current assignment/generation/membership revision, exact review/read/operation resources and expiry. The custodian and account creator cannot approve the exception. Custody and the independently delegating client ceiling still bound all data operations. The reviewer cannot contribute unrelated policy as a broad union.

For every review operation, the service must have readable evidence, the exact write/approval action and reviews:decide on the relevant resource. Server-derived actor provenance records the human sponsor/team/service and approval revision at authoring time. Fenced immutable author history includes every verified sponsor, so changing a last writer or client name cannot permit same-sponsor self-review. Unknown historical authorship is refused. Human reviewers also cannot approve work sponsored by themselves. Current machine ownership never rewrites event-time attribution. Revoking the independent reviewer's ancestry disables the exception.

API surface and verification

All paths are relative to /api/v6/organizations/{org_id} and require the current human session/org context. Every mutation requires Origin, CSRF and recent MFA. Bearer V1–V5/MCP cannot use browser cookies.

Method/path Purpose
GET /managed-clients Bounded, authorized own/team/org metadata
POST /managed-clients/preview Explicit policy/template preview; no assignment
POST /managed-clients Independent reviewed create/reassignment
GET /managed-clients/{id} Authorized policy/effective tuples and secret-free receipts
POST /managed-clients/{id}/credentials Recipient/custodian-only issue or explicit rotation
POST /managed-clients/{id}/revoke Conditional client revocation
POST /managed-clients/{id}/credentials/{key}/revoke Conditional credential revocation
GET/POST /service-accounts Bounded authorized directory / independent custody approval
POST /service-accounts/{id}/reviewer-approval Separate independent reviewer exception
POST /service-accounts/{id}/revoke Conditional service revocation
PUT /client-templates/{id} Explicit revisioned V5 template edit; no propagation

expected_revision=0 creates a new client/template. First adoption of an existing unmanaged V4 client uses its actual current client revision; subsequent approvals use the returned managed approval revision. Credential commands always use that managed approval revision. Natural-key indexes start with organization identity; key public IDs remain globally unique only for initial authentication lookup. New storage is tenant-owned service_accounts, managed_clients, managed_credentials, plus installation metadata _managed_agents_control. None is a corpus search source or an ordinary org directory identity DTO.

Run scripts/test-v6-managed-agents.sh only in disposable infrastructure. It runs the prerequisite unit/MongoDB/mongot/Keycloak selectors plus the three Phase 7 real selectors. Focused files retain the requested names. Reports include exact runtime/test fingerprints. Skipped real provider/database tests are an incomplete gate. Use fictional identities/test delivery only. No new dependency or license is introduced by Phase 7.

docs/management-policy.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Managed roles, grants and delegation (V6 Phase 5)

The opt-in policy engine uses verified human identity and explicit organization context. V6_MANAGEMENT_POLICY=false remains the default; enabling it does not perform the operator bootstrap. Human management, managed machines and the console consume this engine. This reference describes the schema-40 cutover within the current staged migration, whose full head is 42.

Authority model

The fixed catalog contains 28 management permissions and nine role templates in app/security/policy/catalog.py. Templates describe selectable capabilities; a role label grants no corpus access and does not authorize arbitrary targets. Installation operators are a separate host boundary and have no human role permissions. Monitoring (activity, audit, reports), grant issuance authority and data use are separate action/resource tuples.

Every assignment starts with empty use/delegation tuples and NONE targets. Selectors are none without IDs, include with 1–50 unique IDs, or explicit all_in_org without IDs. ALL includes future resources in that organization. Issuing ALL requires distinct current grants:all-in-org approval. Empty arrays never mean ALL in managed policy. Only the reviewed legacy adoption adapter preserves the earlier explicit all_in_org spelling.

A tuple couples one action to one resource dimension. context:read on A plus context:write on B cannot authorize a write on A. Query/count/join/search and result checks use the current action. Unified search intersects search:read with each source's own read tuples before lexical/vector candidate selection. Content also intersects inherited project/private-client boundaries; research requires its research-project boundary and every linked project. Unlinked research and organization-global memory need explicit organization_knowledge access. Imported skills/skill_chunks need explicit skill access. Private memory needs client_memory; a missing project is never global permission. Project-directory bootstrap rights do not grant project context access.

Issuance ceilings are separate from effective use. A lead may have an explicit ceiling to appoint reviewers while having no personal reviews:decide tuple. Every child must fit the parent's actions, resources, named user targets, allowed roles, remaining depth and expiry. The parent must itself hold current issuance authority for that target. Owner/admin can appoint executive/lead; those roles can appoint member roles only. Owner-to-admin appointment consumes one level; a lineage has at most four records. No nested-team or script policy exists. Named team workflows use explicit team edges and current delegated envelopes; no team title expands target selectors.

Self-grants, self-ceiling changes and appointment of owner/admin by leads are refused. Regrant creates a new assignment ID. Narrowing/revocation advances the parent generation; suspension/reinstatement advances membership revision. Old descendants remain ineffective after regrant, widening or reinstatement. There is no authorization cache. Expiry is checked during resolution, not by TTL.

Bootstrap and operator boundary

Stop and drain old API, job and MCP workers before initial policy cutover. The API will refuse to apply migration 40 automatically. The host operator uses the existing recorded, verified initial owner's pending_phase5 intent:

contextctl --org-id "$ORG" policy activate-bootstrap \
  --user-id "$VERIFIED_OWNER" \
  --target-user-id "$VERIFIED_LEAD" --target-user-id "$VERIFIED_MEMBER" \
  --allowed-role team_lead --allowed-role contributor \
  --expires-at "$REVIEWED_EXPIRY" \
  --approval-reference "$OPERATOR_APPROVAL" --approve-management-template \
  --writers-stopped --worker-schema-version 40

Enable the existing Phase 1–4 flags and mounted identity/provider configuration, plus V6_MANAGEMENT_POLICY=true, for this command and subsequent workers. Root expiry is at most 365 days. Target and role lists default to NONE. The recorded root ceiling is preserved exactly. Activation creates explicit management assignments plus only the already approved project-directory read/write tuples; it does not grant the owner effective use of the root's corpus ceiling. Audit and outbox commit with activation. Repeating activation does not widen it.

The shared control stage becomes managed, workers must declare version 40, and both browser identity markers become 40. Old bearer/browser/job/CLI binaries refuse the new state. A partially failed cutover remains closed and resumable; do not downgrade or mix writers. Run/review the complete disposable evidence selector below before cutover. Schema presence alone is not test evidence.

Unreviewed credentials fail closed. An operator may explicitly approve an unchanged adopted version-1 credential, bounded to its adoption organization, current client/scope/resource envelope and at most 30 days:

contextctl --org-id "$ORG" policy approve-legacy-adapter \
  --key-id "$ADOPTED_KEY_ID" --hours 24 --approval-reference "$ADOPTION_REVIEW" \
  --writers-stopped --worker-schema-version 40

This is the reviewed adoption-operator exception, not a managed service-account sponsor. New credentials cannot choose it. Even adopted admin/bearer keys cannot approve reviews after managed cutover: they do not establish verified human identity or service sponsorship. This deliberate review restriction is separate from preserved ordinary data access. Existing REST/MCP/admin paths retain its resource checks and refresh it on authentication, job execution and result access. Operator key revocation and client-envelope writes share the anchor and strict governance audit. Managed issuance requires the verified sponsorship engine and recipient-only delivery; legacy keys create remains refused. Whole-database backup/restore and raw shared metrics stay installation-only.

An owner who needs additional corpus use cannot grant it to themselves. Until an independently approved human delegation lineage is available, the documented host recovery exception is an explicit, expiring use-only assignment:

contextctl --org-id "$ORG" policy recover-owner-corpus \
  --user-id "$VERIFIED_OWNER" --tuples-file "$REVIEWED_CORPUS_TUPLES" \
  --expires-at "$REVIEWED_EXPIRY" --approval-reference "$INDEPENDENT_APPROVAL" \
  --writers-stopped --worker-schema-version 40

The file is a nonempty JSON list of at most 100 typed data-use tuples, at most 64 KiB. Recovery is at most 30 days, creates no delegation ceiling or management permission, preserves the original root ceiling and records the operator exception transactionally. No browser route can invoke it. Ownership transfer moves the explicit governance/directory root after fresh MFA on offer and acceptance; it does not transfer personal corpus assignments. The old owner's membership revision changes, invalidating its grants and descendants. Ordinary suspension or role assignment cannot remove an owner; transfer preserves an active verified owner and invalidates both old session contexts.

Review and transactional contracts

Managed review decisions need reviews:decide on the actual profile/research boundary, source readability and the operation's domain permission (content:write or research:approve). Promotion/publication remain separate permissions. New records cannot begin in an approved review state. Service and repository hooks cover lifecycle shortcuts as well as explicit decision routes.

A server-attested authorship ledger records human sponsors with authored writes in the same fenced transaction. Every contributing author is excluded from review. An adopted record without this proof remains unreviewable by managed humans; editing it cannot manufacture sponsorship. Unknown machine authorship fails closed. Managed machine review requires a separately approved service account, verified active sponsor/generation, exact review operations/resources, expiry and sponsor-based self-review exclusions. owner_id, equal emails, IdP roles or content:write alone do not establish it.

Each organization has a shared policy_anchors document. Issuance, revoke, narrowing, suspension, ownership changes, sensitive domain writes and operator credential/client mutations conditionally change that anchor. Governance uses snapshot transactions with majority commit and an actual increment, not a no-op or reads/writes to unrelated documents. Conflicting governance transactions retry at most three times against freshly read policy and original expected revisions/generations. Stale human domain review is never automatically replayed. Browser mutations also fence the live session, user and membership.

Assignment/authority mutation, immutable governance event and durable outbox are one transaction. Audit contains assignment before/after metadata, not corpus bodies, factor secrets or credentials. Audit/outbox failure aborts the mutation. The existing ordinary domain audit remains best-effort. Outbox records are persisted without credential plaintext; they do not themselves send messages or replay one-time secrets.

This follows MongoDB's documented transaction conflict/stale-read behavior and PyMongo transaction semantics. No dependency was added; the existing pinned PyMongo async driver and standard library implement this phase.

Session-only API foundation

All routes use the current verified active organization; path selectors are not authority. Mutations require HTTPS, exact Origin, CSRF, current session context and recent MFA. Effective-access explanations show exact tuples, generations, expiry and inactive ancestry without exposing private login identities.

Method Path Gate
GET /api/v6/me/effective-access grants:read on self
GET/PATCH /api/v6/organizations/{org_id} org:read / org:manage
PATCH /api/v6/organizations/{org_id}/policy org:manage; provider already operator-approved
GET /api/v6/organizations/{org_id}/assignments?subject_id=… grants:read on that member
POST /api/v6/organizations/{org_id}/assignments or /delegations grants:delegate and current parent ceiling
PATCH /api/v6/organizations/{org_id}/assignments/{id} narrow only; expected revision
POST /api/v6/organizations/{org_id}/delegations/{id}/revoke ancestor authority; expected revision
POST /api/v6/organizations/{org_id}/ownership-transfer current owner; distinct verified target
POST /api/v6/organizations/{org_id}/ownership-transfer/{id}/accept named target; unexpired unchanged offer

Membership suspension/reinstatement uses these transactional primitives. Human-management APIs, managed credentials and console workflows have additional operation-specific gates; this policy selector alone does not prove those complete journeys.

Storage, bounds and verification

Seven new collections are tenant-owned and excluded from ordinary corpus repositories: policy_anchors, policy_assignments, policy_credentials, governance_events, governance_outbox, ownership_transfers, review_authorship. _management_policy_control is installation metadata. All have strict validators; natural indexes begin with organization. Existing private identity collections remain private. No new public filesystem/cache path or authorization cache is introduced.

Initial evaluation refuses organizations exceeding 1,000 retained assignments. This conservative bound includes revoked history; reaching it requires operator capacity work, not silent truncation or deleting audit history. Selectors cap at 50 IDs, commands at 100 tuples, live lineage at four records, root expiry at 365 days and operator recovery/adoption adapters at 30 days. The shared anchor serializes organization-sensitive writes. These are implementation bounds, not throughput, latency or visual benchmark results. Existing Phase 0 performance budgets remain targets; verification records unresolved measurement and acceptance limits.

python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_security_models.py tests/unit/test_api_authorization.py tests/unit/test_content_publication.py tests/unit/test_knowledge_candidate_service.py tests/unit/test_agent_client_service.py
python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_v6_management_policy.py tests/unit/test_v6_delegation.py tests/unit/test_v6_governance_audit.py
scripts/test-v6-policy.sh

The full runner uses generated test-only secrets, a disposable MongoDB replica set, real mongot and HTTPS Keycloak. It runs the full units and prior isolation, local identity and SSO selectors before the real policy selector. Reports bind to runtime/test bytes; skips do not establish a gate. Development selectors are explicitly labeled and do not replace a complete run. Test evidence and planning stay under ignored .private/; Graphify's local graph stays ignored too.

Acceptance verification for this implementation: 3,100 unit tests; 12 real policy tests; 12 complete tenant-isolation tests; 9 local-identity tests; and 9 HTTPS Keycloak/org-switch tests. All passed without skips. The named focused selectors passed 291 new policy cases and 140 existing regressions. These are correctness results from disposable infrastructure, not capacity benchmarks.

docs/mcp.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

MCP server

The MCP server is how an agent reaches this platform. It exposes client-neutral tools over the Model Context Protocol. It validates arguments, checks caller grants, calls the corresponding API operation, and shapes the result for a model to read. Gateway capability checks also expose safe integration metadata.

What it is not

It holds no business logic, and the boundaries are structural rather than a matter of discipline:

  • No database access. app/mcp/ uses shared validated types but no repository or MongoDB driver. The local MCP process runs on settings that do not contain a database URI at all (McpSettings), so a container running it is handed no credentials it could misuse.
  • No retrieval logic. Ranking, deduplication, token budgeting, and the embedding model live behind the API. search_knowledge is one POST.
  • No isolation rules of its own. Which project may see what is decided by the services and enforced three times over there. The MCP layer adds a grant check before that, so a refused call never leaves this process — it does not replace the rule, it stops short of it.
  • Fixed API operations. No tool accepts an arbitrary database query, pipeline, filesystem path, or shell command. Every tool names a route this server already knows; a caller chooses arguments, never destinations.
Codex ──MCP/stdio──┐
                    ├──► one MCP server ──HTTP──► Context API ──► services ──► MongoDB
Claude ──MCP/HTTP──┘

Core and creator planning tools

Tool Scope Reaches

search_context context:read POST /api/v1/context/search
get_context context:read GET /api/v1/context/{id}?project_id=…
save_context context:write POST /api/v1/context
search_memory memory:read POST /api/v1/memory/search
save_memory memory:write POST /api/v1/memory
update_memory memory:write PATCH /api/v1/memory/{id}
search_knowledge search:read POST /api/v1/search
get_system_status system:read GET /health/ready
get_creator_profile creator:read GET /api/v2/creator-profiles/{id}
update_creator_profile creator:write PATCH /api/v2/creator-profiles/{id}
list_content_pillars creator:read GET /api/v2/content-pillars
search_content content:read POST /api/v2/content/search
get_content content:read GET /api/v2/content/{id}
get_content_history content:read GET /api/v2/content/{id}/versions
discover_content_ideas content:read POST /api/v2/content-ideas/discover
save_content_idea content:write POST /api/v2/content-ideas
search_content_ideas content:read POST /api/v2/content/search restricted to ideas
prepare_content_brief content:read POST /api/v2/content-briefs/prepare
check_content_novelty content:read POST /api/v2/content/novelty
prepare_repurpose_plan content:read POST /api/v2/content/{id}/repurpose

The complete tool inventory, including research, publication, and metric tools, is in the HTML usage guide. Domain workflows are documented in research.md, content-export.md, content-publishing.md, and content-metrics.md.

search_skills goes through the unified pipeline restricted to one source rather than a second retrieval path, so a skill answer is ranked exactly as any other answer is.

discover_content_ideas and prepare_content_brief return structured evidence and a non-persistent brief package; neither generates prose. save_content_idea is explicitly a content:write operation, so discovery never turns into an automatic write.

check_content_novelty reports advisory, explainable history overlap rather than a truth claim. prepare_repurpose_plan returns source-backed, platform-specific planning fields without a target body, version, or publish action. Both remain one protected API request and have no MongoDB or writing logic in MCP.

Creating a project is deliberately absent. A project is the isolation boundary every other rule is written against, so bringing one into existence is an operator's decision through the API, not something an agent does while answering a question. Nothing deletes, either: a correction supersedes, and update_memory is revision-guarded.

Arguments

Every tool publishes a JSON Schema with additionalProperties: false, built from the same field constraints the API's own schemas use. A misspelled argument is refused rather than ignored, so a caller never receives an answer to a question it did not ask.

Validation happens twice on purpose, and they are different checks: the protocol layer rejects anything the published schema forbids, and the tool's model then produces typed values and the message a caller is shown. The record rules — that a project exists, that a memory cannot be superseded twice — stay in the services, where they already are.

Project identity

search_context, get_context, and save_context require project_id. It has no default and is never inferred. A tool that guessed which project a caller meant would be choosing an isolation boundary on its behalf, which is the one thing this layer must not do; list_projects exists so a caller can find the right identifier instead of guessing.

search_knowledge, search_memory, save_memory, and update_memory take an optional project_id. Omitting it cannot address project-owned knowledge. Shared global memory remains available; authenticated clients can also explicitly address their own agent memory. Project-agent memory requires the project and the authenticated client. See memory.md.

resolve_project is the only exception to a tool requiring an already-known project ID: it maps client-supplied repository or workspace metadata through an administrator-created exact binding. It accepts an explicit project_id, Git remote, repository URL/name, or workspace alias in that priority order. SSH and HTTPS forms of the same standard remote normalize to one credential- free repository locator. No client workspace is read by the server; ambiguous or unmatched metadata returns candidates or no match rather than selecting a project.

Agent sessions

begin_agent_session, get_agent_session, update_agent_session, and end_agent_session are optional lifecycle tools with practical value for long-running Codex and remote Claude Code work. They use the same gateway, credential, and client-neutral MCP server as every other tool; there is no Claude-specific session backend.

Beginning a session derives client_id and client_type from the authenticated credential. A caller cannot select another agent's identity. It may associate one authorized project_id, a repository label, and up to twenty small scalar metadata labels such as a workspace name or client version. It never stores prompts, messages, a transcript, a context window, chain-of-thought, a token, or a credential. Nested metadata is refused for the same reason.

After a successful begin_agent_session, the MCP gateway carries the server-created session_id on subsequent calls within that MCP process or remote MCP transport session. The API validates that the session remains active and belongs to the bearer-linked client before accepting it. Activity events and retrieval logs therefore correlate search_knowledge, save_context, and other calls without retaining their raw request bodies. Durable write provenance remains the stable actor identity (client_id and client_type); a transient session is operational correlation, not a new durable actor identity.

Sessions transition from active to ended, or lazily to expired after eight hours without a gateway heartbeat. update_agent_session and end_agent_session require expected_revision; a stale revision returns REVISION_CONFLICT and the client must reload, compare, then retry or ask for review. A normal client can read or change only its own sessions. An existing administrative agent:manage grant is the sole elevated exception at the API boundary; credential administration remains outside normal MCP tools.

Per-client protection

The single self-hosted gateway applies independent, process-local limits to each credential-derived client_id: requests per minute, concurrent MCP calls, writes per minute, research ingestions per hour, and long-running jobs. One Claude Code loop therefore cannot consume Codex's budget. Legacy keys have no fabricated client identity and retain their existing behavior.

search_knowledge, search_context, save_context, and search_memory use the fast deadline. Evidence-packet and content-brief preparation use the standard deadline. ingest_research_source is the declared long-running V3 path and returns the existing persisted ingestion-job record; it does not add a second queue or keep an MCP call open without a deadline. Configure the single-instance policy with MCP_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE, MCP_CONCURRENT_CALLS, MCP_WRITES_PER_MINUTE, MCP_RESEARCH_INGESTIONS_PER_HOUR, MCP_LONG_RUNNING_JOBS_PER_CLIENT, and the three MCP_*_TIMEOUT_SECONDS values. A future multi-instance deployment can replace the limiter backend without changing the MCP tool contract.

Retry-prone writes accept an optional opaque idempotency_key: save_context, save_memory, create_research_project, propose_knowledge_candidate, mark_content_published, and ingest_research_source. The gateway never logs a key and persists only its SHA-256 digest, a payload digest, and a short-lived completed result. A retry with the same client, operation, key, and payload replays that result without performing another write. Reusing the key with a different payload returns IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; a still-pending, uncertain attempt returns OPERATION_TIMEOUT rather than being blindly repeated. Records expire after MCP_IDEMPOTENCY_RETENTION_SECONDS (24 hours by default).

Authorization

The grant is checked before anything else happens, so a refused call never reaches the platform:

tool exists → caller holds the scope → arguments validate → project/profile is allowed → one API request

Scope is checked before the arguments are even parsed, so an unauthorized caller learns nothing about a tool's shape.

Setting Effect
MCP_SCOPES Optional local scope restriction. Empty adds no narrowing; backend policy still applies.
MCP_PROJECT_IDS Optional local project restriction; empty never widens authenticated rights.
MCP_PROFILE_IDS Optional local creator-profile restriction; empty never widens authenticated rights.
MCP_API_TOKEN / MCP_API_TOKEN_FILE Sent to the API as a bearer token, never logged

Empty local filter settings add no further narrowing; they do not grant backend authority. An unconfigured credential or missing trusted org fails closed. Local stdio process access does not bypass current sponsor/resource policy. The two halves narrow independently — MCP_SCOPES=search:read,context:read with MCP_PROJECT_IDS=payment-service gives an agent read-only retrieval inside one project. For V2 creator data, MCP_PROFILE_IDS=personal-brand is checked before a request reaches the API. It is an additional allow-list, not a substitute for the API key's profile grant.

An unknown scope is refused while settings load, rather than ignored: silently dropping one would quietly widen a grant meant to narrow.

There are two grants, and they compose. This one is the server's own, checked before a request is built, so a refused call never leaves the process. The other belongs to the key the server presents to the API — issued with contextctl keys create, pointed at by MCP_API_TOKEN_FILE — and is checked again at the API, which is what stops a misconfigured server from exceeding what its credential allows. A caller gets whichever is narrower.

The API's refusals arrive as tool errors written for a model to read: the platform refused this call as unauthorized: this key is not authorized for context:write. A refused project is never named, there or here, because naming it confirms the project exists. See security.md.

Results
