query_id which search, matching the trace.query_id in the response
result_count how much came back
duration_ms how long the whole call took
latency_ms how long the retrieval inside it took

request_id is created at the edge and carried in a context variable, so every line a call produces has it without any function being handed one.

It crosses the process boundary. The MCP server mints an identifier for each tool call and sends it to the API as X-Request-ID; the API adopts it and answers with it. One tool call and the API request it became therefore share an identifier in two processes' logs:

mcp   {"message":"mcp_tool_completed","request_id":"7f3a…","mcp_tool":"search_knowledge","outcome":"ok","duration_ms":231.4}
api   {"message":"http_request_completed","request_id":"7f3a…","operation":"search_knowledge","result_count":6,"duration_ms":214.8}

A supplied identifier is adopted only if it is at most 64 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]; anything else is replaced with a fresh one. The identifier is repeated on every line of the call, so nothing that could be mistaken for structure by whatever later reads those lines is carried.

Any client may send X-Request-ID and get the same behaviour.

The events worth knowing

Event Logger When
http_request_completed agent_context.http one per answered request
http_request_failed agent_context.http a request that raised
unhandled_request_error agent_context.http with the stack, never sent to the caller
retrieval_completed agent_context.retrieval one per search, without the query
mcp_tool_completed agent_context.mcp one per tool call, with its outcome
mcp_tool_failed agent_context.mcp a defect in the MCP server, with the stack
authorization_denied agent_context.security a refusal, with key_id and the reason
mongodb_command_failed agent_context.mongodb a failed command, without its reply
skill_import_completed agent_context.skills one per contextctl skills import

LOG_LEVEL sets the threshold; INFO is the default and is what produces the access line.

Reading them

docker compose logs -f context-api | jq -c 'select(.message == "http_request_completed")'
docker compose logs context-api | jq -c 'select(.request_id == "7f3a…")'      # one call
docker compose logs context-api | jq -c 'select(.duration_ms > 1000)'          # the slow ones
docker compose logs context-api | jq -c 'select(.level == "WARNING" or .level == "ERROR")'

Metrics

GET /metrics renders process-local counters and last-observation latency summaries in Prometheus format. It is installation-operator-only: mount a separate random credential and set OPERATOR_METRICS_TOKEN_FILE. Tenant keys, including system:read, do not authorize raw shared metrics. An unset token path disables access. Configure the private installation scraper with that credential; do not embed it in a dashboard, example URL or browser bundle.

These values are not historical organization chart series. The monitoring console uses separate authorized events and declared coverage, retention and population. Never infer employee presence, productivity or model cost from last observations.

A scrape runs no dependency checks. It walks a dictionary and returns; the readiness gauges are whatever /health/ready last wrote. Monitoring must not be on the critical path of the thing it monitors.

METRICS_ENABLED=false removes the endpoint entirely — 404, not an empty body, so a scraper pointed at it fails visibly instead of recording that all is quiet — and stops the driver publishing a timing for every MongoDB command.

The catalogue

Metric Type Labels
acp_http_requests_total counter method, route, status
acp_http_request_duration_seconds summary route
acp_mongodb_command_duration_seconds summary command
acp_mongodb_command_failures_total counter command
acp_embedding_duration_seconds summary operation
acp_embedding_failures_total counter operation
acp_search_duration_seconds summary method, collection
acp_search_failures_total counter method, collection
acp_retrieval_duration_seconds summary operation
acp_retrieval_results summary operation
acp_mcp_calls_total counter tool, outcome
acp_mcp_call_duration_seconds summary tool
acp_memory_operations_total counter operation, outcome
acp_skill_imports_total counter outcome
acp_dependency_ready gauge dependency
acp_readiness_check_duration_seconds summary —
acp_uptime_seconds gauge —
acp_build_info gauge version

Label vocabularies: method is vector or lexical; collection is skill_chunks, project_context, or memories; operation on embedding is query or documents; outcome on MCP is ok, refused, unavailable, or failed; outcome on memory is ok, unchanged, or failed; outcome on a skill import is new, updated, unchanged, or failed.

Percentiles

Every summary reports p50, p95, and p99:

acp_http_request_duration_seconds{route="/api/v1/search",quantile="0.5"} 0.184
acp_http_request_duration_seconds{route="/api/v1/search",quantile="0.95"} 0.501
acp_http_request_duration_seconds{route="/api/v1/search",quantile="0.99"} 0.912
acp_http_request_duration_seconds_count{route="/api/v1/search"} 1043
acp_http_request_duration_seconds_sum{route="/api/v1/search"} 217.4

The quantiles are computed over the last 1024 observations of that series; _count and _sum are lifetime figures. That split is deliberate and is what the format's summaries have always meant: a p99 should describe now, while a rate should cover the whole process. The value reported is one that was actually measured — nearest rank, not interpolation — so a p99 names a request that really did take that long.

Why vector and lexical are counted apart

They fail apart. A rebuilding vector index takes semantic search down while lexical search keeps answering, and a single "search failures" number would go red for that half-outage without saying which half. acp_search_failures_total splits by method and by collection, so the failing index is the one the number names.

A missing index is not a failed query

An empty query result does not prove that a search index is ready. Search failures and readiness are separate signals, so alert on both. A dropped or rebuilding vector index is detected by acp_dependency_ready{dependency="vector_search"} going to 0, because readiness asks whether each index is queryable rather than inferring it from whether queries failed.

The failure counter is for the other case: a query that could not be served at all — the coordinator down, the pipeline refused, a score that came back unusable. Both signals exist because they catch different outages, and an alert on only one of them would miss the other silently.

Cardinality

A registry cannot grow without bound. Metrics are declared up front, an undeclared name or an unexpected label is a programming error rather than a new series, each metric keeps at most 128 label combinations, and each summary keeps at most 1024 recent observations. Nothing a caller sends can add a series, so the scrape endpoint can never become the way a process runs out of memory.

The processes that have no port

contextctl and the local stdio MCP bridge do not expose scrape endpoints. They record into the same registry and also emit one structured event per operation — mcp_tool_completed, skill_import_completed — carrying the same figures. Whatever collects container logs therefore has those numbers, without either process opening an additional port. The remote HTTP MCP gateway runs inside the API process and uses its normal metrics endpoint.

Scraping

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: agent-context-platform
    scrape_interval: 15s
    metrics_path: /metrics
    authorization:
      type: Bearer
      credentials_file: /etc/prometheus/agent-context-key
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:8000"]

Run the scraper on the same host or the same private network. The API port is published to loopback only by default, which is where it should stay.

Readiness

GET /health/live says the process is answering. GET /health/ready says whether it can actually work, and answers 503 when it cannot — checking MongoDB, the replica set, the search coordinator, the embedding model, and all six search indexes. It never reports healthy merely because the HTTP process is alive.

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/ready | jq '{status, api, mongot, embedding: .embedding.ready}'
contextctl health                       # the same answer, exit 3 when not ready

{
  "status": "ready",
  "api": { "ready": true, "version": "0.1.0", "uptime_seconds": 4172.8 },
  "authentication": { "enabled": true, "audit": true },
  "mongodb": true, "database": true, "replica_set": true, "mongot": true,
  "embedding": { "enabled": true, "available": true, "model": "…", "dimensions": 384, "ready": true },
  "vector_search": { "…": "…", "ready": true },
  "lexical_search": { "…": "…", "ready": true },
  "context_search": { "…": "…", "ready": true },
  "memory_search": { "…": "…", "ready": true }
}

The api block names the build that answered and how long it has been up, which turns "it started failing after the deploy" from a guess into a reading.

Each check also writes acp_dependency_ready{dependency=…} as 1 or 0, so an alert can fire on a failing dependency without anything having to parse this body. The container health check calls this endpoint every ten seconds, which is what keeps those gauges as fresh as readiness itself.

dependency Ready when
api the process answered
mongodb the application database accepts commands
replica_set this member is primary of the expected set
mongot the coordinator path answers
embedding the model is loaded, or embeddings are disabled
vector_search the skill vector index is queryable at the right dimensions
lexical_search the skill Search index is queryable
context_search both project-context indexes are queryable
memory_search both memory indexes are queryable
platform every one of the above

Alerts worth having

acp_dependency_ready{dependency="platform"} == 0
rate(acp_search_failures_total[5m]) > 0
rate(acp_embedding_failures_total[5m]) > 0
acp_http_request_duration_seconds{route="/api/v1/search",quantile="0.95"} > 1
rate(acp_mcp_calls_total{outcome="unavailable"}[5m]) > 0
rate(acp_http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]) > 0

These are example alert rules. Set latency thresholds from representative measurements and the service objectives of your own deployment.

OpenTelemetry

OpenTelemetry is not included. Structured logs and /metrics provide the shipped observability interface. A deployment that needs tracing can add a compatible exporter and collector at the existing instrumentation boundary.

The extension point exists if a deployment wants it. Every call already has one identifier that crosses the process boundary in a header, every operation is already timed in one place, and app/observability/ has no dependency on the rest of the application — an exporter would be an additional consumer of the same recordings, not a rewrite of them.

Configuration

Variable Purpose Default
LOG_LEVEL CRITICAL, ERROR, WARNING, INFO, DEBUG INFO
METRICS_ENABLED publish /metrics at all true
RETRIEVAL_LOG_ENABLED additionally store each search, query text included false
AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED store every authorization decision true

RETRIEVAL_LOG_ENABLED is the one setting that changes what is retained rather than what is measured. The structured retrieval event never carries the query; enabling this stores one retrieval_logs document per search with the query text, which is a deliberate retention decision — it is the one field that can describe who asked what. See retrieval.md.

Verification

python -m pytest tests/unit/test_metrics.py tests/unit/test_instruments.py \
  tests/unit/test_logging.py tests/unit/test_api_metrics.py \
  tests/unit/test_observability_context.py tests/unit/test_observability_mongo.py \
  tests/unit/test_search_observability.py tests/unit/test_knowledge_observability.py \
  tests/unit/test_mcp_observability.py
docker compose --profile test run --rm --build test

The tests assert the guarantees this page makes, not only the plumbing: that a record carrying a credential cannot have it serialized, that no metric declares a label naming a project or a query, that an unknown tool name and an unmatched route cannot create series, and that a vector failure and a lexical failure are countable apart.

docs/onboarding.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Agent Context Platform — codebase onboarding

This is a self-contained guide to the code in this repository. It is written to be read beside the linked source files in an editor. It explains the purpose of each subsystem, the important functions and classes, normal execution paths, and the database design.

The platform is an asynchronous Python service that gives agents durable, project-isolated context. It stores engineering knowledge, canonical Markdown skills, memories, creator preferences, content records, and historical content performance observations, research evidence, client identity, sessions, and audit history in MongoDB. This guide explains the core knowledge and creator subsystems in depth; use architecture.md, research.md, and client-profiles.md for the research and shared-client workflows. MongoDB Search and the local embedding provider support lexical, vector, and hybrid retrieval. FastAPI, MCP, and the CLI are three ways to reach the same service layer.

1. The architectural rule

A request should move in one direction:

REST client / MCP client / CLI
             ↓
route or adapter
             ↓
service: business rules, authorization, workflow
             ↓
repository: MongoDB persistence and queries
             ↓
MongoDB collections, indexes, migrations, Search indexes

Keep these responsibilities separate:

Layer Owns Must not own
Model/schema Data shape, enum values, serialization validation MongoDB queries or authorization policy
Route HTTP parsing, status codes, response encoding Workflow decisions or raw database access
MCP/CLI adapter Small argument contract, API call, human/agent formatting Duplicated business rules or MongoDB access
Service Lifecycle, security policy, provenance, orchestration HTTP details or ad-hoc BSON construction
Repository Collection filters, writes, transactions, pagination API permissions and user-facing prose
Database package Connection, migrations, validators, indexes, readiness Feature-specific business workflows

This organization is more than aesthetic. It makes the same rules apply whether a caller uses REST, MCP, a command, or a test.

Terms used throughout the code

Term Meaning here
Project isolation A principal can only access documents from projects it has been granted. It is a security boundary.
Profile isolation V2 creator/content documents belong to profiles, and profile access is also authorized.
Provenance IDs and references showing the knowledge sources behind a result or content record.
Canonical skill A reviewed Markdown file in Git. MongoDB stores its imported search representation.
Revision A number incremented on change for optimistic concurrency control.
Current representation The current meaningful version of an idea, brief, or content item, which may be embedded for search.
mongot MongoDB Search's sidecar search process. The application communicates with MongoDB, not mongot directly.
Retrieved text Data to inspect and cite, never instructions to execute automatically.

2. Program entry points and startup

File Role
app/main.py FastAPI application factory, lifespan, router registration, startup subsystem assembly.
app/run.py Uvicorn configuration and normal HTTP server entry point.
app/run_mcp.py MCP process entry point.
app/core/config.py Typed application settings loaded from the environment.
app/core/logging.py Logging setup and structured logging conventions.

app/main.py

The central function is create_app(settings=None). It creates FastAPI rather than relying on an irreversible global singleton, which allows tests to create an application with test settings.

Its lifespan follows this sequence:

  1. Configure logs and record build information.
  2. Create and connect the asynchronous MongoDB client.
  3. Check database, replica-set, and search availability.
  4. Run migrations and ensure standard MongoDB indexes.
  5. Reconcile lexical MongoDB Search indexes.
  6. Build the local embedding service and reconcile vector indexes.
  7. Store shared settings, database, embeddings, authentication, and audit services on app.state for dependency providers.
  8. Close database resources on shutdown.

The helper functions start_lexical_search, start_embeddings, and start_authentication deliberately isolate startup concerns. Search/embedding unavailability is observable through health/logging rather than turning a collection-creation mistake into a hidden failure.

app/run.py

options(settings) configures host, port, logging, graceful limits, and worker behavior. The service is deliberately conservative about workers because the local embedding model consumes process memory. A worker count is an operational choice tied to that model, not just a throughput setting.

app/core/config.py

Settings are the one acceptable boundary for environment-derived values. A service receives a typed setting or a constructed dependency; it should not call os.environ itself.

When adding configuration:

  1. Add a typed, validated setting field.
  2. Give it a documented default only if that default is safe.
  3. Pass it to the construction boundary needing it.
  4. Test it through a settings fixture.
  5. Avoid creating an undocumented environment lookup inside a route/service.

3. HTTP API, dependencies, and middleware

The HTTP layer is in app/api. It turns a network request into a typed service call and turns the typed result back into a network response.

File Responsibility
app/api/dependencies.py Creates service/repository dependencies from app.state.
app/api/security.py Extracts HTTP credentials and enforces scopes.
app/api/middleware.py Request IDs, timing, and exception-to-HTTP translation.
app/api/routes/health.py Liveness/readiness and component health routes.
app/api/routes/metrics.py Operational metrics route.
app/api/routes/projects.py Project API operations.
app/api/routes/context.py Project-context API operations.
app/api/routes/memory.py Memory API operations.
app/api/routes/skills.py Skill import/list/get operations.
app/api/routes/search.py V1 unified search/retrieval endpoints.
app/api/routes/creator.py Creator profile and content-pillar endpoints.
app/api/routes/content.py V2 content, retrieval, discovery, novelty, repurpose, export, publication-safety, publishing, and metrics endpoints.

Reading one route handler

A typical handler has this shape:

Pydantic request body / path / query parameters
             ↓
authenticated Principal dependency
             ↓
specific service dependency
             ↓
service method
             ↓
Pydantic response model and HTTP status

Routes answer protocol questions: which path, which status code, how to decode a cursor, and how to serialize JSON. Services answer domain questions: whether a profile is accessible, whether a content transition is legal, and whether a body change must create a version.

app/api/dependencies.py is the request-time composition root. It retrieves shared infrastructure from app.state and wires repositories into services. This is why route functions should not instantiate a Mongo client, an embedding model, or a repository directly.

app/api/security.py converts a valid API key into a Principal. It verifies both a coarse permission, such as content:read, and resource grants such as permitted profile/project IDs.

app/api/middleware.py attaches request context and maps expected domain errors to stable HTTP responses. It should not hide unexpected programming errors as successful results.

4. Models and schemas

Models in app/models are Pydantic data contracts. They validate input and document shapes, but they do not save themselves. Keeping models separate from repositories avoids accidental database writes from validation code.

File Main purpose
app/models/common.py UTC helpers, deterministic IDs, shared document fields, tags, cursor encoding/decoding, Page.
app/models/project.py Project documents and project request/response schemas.
app/models/project_context.py Project-context documents, types, source/status/importance schemas.
app/models/memory.py Memory scope/type/status and memory API contracts.
app/models/skill.py Skill identity, trust level, version, status, and metadata.
app/models/skill_chunk.py Searchable chunk content, section, token, and embedding fields.
app/models/embedding.py Stored vector, model ID, dimensions, and generation timestamp.
app/models/conversation.py Conversation-turn storage model.
app/models/retrieval_log.py Retrieval query/result audit data.
app/models/api_key.py API-key metadata, grants, status, expiration contracts.
app/models/audit_log.py Immutable audit event contracts.
app/models/content.py V2 creator/content enums, documents, publication receipt fields, generic metric observations, pagination, and search types.

Common document behavior

MongoDocumentModel in app/models/common.py provides the common persistence fields:

_id          MongoDB primary key
created_at   UTC creation timestamp
updated_at   UTC last-change timestamp
revision     optimistic-concurrency number

TaggedDocument adds tag validation. Page is the common cursor-pagination result: items plus a next cursor. Cursor pagination is preferable to deep offset/skip pagination because it is stable when later documents are inserted and avoids an ever-growing skip cost.

The deterministic ObjectId helpers create stable application identities where an import or create operation needs idempotency. These public IDs complement MongoDB's internal _id; they do not replace it.

Content lifecycle and platform validation

ContentStatus in app/models/content.py admits only:

idea → selected → researching → brief_ready → drafting → review
     → approved → published → archived

The enum catches invalid vocabulary at the API/document boundary. The service, not the enum, decides whether an arrow is allowed. For example, published to drafting requires an explicit revision workflow; it is not a normal PATCH transition.

ContentPlatform currently admits linkedin, medium, and github. This lets invalid platform values fail before they reach persistence or platform formatting. Adding youtube, x, reddit, newsletter, or blog requires a deliberate enum, adapter, test, and possibly skill change.

Generic metric validation and identity

ContentMetricDocument in app/models/content.py is the persisted model for a single observation. Its deterministic MongoDB ID is derived from the profile ID and metric_id, so retrying the same logical metric insert produces a conflict instead of a duplicate. It has the normal creation and revision fields, but metric observations are append-only: the API exposes creation and history reads, not an edit operation.

The metrics map is deliberately generic rather than a fixed table of social network columns. Model validation requires a non-empty map whose keys are safe identifiers and whose values are finite, non-negative numbers. source tells a reviewer where the observation came from, while provider_metadata is a bounded structured place for provider-specific descriptive data. Neither field grants the server permission to contact that provider.

app/schemas/content.py keeps the HTTP contract separate through ContentMetricCreateRequest, ContentMetricResponse, and ContentMetricListResponse. This is why the route can accept a create request without exposing MongoDB _id, and can return a cursor page without letting a caller submit persistence-only fields.

Public request and response schemas

The API-specific Pydantic contracts are intentionally separate from MongoDB documents. A request model controls what a caller may submit; a response model controls what the API exposes. The service maps between request schemas and domain documents.

File Contract family
app/schemas/project.py Project create/update/list/detail request and response contracts.
app/schemas/context.py Project-context create/update/search/list contracts.
app/schemas/memory.py Memory create/update/search/list contracts.
app/schemas/skill.py Skill front matter, import/list/detail/search contracts.
app/schemas/search.py Unified engineering search request/result contracts.
app/schemas/creator.py Creator profile and content-pillar create/update/list/detail contracts.
app/schemas/content.py Content lifecycle, versions, search, discovery, novelty, repurpose, export, publication, and metrics contracts.

Request schemas reject forbidden lifecycle/platform values and malformed references before a service is called. Document models additionally protect the data that can actually be persisted. Do not expose a database document directly just because it happens to serialize.

Startup order and idempotency

initialize_database in app/db/initializer.py retains this order:

run migrations → ensure normal MongoDB indexes → reconcile Search indexes

A migration changes durable historical state. The migration runner records completed versions in _schema_migrations using a unique version identity. It is safe to run at every startup and handles concurrent startup attempts. Never alter the intended effect of a migration that might already have run in an environment. Add the next migration instead.

Collection creation in app/db/collections.py is idempotent. Existing collections are expected during a repeated startup. Validators in app/db/schema.py are strict: unexpected stored fields are rejected with additionalProperties false. This catches schema drift early, but it means a durable field addition must update model, validator, migration, repository, and tests together.

Standard index vs Search index

Normal indexes in app/db/indexes.py serve uniqueness, filtering, sorting, cursor pagination, and ordinary lookup. An example is the unique compound identity for a content version: profile_id plus content_id plus version.

MongoDB Search indexes are derived search resources:

Index kind Good at
Text/lexical Exact terms such as Outbox, Keycloak, identifiers, and names
Vector Semantically related phrasing and concepts
Hybrid Combining both candidate sets before policy ranking

The application uses MongoDB's Search-index management API through app/db/search_indexes.py. MongoDB coordinates mongot. The application does not connect directly to mongot.

Content index code is careful to translate profile, platform, project, status, pillar, and tag filters into equivalent lexical and vector prefilters. A security filter must behave identically in every retrieval mode.

6. Repositories

A repository is the only code that turns domain values into collection filters, BSON updates, aggregation pipelines, sessions, and cursor bounds. Repository methods accept/return typed data; they do not return loose database documents to routes.

File Persistence responsibility
app/repositories/base.py MongoRepository shared CRUD, pagination, search, errors, timestamps, and revision-aware updates.
app/repositories/project_repository.py Project identity and persistence.
app/repositories/context_repository.py Project context and context search candidates.
app/repositories/memory_repository.py Memory scope, recency, search, and supersession persistence.
app/repositories/skill_repository.py Skill metadata and active-version queries.
app/repositories/skill_chunk_repository.py Chunk writes and lexical/vector candidate queries.
app/repositories/conversation_repository.py Conversation turns.
app/repositories/retrieval_repository.py V1 retrieval read models.
app/repositories/vectors.py Shared vector data/query support.
app/repositories/api_key_repository.py Active/revoked/expired key persistence.
app/repositories/audit_repository.py Append-only audit events.
app/repositories/content_repository.py Creator profile, pillar, idea, brief, item, version, link, metric, campaign, and content search persistence.
app/repositories/backup_repository.py Persistence-side backup/restore integration.
app/repositories/errors.py Not-found, conflict, validation, and concurrency persistence errors.

The base repository methods

MongoRepository in app/repositories/base.py centralizes the repeated safe patterns:

Method What it is for
_create Serialize and insert a validated model; translate duplicate identity to conflict.
_get Fetch exactly one safe filter and translate missing documents.
_page Apply stable ordering and cursor bounds, then return Page.
_recent Bounded recent-document query used by discovery/retrieval.
_scored_search Run a score-producing search query/pipeline and return typed candidates.
_search Shared filter/search dispatch.
_update Revision-aware update, timestamp update, revision increment.
_update_fields Safe partial field update helper.
_delete Explicit deletion only for resources whose lifecycle allows it.

Optimistic concurrency is based on a filter like this:

update_one(
  { _id: id, revision: expected_revision },
  { $set: changed_fields, $inc: { revision: 1 } }
)

If the matched count is zero, a caller used an obsolete revision or no longer has a valid target. The code reports a conflict instead of silently erasing a newer edit. No long lock is held while a person or agent is deciding what to write.

Content versions use a MongoDB transaction

MongoContentItemRepository in app/repositories/content_repository.py uses a MongoDB session with a transaction for initial content creation and version append. It changes these two representations atomically:

content_items current title/body/status/current_version
                         +
content_versions immutable snapshot insert

If either write fails, neither becomes visible. This prevents a current content item from referring to a missing version and prevents orphaned version records.

V1 context, memory, and skills

ContextService handles explicitly supplied project facts, decisions, documents, and technical context. MemoryService handles remembered information and checks scope/project/client ownership. Shared scopes are global and project; operational scopes are agent and project_agent. Agent identity is derived from authentication, and project scopes require an explicit project. Supersession links an old memory to newer knowledge instead of deleting important history.

SkillService delegates Markdown parsing/chunking to app/skills, records imported versions/chunks, and selects active versions. Canonical skill files remain in Git. MongoDB stores the indexed copy used by retrieval, not a second authoring source.

Retrieval is evidence assembly

RetrievalService gathers candidates from authorized project context, memory, skills, and conversation sources. It then uses pure deterministic functions in app/retrieval to merge, filter, score, de-duplicate, and trim them to a token budget. It returns source IDs and metadata so callers can explain where an answer came from.

A retrieval result is not an instruction channel. Agents must treat content in a returned skill, memory, or conversation as evidence/data.

V2 creator and content guarantees

CreatorService supports multiple active/inactive profiles. A creator profile is data describing audiences, voice, terminology, formatting, language, interests, and objectives. It is not hidden system instructions.

ContentService guarantees:

  • Ideas, briefs, items, and versions retain source references.
  • Body changes create/record immutable versions rather than overwriting history.
  • Rollback restores a previous representation through service logic.
  • Invalid transitions are rejected.
  • Published content cannot casually move back to drafting.
  • Archived records can remain searchable when the request allows them.
  • Current meaningful representations, not every historical version, are embedded.

Discovery, novelty, and repurposing services return structured material for a human or agent to judge and write. They do not add an LLM dependency to the server and do not fabricate project experiences.

Publication review is an advisory safety layer, not a confidentiality guarantee. It returns redacted, explainable indicators and leaves the source content unchanged. Approval rescans the current revision, so a stale review cannot approve a changed document. Publishing is a separate explicit action on an already approved item; a provider receives stored content, never arbitrary prose submitted to a publishing endpoint.

ContentMetricsService stores descriptive observations only. It does not fetch third-party analytics, infer a content strategy, rewrite creator preferences, change pillars, or optimize toward engagement. A future provider integration may submit the same validated observation shape, but it remains optional.

8. Pure retrieval and ranking modules

The app/retrieval package avoids FastAPI/MongoDB dependencies so its behavior can be tested as deterministic functions.

File What to learn from it
app/retrieval/types.py Candidate, match, source, score, and result structures.
app/retrieval/query.py Query normalization and query validation.
app/retrieval/filters.py Shared filtering rules.
app/retrieval/ranking.py Source priority, recency, configurable weights, final scoring.
app/retrieval/hybrid.py Merge/deduplicate lexical and vector candidates.
app/retrieval/context_builder.py Token-budget-aware selection and final context assembly.

Content retrieval adds named profiles in app/services/content_retrieval_service.py without changing engineering ranking globally:

Profile Purpose
content_creation Combine project context, memory, technical/content skills, published history, and conversation with configurable priorities.
content_history Find authored content and its history.
content_ideation Find ideas, pillars, recent evidence, and unpublished overlap.
content_repurposing Find source content plus relevant historical content and platform guidance.

The content_creation starting source priorities are designed to prefer private, relevant engineering evidence over generic text:

project_context   1.00
memory            0.95
technical_skill   0.85
content_skill     0.85
published_content 0.70
conversation      0.40

Those values are policy configuration, not globally forced V1 behavior.

9. Embeddings and MongoDB Search

File Purpose
app/embeddings/base.py Embedding provider protocol.
app/embeddings/types.py Input/output types for embeddings.
app/embeddings/config.py Provider configuration contract.
app/embeddings/local.py Local model implementation/loading/inference.
app/embeddings/errors.py Explicit provider failures.
app/search/types.py Search result/diagnostic data types.
app/search/logging.py Structured search logging.

Services depend on the small EmbeddingProvider protocol, not directly on a model library. Persisted vectors carry the model identifier, dimensions, and generation time. That metadata makes it possible to notice model incompatibility rather than mixing unrelated vector spaces silently.

Lexical search is valuable for exact technical vocabulary. Vector search is valuable when a query and source express the same concept in different words. Hybrid retrieval gathers both candidates, applies authorization and filters, and then uses explicit source/recency policy ranking. It is not merely an average of two scores from different systems.

11. Platform abstraction and exporting

The content package formats already-written content. It does not create core prose and it does not publish externally.

File Responsibility
app/content/errors.py Content-platform domain errors.
app/content/discovery.py Structured discovery input/result types.
app/content/novelty.py Overlap and novelty result types.
app/content/repurposing.py Repurpose-plan input/result types.

app/content/platforms/github.py GitHub Markdown, code fences, and file-path suggestions.

ContentPlatform is the extension seam:

validate(content)     reject invalid platform-specific material
format(content)       create the platform representation
export(content, mode) return stdout/file/Markdown representation

To add a new platform, extend the enum, implement this protocol, register it, test format/Unicode/length/code constraints, and add a canonical skill if writing guidance is needed. Keep the adapter deterministic and side-effect free.

Publication safety, explicit receipts, and metrics

These are deliberately separate operations. A safety review is read-only; approval is a revision-aware lifecycle transition; publishing is an explicit publication-receipt request with the shipped manual adapter; and a metric snapshot is descriptive data captured after the fact. None of them generates prose or automatically changes a creator profile.

File Classes and methods to study What the code teaches
app/content/publication.py PublicationSafetyPolicy, PublicationReview, PublicationFinding, review_content_for_publication() A deterministic pattern scanner can return a finding type, severity, field, and line/column without returning or logging the matched secret. It is advisory, bounded, and policy-configurable.
app/services/content_publication_service.py ContentPublicationService.review_content_for_publication(), review_item_for_publication(), approve_content() Approval requires review status and the expected current revision, performs a fresh scan, blocks configured high-severity findings, and persists only the legal review → approved transition.
app/content/publishers/base.py Publisher protocol, PublisherRegistry, PublicationReceipt Provider adapters have one narrow contract: validate a connection, publish a stored item with an idempotency key, and return redacted status. The registry contains only explicitly configured providers.
app/content/publishers/manual.py ManualPublisher The safe default integration pattern: record a human-confirmed publication locally without credentials, network traffic, or an implicit external post.
app/services/content_publishing_service.py ContentPublishingService.publish_content() Publishing rereads and rescans the current item, requires approved, generates or accepts an idempotency key, and persists the receipt with a revision-aware update. A retry with the same durable receipt is safe.
app/services/content_metrics_service.py ContentMetricsService.create_metric(), list_metrics() Metric capture checks profile and content ownership before it creates an immutable observation. Retrieval validates time bounds and returns one content item plus a newest-first page.
app/repositories/content_repository.py MongoContentMetricRepository.list_for_content() Time-series pagination uses the tuple (captured_at, _id) as its descending cursor. That avoids skipped or duplicated snapshots when equal capture times occur.
app/db/migrations/v012_content_metric_source_metadata.py ContentMetricSourceMigration.up() A strict-schema migration temporarily permits legacy documents, backfills safe defaults, then reapplies the final validator. Its down() refuses to delete durable provenance.

The approval and publication sequence

draft → review ──POST publication-review──> redacted findings (no mutation)
              └─POST approve, expected_revision──> approved + audit event
approved ──POST export──> formatted representation only
approved ──POST publish, expected_revision + provider──> provider receipt
                                                    ↓
                                         published + durable receipt

A review response can contain project IDs and source references so an authorized reviewer can make a decision, but it does not echo a detected secret. The scanner checks current title/body, public URL data, and configured sensitive project/provenance policy. It can find likely API keys, credentials, tokens, private URLs and hosts, internal network addresses, customer identifiers, PII, and sensitive repository/architecture references. Detection is intentionally not a claim that a document is safe to disclose.

POST /api/v2/content/{id}/publication-review requires content:read; POST /api/v2/content/{id}/approve requires content:write; POST /api/v2/content/{id}/publish requires the separate content:publish scope. All three first check profile access and every project referenced by the current item or its provenance. The publish endpoint receives an ID, provider, revision, and idempotency key—not a free-form body—so it cannot be used as a broad arbitrary text publisher.

Generic content-metric time series

A ContentMetricDocument is a deterministic, profile-owned observation:

metric_id          caller-supplied deterministic identity within a profile
content_id         existing content item that owns this observation
platform           linkedin | medium | github (extensible enum)
captured_at        when the numbers were observed, not when they were written
metrics            non-empty map of identifier keys to finite, non-negative numbers
source             provenance label; migration v012 defaults legacy records to manual
provider_metadata  provider-specific descriptive object; no provider call occurs

The public API is intentionally small:

  • POST /api/v2/content/{id}/metrics requires content:write and stores one explicit snapshot.
  • GET /api/v2/content/{id}/metrics requires content:read and accepts an optional platform, capture-time range, limit, and cursor.
  • MCP get_content_metrics calls that GET endpoint through the normal MCP HTTP client; it never reads MongoDB directly.

Metric keys are generic, so views, impressions, likes, comments, shares, clicks, bookmarks, and followers_gained fit without creating a new schema column. A numeric value must be finite and non-negative; booleans, negative counts, NaN, and Infinity are rejected. The service does not add an analytics provider, collect remote data, produce automatic strategy insights, or alter creator voice, pillars, or content. For the database mechanics behind this design, read the MongoDB tutorial alongside the source files above.

12. Security and audit

File Purpose
app/security/keys.py Secure key generation/parsing/hashing/verification helpers.
app/security/principal.py Principal scope, project, and profile grant methods.
app/security/scopes.py Canonical scope vocabulary and validation.
app/services/auth_service.py Loads active API keys and enforces permissions.
app/services/api_key_service.py Key lifecycle.
app/services/audit_service.py Audit-event service.

Authentication answers who made a request. Authorization answers whether that principal may perform the operation on the target resource. Both are necessary.

V2 uses scopes including creator:read, creator:write, content:read, content:write, and the separate content:publish grant. A scope alone is insufficient: a service also verifies the profile/project grant before it creates or returns data. Search filters must be pre-authorized, not trusted as client-provided security constraints. The same content scopes govern publication review, approval, explicit publishing, and metric history: the route verifies the profile and every project in the current content item or source reference before it reads or changes a record.

Plaintext API keys are only shown during creation. The database stores hashes and non-secret metadata. Audit records identify key IDs/names and request outcomes, never secret key material.

app/cli/commands/content.py Content lifecycle, search, novelty, repurpose, export commands.
app/cli/commands/keys.py Operator key-management commands.
app/cli/commands/backup.py Operator backup/restore commands.
app/cli/commands/health.py Health/diagnostic commands.

Administrative commands are explicit operator workflows. They still use the same core services instead of embedding feature-specific MongoDB queries in argument parser code.

15. Observability

File Responsibility
app/observability/context.py Request-scoped IDs/context for diagnostics.
app/observability/instruments.py Metric counter/histogram/gauge definitions.
app/observability/metrics.py Registry, collection, and metric exposition.
app/observability/mongo.py PyMongo command listener and Mongo command telemetry.

The /metrics route exposes operational measurements; it does not decide what to measure. Metric definitions live in instruments.py. The Mongo listener observes commands at the client layer, avoiding hand-written timing code in every repository.

Do not confuse operational telemetry with V2 content metrics. Operational telemetry answers questions such as request latency and MongoDB command health; content_metrics holds authorized, user-supplied performance snapshots of a specific content item. The first is emitted by the running service; the second is durable product data retrieved through the content API.

Correlate a request through request ID, API logs, audit records, and metrics. Do not log raw API keys, sensitive source bodies, or vector contents merely for debugging convenience.

16. Backup and restore

File Responsibility
app/backup/naming.py Safe/deterministic archive names.
app/backup/manifest.py Manifest format, checksums, collection inventory.
app/backup/retention.py Retention-policy calculation.
app/backup/tools.py Controlled wrappers around MongoDB backup tools.
app/services/backup_service.py Backup/restore orchestration and validation.
app/repositories/backup_repository.py Backup persistence support.

A persistent collection is not fully implemented until the backup configuration and restore validation include it. A manifest records the archive inventory and integrity information. Search indexes are derived resources which can be reconciled/rebuilt; source documents and content version history are durable data that must be preserved. content_metrics is an existing content collection, so migration v012 extends its validator rather than creating a second database or backup path. The whole MongoDB database archive therefore continues to include metric history and its source metadata.

17. Small supporting packages

File Responsibility
app/projects/types.py Project-domain value types.
app/projects/errors.py Project-domain exceptions.
app/memory/types.py Memory-domain value types.
app/memory/errors.py Memory-domain exceptions.
app/creator/errors.py Creator-domain exceptions.

Most package initializer files only mark a directory as a Python package. The notable behavior-bearing initializers are app/content/platforms/init.py, which registers platform services, and app/mcp/tools/init.py, which holds the tool registry.

18. Safe change checklists

Adding a field to an existing stored document

  1. Extend the relevant Pydantic model in app/models.
  2. Extend the matching validator in app/db/schema.py.
  3. Add an append-only migration if existing persisted documents need alteration, backfill, or validator evolution.
  4. Add a normal index only when a real query, sort, or uniqueness constraint needs it.
  5. Extend the matching repository serializer/filter/update.
  6. Add business validation to the service.
  7. Extend public API schemas/routes only if it is an API contract field.
  8. Extend backup/restore configuration for a new collection.
  9. Test validation, migration, persistence, authorization, and API behavior.

Adding a searchable field/resource

Perform the previous steps, then:

  1. Choose the embedding text representation deliberately.
  2. Store embedding model, dimensions, and generated timestamp.
  3. Add lexical and vector definitions to the correct DB index module.
  4. Make lexical/vector prefilters semantically identical.
  5. Reconcile the Search indexes at startup.
  6. Test exact lexical hits, semantic hits, hybrid merge, filters, profile/project isolation, and archived behavior if applicable.

Adding an API/MCP/CLI operation

  1. Define Pydantic input/output schemas.
  2. Add a service method; do not hide the rule in a route.
  3. Add/extend repository queries only as needed.
  4. Enforce the narrowest scope and resource ownership.
  5. Add the route using existing dependencies.
  6. Add audit behavior where it is security-sensitive.
  7. Add an MCP wrapper only if agents need it; it calls the API.
  8. Add a CLI command only if humans need it; it calls API/service boundaries.
  9. Add focused tests at each relevant layer.

Extending content metrics safely

  1. Keep ContentMetricDocument as an append-only observation; never overwrite a historical capture merely because newer numbers arrive.
  2. Use a stable metric_id for a retryable capture and create a new ID for a distinct observation.
  3. Validate raw values before persistence: identifier keys, finite non-negative numeric values, timezone-aware captured_at, and bounded metadata.
  4. Query through list_for_content() so the profile/content filter and (captured_at, _id) cursor stay paired with the index.
  5. Preserve the route/service authorization sequence: profile grant, current content lookup, then all referenced project grants.
  6. If an optional provider is added later, implement a narrow adapter that supplies this explicit shape. Do not make startup, reads, or manual entry depend on provider credentials or availability.
  7. Add model, migration, repository, service, API, MCP, authorization, and no-provider tests; document any new durable field and backup consequence.

Adding a platform

  1. Extend ContentPlatform in app/models/content.py.
  2. Implement the protocol under app/content/platforms.
  3. Register the adapter in the platform registry.
  4. Keep validation/format/export deterministic and non-publishing.
  5. Test invalid platform values, Unicode, long content, and code formatting.
  6. Add canonical writing guidance when it improves retrieval.

19. Testing and reading order

Use focused tests while changing one subsystem. Broad end-to-end and MCP scenario tests are important integration confidence, but they should not be the only feedback loop for a small change. Use Ruff for style/lint issues and mypy for type safety. Do not weaken validation or security just to satisfy a test.

For the publication and metric service boundaries, start with tests/unit/test_content_publication.py, tests/unit/test_content_publishing.py, tests/unit/test_content_metrics.py, and their migration tests: tests/unit/test_content_publication_migration.py and tests/unit/test_content_metric_migration.py. Then read the content MCP tests in tests/unit/test_content_mcp.py. Together they show the intended redaction, approval, idempotency, invalid-value, authorization, pagination, migration, and thin-MCP behavior without requiring every long-running end-to-end MCP scenario.

A practical reading order is:

  1. app/main.py and app/api/dependencies.py.
  2. app/models/common.py and one domain model such as app/models/content.py.
  3. app/repositories/base.py, then a domain repository such as app/repositories/content_repository.py.
  4. A matching service such as app/services/content_service.py, then its API route.
  5. app/db/initializer.py, app/db/schema.py, and the migration runner.
  6. app/retrieval/hybrid.py plus app/services/retrieval_service.py.
  7. The matching MCP/CLI adapter to verify it remains thin.

Normal indexes enforce local identity/query speed, JSON schema enforces shape, and services enforce cross-collection rules, lifecycle, and provenance.

docs/organization-management.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Organization management

Human management uses session-only /api/v6 endpoints and the current verified organization. People, teams, invitations, assignments, delegations and access requests are tenant-scoped. A submitted organization, team or user ID selects a resource; it never establishes authority. See the console guide for navigation and verification for release-gate status.

Roles and effective permission

The fixed human templates are org_owner, org_admin, executive, team_lead, reviewer, contributor, auditor and viewer. installation_operator is a separate host boundary. The authoritative capability catalog is catalog.py.

A template lists eligible capabilities. An actual assignment must name each action, resource dimension and selector, and be within current ancestry, target, role, depth and expiry limits. Grant authority, metadata monitoring and data use are separate. An owner title is not an unrestricted corpus bypass.

Selector Meaning
none No resources; the default for new managed assignments
include Only the explicitly selected existing IDs
all_in_org Existing and future resources in this organization, with separate explicit issuance authority

Empty arrays never become ALL in managed policy. The reviewed legacy-adoption adapter preserves explicit all_in_org only within its adoption organization. Read-A/write-B assignments remain separate; their actions and resources cannot be combined into write-A. Project-directory rights do not imply context rights. Organization-global knowledge, imported skills and private client memory each have explicit policy dimensions.

Effective-access views explain only authorized sources. A worker can inspect their own access; a lead's view is limited to the delegated management boundary. Global users, login identities, factors and other organizations' memberships are not exposed through tenant directory search. Directory search uses permitted tenant display names, with bounded pagination and policy-bound cursors.

Initial owner and bounded delegation

The installation operator provisions the initial owner and records independent approval of the root ceiling and minimal project-directory bootstrap policy. The policy engine activates explicit assignments transactionally. This is the documented operator bootstrap exception, not anonymous ownership or an owner corpus bypass. Further self/corpus grants require independent approval or the documented operator recovery procedure.

Owner/admin delegation can appoint executive/lead policy within its reviewed ceiling. An executive needs explicit delegation authority. Leads can appoint permitted member roles within their named team and parent envelope; they cannot appoint owner/admin or widen themselves. Team-member leaf assignments have no further child delegation. Self-grants and self-ceiling changes are refused.

Every child is bounded by parent generation, allowed targets/roles, remaining depth, exact action/resource policy and expiry. Parent revoke/narrow and child issuance contend on the shared organization policy anchor. Governance mutation, immutable audit and outbox commit together; audit failure refuses the mutation. Ordinary domain audit retains its documented best-effort contract.

Invite a lead or worker

  1. Inspect your effective management and delegation rights. Create/manage a team only if that action is authorized; a lead cannot place arbitrary people into a team to acquire authority over them.
  2. Select the recipient/team, exact role and resource policy, and expiry. Review NONE/selected/all-in-org explicitly. Invitations retain the reviewed parent generation and team boundary, not just a role name.
  3. Submit with current revisions and recent MFA. The configured private local mail sink provides operator handoff; this distribution makes no SMTP delivery claim. Never use real recipients in verification fixtures.
  4. The recipient verifies the invitation and authenticates an existing identity or completes invitation-only local enrollment and MFA. Acceptance rechecks current issuer authority, ownership, generations and expiry and consumes the purpose-bound secret atomically.

An invitation cannot reset an existing person's credentials/MFA, restore a suspended membership or satisfy another organization's required SSO provider. Equal emails never link identities. Renewing a proposal invalidates the previous pending challenge; it does not revive an expired or revoked grant.

Request and approve access

A worker requests exact action/resource policy with the current membership and policy revision and an expiry. The request grants nothing. An independent authorized approver checks the exact current revision, resource ownership and their still-current parent envelope before deciding. A lead cannot approve beyond delegated team/resources. Self-approval, stale revisions and foreign references fail. Decisions are immutable; an edit needs a new reviewed request.

After a conflict, reload the current policy and deliberately retry. The console does not silently replay a review or credential issuance. Expiry, suspension and generation changes are current authorization inputs, not delayed TTL cleanup.

Approve a client, then issue its credential

Client policy approval and secret issuance are separate actions. The lead or other authorized manager approves the bounded client policy and verified human sponsor/team relationship. Old descriptive owner_id is not verified ownership. Legacy keys must be explicitly claimed to a verified owner/service account or revoked before managed activation.

The recipient authenticates and generates their own credential once after the required step-up. Leads inspect/revoke permitted metadata; they cannot recover another worker's token. Retry returns safe metadata, and lost delivery requires revocation/replacement. Rotation, expiry and revocation are explicit and revision-checked. Tokens are not replayed through idempotency or outbox state.

Unattended automation uses an explicit organization service account with an authorized custodian. Effective rights intersect the credential, client and current sponsor/team/delegation policy for each action/resource in REST and MCP. Capability previews describe limits and never authorize operations themselves. Permission-template edits/disable do not propagate to assigned clients or keys.

Normal machines cannot approve content/research merely with write permission. The separately approved service-account reviewer exception also requires current custody, operation-specific review/read rights and independent reviewer ancestry. Verified human and event-time sponsor provenance enforce self-review exclusion; a different client belonging to the same sponsor is not independent. See managed agents and management policy.

Offboard, reinstate and hand over ownership

Inspect the impact on membership, teams, assignments, clients, credentials, browser sessions and pending jobs. Suspend only within your management boundary, using the expected revision and step-up. Future authorized work and result downloads are denied after the current policy revocation fence; already committed work, authored knowledge and historical audit are preserved.

Membership suspension advances its authority revision and revokes human browser sessions. Team suspension/removal advances the relevant generation/edge revision. Reinstatement advances authority again and does not reactivate revoked children. Removing membership in one organization does not suspend another membership. Team moves do not rewrite event-time attribution or expose previous-team history.

The last active owner is protected. Ownership uses a distinct offer/acceptance handover with verified active membership, recent MFA and current revisions. The reviewed governance root transfers; personal corpus assignments do not automatically transfer. Ordinary role editing/suspension cannot remove the owner. If a legitimate independent approver is unavailable, use documented installation operator recovery with explicit approval and transactional audit; do not invent a browser self-grant or anonymous owner claim.

Operator boundary and further contracts

Logical tenant isolation protects application interfaces. Installation operators with database, secret mounts or raw backups remain trusted and can access all organizations' stored data. An org owner is not automatically such an operator. Whole-installation backup/restore, raw shared metrics, provider configuration, adoption and cutover remain outside ordinary organization permissions. A tenant CSV export never authorizes a database --drop or live restore.

See deployment/recovery, human-management APIs, identity/SSO, and monitoring policy.

docs/production-readiness.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Production readiness

Validate your own deployment and dataset before relying on the service. The shipped Compose configuration is a small self-hosted topology: one API process, one MongoDB replica-set member, and one mongot process. It has persistent storage and backup tooling, with no automatic host failover or published availability SLA.

Resources and capacity

MongoDB, search indexes, and the local embedding model all consume memory. Compose applies per-service memory, CPU, and process limits. Size the host above the combined limits plus operating-system overhead; increase limits based on measurements from your corpus, ingestion workload, and concurrency. A small test dataset is not a capacity guarantee for a larger deployment.

The API loads one embedding model per process. Increasing worker count multiplies that cost and changes the gateway's process-local control behavior. Keep the default single-process gateway unless you have evaluated shared rate/concurrency controls and model memory. Search memory and disk usage grow with indexed content. Monitor free disk and index build status as well as request latency.

Use the benchmark harness against a representative isolated dataset:

.venv/bin/python scripts/benchmark.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --token-file ./secrets/benchmark-api-key --project-id payment-service --check

Issue only the scopes needed by the harness. Record the commit, hardware, dependency versions, corpus size, index readiness, concurrency, and cache state with results. The harness's targets are configurable deployment checks, not product guarantees.

Deployment controls

  • Keep API_AUTH_ENABLED=true; issue independent credentials with explicit scope and project/profile grants. Separate coding, review, promotion, and publication responsibilities where your workflow requires it.
  • Use HTTPS for remote MCP/API clients and configure trusted reverse-proxy headers deliberately. Database, bootstrap, and search ports remain private.
  • Provision unique secrets through your deployment's secret-management process. Keep the source checkout, secrets, backups, and private notes outside any public web root. Deploy the introduction website independently.
  • Run the application containers as their configured non-root user with read-only filesystems and resource limits. Upstream MongoDB entrypoints retain capabilities needed to initialize storage and drop privileges.
  • Apply outbound network restrictions when enabling research ingestion from untrusted submitters. DNS preflight checks are not connection pinning; see research.md for the remaining egress boundary.

See deployment.md and security.md for the settings and authorization model.

Readiness and failure behavior

/health/live reports the process. /health/ready checks the authenticated MongoDB path, primary status, the search coordinator, the configured embedding model, and core knowledge search indexes. It does not independently prove every creator-content or research index can answer a query. Verify those workflows with representative authorized requests before putting them into service.

Monitor readiness alongside error rate, request latency, index status, resource usage, disk space, and restore-test results. Database operations and readiness probes have bounded timeouts; dependency failures should produce safe service errors. An embedding outage can leave lexical retrieval available, but model requirements still affect readiness according to configuration.

In an isolated staging deployment, exercise database/search/model unavailability, credential expiration and revocation, denied project access, stale revisions, retry idempotency, and rate limits. Confirm recovery rather than assuming a container restart restored the complete workflow.

Backup and recovery

MongoDB holds durable records, vectors, identity/grants, provenance, and history. Search indexes are derived and must be rebuilt after a restore. Canonical skill sources remain in Git. Store backups away from the service host, restrict access, and test restoration on an isolated deployment.

The backup guide documents retention, integrity checks, restore verification, and recovery. Schedule both backups and actual restore verification. A single-member replica set does not protect against losing its only host.

Release verification

Run the unit/static checks and the relevant live integration checks described in CONTRIBUTING.md. Use a dedicated fixture database; integration tests must not mutate your real knowledge store. Rebuild and inspect the public website/guide. To audit the public source tree, run:

python3 scripts/prepare_open_source_release.py --check

Dependency locks pin versions rather than wheel hashes. Container image digests pin their selected upstream images. Review security updates and rerun build, integration, and license-notice checks when changing those pins.

docs/projects.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Projects and project context

A project is one software system or repository. Project context is the durable technical knowledge that belongs to it: architecture decisions, business rules, API conventions, known issues. Runtime skills are imported per organization and require explicit skill rights; context is what is true about one system in particular, which is why it outranks skills during retrieval.

Project isolation

Every read, write, and search preserves this isolation boundary.

  • Context belongs to exactly one project and can never be moved.
  • A repository is bound to its project when it is built, so no call site can widen the scope.
  • Every read, write, and search is restricted to that project, and a query naming a different project is refused rather than quietly answered.
  • Retrieval applies the rule again on every candidate, so a result that escaped a backend filter still cannot be returned.
  • A request naming no project reaches no project-owned context at all: context must be asked for explicitly and is never inherited by omission.
  • A context item that exists in another project is reported as "not found", the same as one that does not exist. One project must not learn what another stores, including whether an identifier is in use.

There is no API-user authentication yet, so the caller states which project it is asking about. The enforcement is still ours: the query is scoped by the stated project rather than looked up unscoped and checked afterwards. When API keys arrive they constrain which projects a caller may name, without changing any of the rules above.

Projects

Field Meaning
project_id Stable identifier every context item is filed under
name Human-readable system name
description What the system is
repository Where its code lives
environment The environment this boundary describes
tags Free-form labels, unique within a project

The identifier is the boundary itself, so it cannot be taken twice: a repeat create reports a conflict rather than merging two systems' knowledge under one name. _id is derived from project_id, so the uniqueness is structural rather than a check that could be skipped.

Context

Field Meaning
project_id The owning project. Identity, not content: it can never be edited
type One of the fourteen supported context types
title What the entry is about
content The knowledge itself
importance 0..1, assigned by whoever stored it; a ranking signal
tags Free-form labels used for filtering
source Where the entry came from
status active, archived, or superseded
external_id Optional idempotency key. Identity, so it cannot be edited

Supported types: architecture, architecture_decision, business_rule, api, database, infrastructure, deployment, security, integration, convention, troubleshooting, known_issue, implementation, constraint.

Context is written for a project that already exists; context belonging to no project would be unreachable and unattributable, so the write is refused instead.

Lifecycle

Status is how knowledge stops being current without being destroyed. Retrieval returns active context by default; archiving or superseding an entry removes it from answers while keeping the record and its history. The public lifecycle API archives or supersedes context rather than deleting it.

Idempotency

Supplying an external_id makes a create repeatable: the second write returns what is already stored rather than failing or duplicating. That is what makes an interrupted import safe to run again. The identifier derives the document _id together with the project, so two projects can use the same key without colliding.

Updates

PATCH changes only the fields it names. Changing the title or the body re-embeds the document, because a vector that no longer describes the stored text would quietly return the wrong thing. Changing only metadata leaves the vector alone.

expected_revision makes a lost update visible: if the item changed after it was read, the write is refused with a conflict instead of overwriting someone else's edit. Omitting it uses the revision just read, which still detects a concurrent write but cannot detect one that happened before the client decided what to send.

Retrieval

Context is embedded from its title and body together — a vector built from the body alone loses the framing a question is most likely to match — and indexed twice, exactly as skill chunks are: a vector index for meaning and a Search index for exact technical vocabulary.

Because a context document carries its own metadata, every filter is a pre-filter on the same document: project, type, status, tags, and a minimum importance all restrict the search itself rather than trimming its results afterwards.

Two entry points return context:

  • POST /api/v1/context/search searches one project's context only.
  • POST /api/v1/search ranks that project's context alongside every other source it may see; see search.md.
  • POST /api/v1/skills/search/hybrid adds that project's context to skill retrieval when the request names a project, ranking both together.

Ranking is described in retrieval.md. The part that matters here is source priority: project_context scores 1.00 against an active skill's 0.95, so project-specific knowledge beats generic knowledge when both are equally relevant.

API

POST /api/v1/projects
GET  /api/v1/projects
GET  /api/v1/projects/{project_id}

POST  /api/v1/context
GET   /api/v1/context?project_id=…
GET   /api/v1/context/{context_id}?project_id=…
PATCH /api/v1/context/{context_id}?project_id=…
POST  /api/v1/context/search

Creating a project or a context item returns 201. A taken project identifier returns 409, as does a stale expected_revision. Context for an unknown project returns 404, and so does context that exists in a different project. A malformed request returns 422.

The item endpoints take project_id as a required query parameter because the documented paths address a context item by its own identifier alone. Without it there would be nothing to scope the query by, and scoping is what makes isolation enforceable rather than merely checked.

Responses never include vectors, BSON identifiers, or internal fields. revision is returned so a client can send it back as expected_revision.

POST /api/v1/context
{
  "project_id": "payment-service",
  "type": "architecture_decision",
  "title": "Payment idempotency strategy",
  "content": "Payment requests carry a UUID4 idempotency key…",
  "importance": 0.95,
  "source": "user",
  "tags": ["payments", "idempotency"],
  "external_id": "payment-idempotency"
}

POST /api/v1/context/search
{
  "project_id": "payment-service",
  "query": "how do we prevent duplicate charges?",
  "types": ["architecture_decision"],
  "tags": ["payments"],
  "status": "active",
  "minimum_importance": 0.5,
  "limit": 10
}

Readiness

/health/ready reports both context indexes:

{
  "context_search": {
    "enabled": true,
    "vector_available": true,
    "vector_index": "project_context_vector_index",
    "vector_queryable": true,
    "vector_dimensions_match": true,
    "text_available": true,
    "text_index": "project_context_text_index",
    "text_queryable": true
  }
}

Readiness fails while the Search index is missing, building, or unreachable. With EMBEDDING_ENABLED=false the vector half stops being required and context stays lexically retrievable, exactly as skills do.

Verification

python -m pytest                                     # unit coverage, no MongoDB required
docker compose --profile test run --rm --build test  # live mongod + mongot checks

The live checks create projects and context, read them back, update them, exercise the idempotency key, and then assert that neither a context search nor hybrid retrieval can reach another project's entries — including that a request naming no project reaches none of them.

docs/research.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Research, evidence, and reviewed knowledge

The research system turns explicitly supplied sources into searchable material while retaining provenance. A claim, candidate review, and authorized promotion are separate steps. Source class and retrieval relevance never establish truth or factual confidence.

Research question -> registered sources -> immutable snapshots -> searchable chunks
                 -> notes / claims / citations -> evidence packet / research brief
                 -> pending candidate -> review -> authorized promotion

Research projects and permissions

A research project has a stable research_project_id, name, question, type, active/archived status, and zero or more related knowledge-project IDs. Create, list, get, and revision-guarded update routes live at /api/v3/research/projects. The server owns authorization metadata. Access requires every linked project within the caller's grant; stored sources and evidence also retain their original project authorization set. Research with no project links is global to authorized research readers, so do not use that scope for private project facts.

Use research:read for reads and research:write for source, note, claim, brief, and candidate creation. Candidate decisions require research:approve; promotion requires research:promote plus the target's memory:write or context:write scope. Project authorization applies at every step. Scope grants are independent; a research writer need not be a reviewer or promoter.

Register sources and ingest snapshots

POST /api/v3/research/sources records a source before acquisition. Sources have IDs, canonical locators, descriptive source classes, metadata, and preserved project grants. Duplicate canonical registrations are refused instead of replacing history. Snapshot IDs, hashes, retrieval times, and version identifiers pin each observation. Source registration alone performs no acquisition.

The registry accepts manual, url, file, markdown, pdf, git, github, documentation, and rss metadata. The configured providers below determine what can actually be ingested; registration is not a promise of a connector for all source types. RSS feeds and documentation-site crawling have no acquisition provider in this release.

POST /api/v3/research/sources/{source_id}/ingest accepts one mode:

Mode Accepted input Acquisition boundary
Manual text Explicit UTF-8 content, plain text or Markdown Supplied text only
File/PDF Bounded base64 content_base64, content type, optional filename Uploaded bytes; no server-side path
Web URL fetch_url: true for an active registered url source One bounded public HTTP(S) page
Repository fetch_repository: true for active registered git or github sources Public HTTPS repository, read-only

A file: URI is a citation locator, not authorization to read the server's filesystem. File uploads reject unsafe filenames, archives, executable signatures, unsupported types, malformed/encrypted PDFs, and oversized input. Raw bytes are capped at 700,000; normalized text at 200,000 characters; PDF extraction at 100 pages with bounded stream handling. Unsupported PDF constructs fail rather than being delegated to an external executable.

The web provider accepts HTML/XHTML, requests identity encoding, bounds redirects, size, and execution time, and does not run JavaScript or crawl links. It validates public addresses before each request and checks the connected peer after response headers where the HTTP transport exposes it. Ambient proxies are disabled.

Network limitation: preflight DNS validation and the connection do not share a pinned DNS result. A hostname can change between them, and a post-response peer check cannot prevent an already-issued request. Repository transport has the same separate-resolution boundary and no peer hook. Enforce outbound firewall/proxy rules that block private, loopback, link-local, and cloud metadata destinations when accepting untrusted sources. These application checks do not alone prove comprehensive SSRF prevention.

Repository providers disable ambient credentials, redirects, hooks, checkout, submodules, package scripts, builds, and shell execution. They fetch bounded repository objects and read eligible blobs only. They exclude binaries, symlinks, unsafe paths, common build/dependency trees, and detectable secret files/content. GitHub acquisition uses public https://github.com/<owner>/<repository> sources without a provider token. A registered source may select one validated branch, tag, or full commit. Git must be available in the ingestion environment.

Each accepted ingestion stores normalized documents and citable chunks with source/snapshot/document IDs and available headings, page numbers, lines, repository paths, symbols, and commit IDs. Hash-derived IDs make reingesting the same source bytes or repository commit idempotent. Ingestion returns snapshot/job metadata; status is available through the source's ingestion-job route. Jobs are bounded in-process operations, with no distributed queue or durable worker lease.

Search, notes, and claims

POST /api/v3/research/search supports lexical, vector, and hybrid retrieval. Profiles are research_general, research_primary_sources, research_recent, research_content, research_architecture, and research_code. The code profile searches authorized source_code chunks; other profiles can include existing knowledge through the established retrieval service.

Filter by source type/class, publisher/domain, source dates, retrieval dates, as_of snapshot cutoff, research project, and an optional linked knowledge project. Stored provenance and current project links are both authorized before results or hit metadata are exposed. Responses diversify sources where available, use opaque cursors, and respect RESEARCH_RETRIEVAL_TOKEN_BUDGET (default 8,000) and its configured hard maximum. retrieval_score means relevance only.

Notes are working artifacts with source references and working/reviewed/archived states.
