Maintain and validate

Change a skill's semantic version whenever its bytes change after import. Keep one canonical file per ID. Write a precise description and tags that help task selection; keep headings meaningful so independently retrieved sections retain context. Include specific failures and evidence, without asserting perfection. Review generated changes as proposals before activating them.

Regenerate documentation with .venv/bin/python docs/guide/build.py. This refreshes the table, embedded skill bodies and docs/guide/skill-manifest.json. It does not import anything into MongoDB or connect a client. See skills.md for the parser, version lifecycle and operator contract.

docs/skills.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Skills: canonical sources and runtime import

All runtime records and search candidates described here belong to one trusted organization. global means organization-global, with explicit action/resource policy; it never means a null-org or cross-installation corpus. Imported skills are tenant-owned copies of canonical Git. Private agent memory also retains verified client ownership and is not revealed by human management visibility.

Canonical source and directory layout

Git-tracked UTF-8 Markdown under skills/ is the canonical source. MongoDB is a validated runtime representation and must not be edited as a replacement for the files. The expanded structure is:

skills/
├── architecture/
├── content/
├── django/
├── docker/
├── engineering/
├── fastapi/
├── frontend/
├── mongodb/
├── operations/
├── platform/
├── postgresql/
├── python/
└── security/

The catalog contains 39 canonical skills across 11 metadata categories, including six Django skills, four FastAPI skills and ten content skills. Skill versions are declared individually in frontmatter; consult the catalog for the current version of each file. Directory names do not always equal category names: FastAPI uses backend, while Docker uses operations.

Use skill-catalog.md for task routing, source search and the complete generated table, or the HTML catalog for offline search and full bodies. scripts/skill_catalog.py validates and searches the Git sources without importing or connecting a database. Content guidance is also documented in content-skills.md.

Required frontmatter

Every *.md file below the configured directory must start with YAML frontmatter:

---
id: fastapi-production
name: FastAPI Production Engineering
version: 1.0.0
description: Production-grade FastAPI engineering practices.
category: backend
trust_level: trusted
tags:
  - python
  - fastapi
---

# FastAPI Production Engineering

## Purpose

...

All seven fields are required except tags, which defaults to an empty list. Unknown keys, duplicate tags, invalid identifiers, unsupported trust levels, malformed semantic versions, non-UTF-8 input, empty bodies, symlinks, and files above SKILL_MAX_FILE_BYTES are rejected. YAML is parsed with the safe loader. Import errors identify the file but never print its body.

Trust levels are trusted, user, external, and generated. Retrieved text remains data; its trust label does not allow it to override system or application instructions.

Version lifecycle and transactions

The frontmatter version is explicit. The importer never guesses or silently increments a version.

  • First import: creates the active version and its chunks.
  • Identical retry: reports unchanged and performs no writes.
  • Changed bytes with the same version: fails and requires a new semantic version.
  • New declared version: in one replica-set transaction, marks the prior active version superseded, inserts the new active document, and inserts its chunks.

Historical skill documents and chunks are never overwritten or deleted by import. A transaction failure rolls back the entire version transition, so the preceding active version remains valid. Only one canonical Markdown file may declare a given skill ID in one import run.

Section-aware chunking

The parser recognizes ATX headings outside fenced code and retains heading paths in chunk metadata. Short adjacent sections are packed together with their Markdown headings intact. Large sections aim for the environment-driven minimum, target, maximum, and overlap sizes, which default to 500, 650, 800, and 75 approximate tokens respectively. Overlap is taken only from non-code content and stays within the configured maximum.

Chunk token counts use a deterministic word/punctuation estimate. Fenced blocks using backticks or tildes are atomic and are never split or copied as overlap. An unterminated fence or a single atomic block larger than MongoDB's persisted chunk limits is rejected instead of corrupted.

Each chunk is stored separately with:

  • deterministic chunk-NNNN identity within (skill_id, version);
  • global chunk_index order;
  • section label and heading path;
  • source path and overlap count;
  • approximate token count;
  • an optional vector with its embedding model metadata.

Import operation

Start the stack, then run:

make import-skills

Equivalent direct command:

docker compose run --rm --build context-api python -m app.cli.import_skills

For a different canonical root:

python -m app.cli.import_skills --directory /path/to/skills

The CLI connects with the application MongoDB user, ensures the existing schema/index migration, and prints only aggregate counts: discovered, new, updated, unchanged, chunks created, and chunks embedded. It exits non-zero on invalid input, a version conflict, or an unusable embedding model. All files are parsed and chunked before the first database write, preventing a malformed later file from causing a partial directory import.

When embeddings are enabled the importer loads the configured local model before the first write, so a missing or mismatched model fails the run instead of storing half-embedded chunks. Every chunk of a new version is embedded together with that version. Skip embedding with:

python -m app.cli.import_skills --no-embeddings

See embeddings.md for the model configuration and the rules that keep vectors from different models apart.

Configuration:

SKILLS_DIRECTORY=skills
SKILL_MAX_FILE_BYTES=1000000
SKILL_CHUNK_MIN_TOKENS=500
SKILL_CHUNK_TARGET_TOKENS=650
SKILL_CHUNK_MAX_TOKENS=800
SKILL_CHUNK_OVERLAP_TOKENS=75

REST API

GET  /api/v1/skills
GET  /api/v1/skills/{skill_id}
POST /api/v1/skills/search

Listing returns active versions by default and supports status, category, tag, trust-level, limit, and cursor filters. The detail endpoint returns the active version unless ?version=1.0.0 is provided. It includes preserved version history and a chunk page controlled by chunk_limit and chunk_cursor.

Search accepts a bounded query plus optional category, tags, trust level, and limit. It matches escaped literal query terms case-insensitively against active skill metadata and chunk content. At most three matching chunks accompany each result. Regex input is escaped, results are bounded, and BSON identifiers/revisions are not exposed.

This endpoint deliberately uses no search index, so it keeps working when mongot is unavailable, and it returns no relevance scores. Scored retrieval over the same chunks lives at POST /api/v1/skills/search/vector and POST /api/v1/skills/search/lexical, documented in retrieval.md. Hybrid retrieval uses the same stored chunks and is described in that guide.

Runtime integration

The importer supplies versioned chunks and model-tagged vectors to lexical, vector, and hybrid retrieval. The API and MCP gateway enforce the caller's scopes before returning that knowledge. Canonical skill edits remain an operator-reviewed Git workflow; generated proposals cannot import or activate themselves.

docs/sso-identity.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

SSO and active organization context

V6 Phase 4 adds session-only OIDC, exact identity linking and explicit organization switching. It requires the verified Phase 2 isolation gate and Phase 3 local identity/MFA. It creates no corpus grants and exposes no team or data dashboard. All features remain disabled by default. Schema 39 follows the actual schema-38 head. Applying it revokes existing browser sessions once, preserves their history, and refuses older runtimes. Repeating the migration preserves new sessions. Drain API/browser workers before cutover. The migration raises the local identity control marker to 39 before adding OIDC evidence; existing schema-38 workers therefore fail their per-request identity gate, while new workers without SSO configuration refuse startup. Sessions without version-39 authentication evidence are refused by the SSO runtime. In-flight work must be drained operationally.

Installation configuration

Enable V6_SSO=true alongside the existing tenant isolation and local identity settings. Mount a private JSON registration file and set V6_OIDC_REGISTRATIONS_FILE to its container path. A deployment override must explicitly mount this file and any private CA file read-only. Never commit these files or expose them through frontend configuration. Each registration belongs to exactly one organization. Example structure (replace the documentation IP, hostnames and secret through your secret manager before use):

[
  {
    "registration_id": "company-keycloak",
    "org_id": "company",
    "issuer": "https://login.example.com/realms/company",
    "client_id": "agent-context-company",
    "client_secret": "REPLACE_WITH_A_RANDOM_SECRET_FROM_YOUR_SECRET_MANAGER",
    "redirect_uri": "https://context.example.com/api/v6/auth/oidc/callback",
    "post_logout_redirect_uri": "https://context.example.com/api/v6/auth/oidc/logged-out",
    "authorization_endpoint": "https://login.example.com/realms/company/protocol/openid-connect/auth",
    "token_endpoint": "https://login.example.com/realms/company/protocol/openid-connect/token",
    "jwks_uri": "https://login.example.com/realms/company/protocol/openid-connect/certs",
    "end_session_endpoint": "https://login.example.com/realms/company/protocol/openid-connect/logout",
    "connect_ip": "203.0.113.10",
    "algorithms": ["RS256"],
    "mfa_acr": [],
    "mfa_amr": [],
    "require_mfa": false,
    "assurance_version": 1,
    "max_session_seconds": 3600
  }
]

The operator approves exact endpoints and a connection IP. Outbound HTTP pins that IP while retaining the original HTTPS hostname for TLS SNI/certificate and Host validation. DNS is never consulted. Provider endpoints must share the issuer authority. Only discovery, JWKS and token URLs may be fetched; responses are bounded to 128 KiB, four concurrent flows, five-second HTTP timeouts and a twelve-second operation deadline. Redirects, environment proxies, userinfo, dynamic registration and browser-supplied URLs are disabled. IP/trust-root, client secret or assurance changes require a reviewed registration update, worker restart and explicit org reapproval; existing evidence fails closed. ca_file, if supplied, adds an explicit private trust root through a mounted PEM file; its content hash is part of the approved registration version. TLS verification is never disabled, including disposable tests.

Approve a mounted registration and policy through the installation host CLI:

contextctl --org-id company identity configure-sso \
  --registration-id company-keycloak --policy sso_preferred \
  --approval-reference CHANGE-123

Configuration increments the org policy version, invalidating previous policy contexts. local_only permits local login and rejects provider login. sso_preferred permits either explicit login method. sso_required accepts only that org's approved issuer, client registration and configured assurance rules. An outage never changes these policies or automatically selects local login.

Initial enrollment remains operator-invited local enrollment. While the org is sso_preferred, establish local MFA and link the exact external identity before switching the org to sso_required. There is no public signup, automatic membership creation or email-based migration. An already linked identity cannot be moved to another global user by this flow.

Reference provider configuration

Reference provider: Keycloak 26.8.1, image pinned in tests/infrastructure/v6-oidc.compose.yml. Create a confidential OpenID Connect client with Standard Flow enabled, S256 PKCE required, exact callback URI and exact post-logout URI above. Disable Direct Access Grants and implicit flow. Retain the built-in basic client scope (including subject and authentication time) and acr; removing required claims causes token validation to fail closed. Enable HTTPS with a valid certificate; require HTTPS for the realm. No wildcard redirects, origins or registration endpoints are used.

Empty MFA rules convey no MFA assurance, even if an IdP sends a claim named mfa, an acr value of 1, or an administrator group. To trust provider MFA, first review and enforce the provider authentication flow, then allow exact mfa_acr values and/or required mfa_amr methods. All configured conditions must match. require_mfa=true rejects every provider login/link without that proof. Do not label a password-only flow as MFA. Increment assurance_version when rules change. The disposable second realm uses required password and OTP executions with Keycloak's native AMR mapper, rather than hardcoding an MFA claim.

Official sources checked for this implementation:

  • Authlib HTTP clients and Code + PKCE
  • OpenID Connect Core token validation
  • Keycloak endpoints and logout
  • Keycloak TLS configuration
  • Keycloak authentication execution references and AMR

Authlib 1.9.1 and joserfc 1.7.5 are pinned BSD-3-Clause dependencies, verified against Authlib metadata and joserfc metadata; cryptography remains the existing maintained backend. Downloaded wheel hashes are checked against official PyPI metadata. The Authlib HTTPX compatibility adapter supports our pinned HTTPX 0.28.1; it emits an upstream deprecation warning recommending HTTPX2. A future HTTP client migration requires its own compatibility review. Keycloak is Apache-2.0 and runs only as disposable test infrastructure here.

Browser contracts

All routes below use the existing Secure/HttpOnly/host-only session cookies. Every POST requires the exact Origin and matching CSRF token. Authorization headers are rejected. V1–V5 and MCP continue to reject browser cookies.

Method and /api/v6 path Admission and result
POST /auth/oidc/start Preauth cookie + CSRF, {org_id}; returns an approved authorization URL.
GET /auth/oidc/callback Exact registered URI, unique state/code parameters, same browser cookie, persisted single-use transaction, nonce and S256 verifier.
POST /auth/identities/link Current session + recent MFA, {org_id} own active membership; authenticates the target identity freshly and invalidates all old user sessions. Requires fresh login afterward.
POST /auth/oidc/reauthenticate Current session, {org_id, purpose: "switch" or "reauth"}; explicit target-provider login, same exact user identity required.
GET /me/organizations Only the caller's active, verified memberships with minimal directory fields.
POST /me/active-organization Own active target membership and target auth policy; rotates session/CSRF and returns a fresh policy context. No selector conveys authority.
GET /organizations/{org_id}/session-context Path must match active org; X-Session-Context must match the current context.
POST /auth/oidc/logout Revokes the application session before returning the approved provider logout URL.
GET /auth/oidc/logged-out Single-use logout state acknowledgement; conveys no authentication.

OIDC login callbacks are the narrow mutation exception to Origin/CSRF headers; their persisted, five-minute, single-use browser/purpose/org-bound state is the CSRF defense. State hashes and encrypted PKCE verifiers stay in private MongoDB. No token or verifier is stored in browser local/session storage or readable session cookies. Code, ID/access/refresh tokens are not persisted or returned. The access token exists only during ID token validation. Exact issuer/subject is the identity key. Equal email, verified email, roles and groups are ignored. Provider errors and validation diagnostics are generic and secret-free.

Sessions record verified identity ID, issuer, registration/version, client ID, authentication time, assurance version and verified acr/amr. Unconfigured provider assurance is reported as authenticated, never represented as a local password or fake machine identity. Local MFA can step up an OIDC session without turning its provider proof into a local login. Privileged actions still require MFA within ten minutes. /me distinguishes missing MFA enrollment from an enrolled user needing recent step-up, so an ordinary OIDC login does not suggest enrolling an existing factor again.

Organization switching checks both memberships and current policy afresh, then revokes the old session and changes the CSRF token and policy context ID. The new session does not extend the original absolute expiry. Another org's provider registration never satisfies an SSO-required target, even for the same user. Use explicit target reauthentication when a direct switch is refused. Org paths must equal the active org. A supplied stale X-Session-Context is rejected on self routes too. Future UI must attach this context, cancel old queries and clear org caches/drafts/download intents before presenting the new organization. There is no browser management UI in this phase.

Responses are no-store with Referrer-Policy: no-referrer. Application logging redacts OAuth credentials, and the browser boundary strips callback query strings before Uvicorn access logging. Configure external ingress/access logs to omit query strings on /api/v6/auth/oidc/* as well. Do not enable third-party HTTP wire/debug logging or capture callback URLs in analytics.

Revocation and emergency operation

Membership suspension, user disable/epoch changes, policy/registration changes, identity removal, session logout and expiry are checked locally on every request. SSO sessions expire at the earliest of the ID token expiry, configured provider session maximum, existing session absolute expiry and idle expiry. There is no refresh-token extension.

This phase does not implement SCIM, backchannel logout or continuous token introspection. Disabling an account or logging out at the IdP therefore does not instantly terminate an already issued application session. The bounded expiry above and explicit application suspension/revocation apply. Fresh provider login uses prompt=login and max_age=0, and disabled accounts cannot authenticate. RP-initiated logout revokes the local app session even if the provider is down; the browser must complete Keycloak's confirmation page to end its provider SSO session. Closing that page does not prove provider logout completed.

An installation operator may approve a specific active user/member for at most 60 minutes of local MFA access to a required org:

contextctl --org-id company identity break-glass --user-id USER_ID \
  --minutes 15 --approval-reference INCIDENT-456

The exception is scoped to exact org/user, membership revision, policy version and expiry, is audited, requires an existing active local MFA factor, and grants no corpus permissions. There is no automatic exception or MFA removal. Operator recovery and subsequent grant approval remain separate from this login exception.

Storage and verification

organization_oidc and organization_break_glass are tenant-owned operator-only authority records. oidc_transactions is private global identity security state, always accessed through purpose/browser/session/org checks. _sso_identity_control is installation metadata. Existing user_identities retains its unique exact provider/subject constraint; OIDC providers use the exact issuer string while local identities retain local. Browser evidence never enters org directory DTOs. These collections are excluded from domain repository access and included only in installation-operator whole-database backups. A reserved collection name is recognized at activation only with both its schema marker and migration ledger. Private registration files and keyrings are mounted installation storage.

Run the focused commands from the Phase 4 request, or the complete disposable gate with scripts/test-v6-sso.sh. The latter runs all unit tests, real Phase 2 isolation, Phase 3 local identity, then real HTTPS Keycloak tests with separate MongoDB stacks between selectors. V6_SSO_DEVELOPMENT_ONLY=1 is a development selector and cannot establish prerequisite gates. Missing provider configuration produces an integration skip and means the Phase 4 evidence gate is incomplete. No invitations are sent to real recipients; all mail uses the private test sink.

Phase 4 reference verification passed 2,809 unit tests, 12 real tenant-isolation tests, 9 real local-identity tests and all 9 real Keycloak tests, with zero skips. Ruff, strict mypy and the public source audit also passed. These are correctness results on disposable infrastructure, not production latency or capacity measurements.

docs/tenant-adoption.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Tenant foundation and legacy adoption (V6 Phase 1)

This guide describes the guarded schema-36 adoption stage of the implemented V6 runtime. It seals all organizations until the subsequent explicit isolation cutover. The current full schema head is 42; follow staged migration/recovery rather than enabling all later flags at once. The console, identity and policy contracts are described in dashboard and organization management. There is no anonymous owner claim, public org registration or tenant restore.

Adoption was allocated at the actual pre-V6 migration head 35, so its version is 36. Enable foundation only for this stage. Older configurations refuse an installation containing 36, but a pre-V6 binary cannot know that guard: stop all old writers and fence their database credentials. Worker flags are attestations, not process discovery. Quarantine remains operator-only at application interfaces, not physically isolated from trusted installation database operators.

Storage and identity contracts

app/db/tenant_inventory.py maps every one of the 37 served collections to its model and structural references. All are tenant-owned, including keys, logs, client templates, conversations, retry reservations and ingestion jobs. organizations, _schema_migrations, _mongot_health_probe, _tenant_control, _tenant_preservation and _tenant_quarantine are installation metadata. Unknown collections or shapes receive no guessed owner. A nonempty pre-V6 collection using a reserved V6 metadata name is refused before schema changes. Preserve its backup and have an operator classify/rename that collection before retrying; its name or email fields never establish ownership. This phase creates no private global human identity collection.

Adoption selects exactly one organization explicitly. It adds org_id, identity_version=1 and legacy_adoption_id; it retains existing ObjectIds, authored fields, actor labels, timestamps and revisions. Each adopted record has an operator-only preservation manifest containing the original BSON and checksum. The record and manifest commit in one replica-set transaction, with a fenced, renewable maintenance lease and a compare-and-set check of the complete source. New tenant records use version 2. Models freeze the three ownership/identity fields; repository updates exclude them and constrain the stored owner/scheme. New request DTOs cannot select the legacy scheme; normal repository inserts reject version 1 even if a caller constructs a storage model.

Version 1 preserves the original SHA-256 of NUL-separated namespace/key parts. Version 2 takes the first 12 SHA-256 bytes of UTF-8 JSON ["acp-id",2,namespace,org_id,...parts], with ensure_ascii=False and separators (',', ':'). Memory dimensions are scope, project-or-empty, client-or-empty and external ID. Content integrity hashes remain hashes of content. Derived logical snapshot/document/job/review IDs are protected by the tenant compound natural constraints and version 2 document identity. Random document IDs remain random. Natural-key lookups use organization plus natural key, allowing adopted IDs to remain unchanged on update. No request selects a legacy hash fallback.

Unique compound indexes prefix org_id, including unique natural keys and partial active skill constraints. New compound indexes are built before historical indexes are dropped. TTL cleanup indexes remain single-field, and API key IDs remain globally unique for credential resolution. Strict collection validators require non-null ownership and pin version 1 to the chosen adoption org and adoption ID. MongoDB shape validation cannot compare an old and new document to enforce immutability; frozen models and repository write filters supply that guarantee for application writes. A trusted DB operator can bypass validation.

Same-org closure includes project/client/profile/skill references, structured content/research evidence, source/snapshot/document/chunk chains, candidate and promotion references, supersession links, key restrictions and jobs. Actor labels, retired key/owner labels, diagnostic retrieval selections and refused audit or activity targets remain historical descriptions, not required live foreign keys. External conversation session labels are not agent-session IDs. Arbitrary payload metadata is inert. Ambiguous, dangling and foreign-owner structural links fail closure. Legacy empty key projects/profiles and client project lists are recorded as explicit all_in_org modes in the preservation manifest; grant conversion and enforcement follow the isolation and managed-policy cutovers.

Operator rehearsal

Use a disposable copy of a verified full-database backup first. Preserve the archive and its checksum/count manifest. The existing backup facility remains installation-wide; --org-id is refused on backup/restore commands. There is no tenant restore. Credentials and archive contents must remain operator-only.

  1. Stop all old API/MCP processes, imports and workers. Confirm each replacement maintenance binary understands schema 36. Do not run mixed writers.
  2. Take and verify a whole-database backup with its collection counts. Record the selected organization and a stable adoption ID outside served data.
  3. Configure database operator credentials and run the following commands:
contextctl --org-id existing-org organizations provision --name 'Existing organization' --slug existing-org
contextctl --json --org-id existing-org organizations adopt --adoption-id adoption-20261014 --dry-run
contextctl --json --org-id existing-org organizations adopt --adoption-id adoption-20261014 \
  --backup-archive /operator/pre-v6.archive --backup-manifest /operator/pre-v6.manifest.json \
  --writers-stopped --worker-schema-version 36

A dry run changes neither documents nor the migration ledger. Incompatible dry runs and blocked applies return exit code 1 with the structured report on stdout. The apply command validates the backup database, archive bytes/checksum and source coverage/counts. Resume uses the same org, adoption ID and original verified backup. After an interruption, rerun exactly the apply command. An unexpired competing lease refuses a second maintainer. Transaction rollback removes a partially written preservation manifest too. A final audit checks actual MongoDB candidate schemas (without model-default invention), reference closure, preserved-record presence and preservation counts against the original backup before installing strict tenant contracts. Repeating a prepared adoption rechecks closure without rewriting records.

Unknown or incompatible records move transactionally to _tenant_quarantine, with their full original BSON, checksum, reason and unresolved status. Quarantine is outside domain repositories and routes; reports contain identifiers and issue codes, not authored content or credentials. Unresolved quarantine blocks preparation even when served collections appear clean. Missing source records, including records lost during maintenance, also fail preservation counts. Do not mark a quarantine item resolved merely because it was moved. Repair requires operator review against the backup, an explicit classification, complete reference repair and a new rehearsal. This release offers no automatic repair or destructive quarantine-clear command.

Use explicit --org-id on provisioning, imports, keys, agent administration and index maintenance after foundation provisioning. Tenant writes require completed adoption and a registered sealed org. These are trusted operator operations, not browser permissions. A whole-installation rollback requires an isolated verified restore, old-writer shutdown and review before exposing traffic; migration 36 has no automatic downgrade.

Evidence commands

The new focused unit targets retain the requested names:

python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_v6_tenant_models.py tests/unit/test_v6_tenant_migration.py
python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_indexes.py tests/unit/test_models.py tests/unit/test_agent_identity_migration.py tests/unit/test_client_profile_migration.py tests/unit/test_backup_catalog.py

The real selector requires an explicitly named disposable loopback replica set and its Docker container (prefix acp-v6-phase1-test-). It creates only uniquely named acp_v6_* databases and drops them in fixture cleanup. It uses a real mongodump archive. Without the environment, it skips and supplies no integration evidence:

V6_TEST_MONGODB_URI='mongodb://127.0.0.1:PORT/?replicaSet=SET&directConnection=true' \
V6_TEST_MONGODB_CONTAINER=acp-v6-phase1-test-DATE \
python -m pytest -q tests/integration/test_v6_tenant_adoption.py

The fixture covers every collection with real pre-V6 validators, preserved actors and revisions, linked content/research evidence, keys and jobs. Acceptance checks strict validators and tenant uniqueness on MongoDB, adopted-object updates, transaction rollback, interrupted/repeated adoption, unresolved quarantine, backup/writer refusal and the API/MCP traffic seal. This stage-specific selector alone does not establish runtime isolation, search-policy, dashboard or human-auth acceptance; those require their real gates.

docs/tenant-isolation.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Tenant isolation and stage-37 activation

This guide describes the schema-37 isolation stage after preserved schema-36 adoption. The current runtime also implements human identity, management and the console; those require the subsequent staged cutovers. Do not substitute current head 42 into a command that deliberately activates stage 37. There is no public registration, anonymous owner claim or tenant restore.

Every domain collection is tenant-owned. The authoritative catalog is app/db/tenant_schema.py:TENANT_COLLECTIONS; the reference/identity catalog is app/db/tenant_inventory.py. All 37 collections pass through TenantCollection, including auxiliary skill chunks and content versions. Installation exceptions are the schema ledger, mongot health probe, organization registry, tenant control, preservation manifests, and quarantine. Backups, restored-check collections, canonical Git files, embedding model files, and raw shared process metrics belong to the installation operator. Runtime skill imports, memory (including global), embeddings attached to domain records, jobs, and replay results belong to one organization.

Path Trusted context and policy gate
Ordinary V1–V5 APIs, including agent:manage Verified bearer → globally unique public key lookup → enabled organization → principal → action/resource policy. Organization selectors never establish authority.
Services and repositories Public async service guard; immutable organization on all domain driver operations; same-org resource/reference validation on writes; independent ownership checks on reads and joins. Export/review methods also check their input ownership.
Counts, distinct, pagination, joins Tenant/resource query predicate before selection; cursors are signed and bind organization, action, subject/grants, collection, and filters. Old unsigned cursors must be restarted.
Lexical/vector retrieval All eleven production definitions index organization and candidate IDs. Filters are inside $search.compound.filter / $vectorSearch.filter, before limits. Complex research predicates and live content provenance compile to bounded authorized candidate IDs. Results are checked again.
Content provenance and history Same-org reference closure; live project/private-client authority inherited through source links before candidate selection, counts, exports, or history reads. Cached project metadata is descriptive, not authority.
stdio and HTTP MCP Fresh authenticated identity preflight per call; one organization per gateway runtime; HTTP sessions bind both organization and key. Existing tool names and API paths remain.
Ingestion Existing synchronous provider/job path. Server-issued initiating authority is checked before work, persistence steps, replay, and status/result access. Revoked/expired keys, disabled clients, inaccessible sources, and foreign organizations are refused. There is no new queue. Legacy jobs with no established initiator cannot be downloaded/replayed through bearer traffic.
Quotas and replay cache Organization + client (or verified legacy key for quota purposes); replay additionally binds effective initiating grants. A changed grant refuses a cached response.
Temporary checkouts and downloads Private temporary directories include the validated organization; provider cleanup remains scoped to that directory. Export reads the authorized tenant item before formatting. No tenant database download/restore route exists.
Provisioning/import/admin CLI Explicit contextctl --org-id …; direct database credentials are the installation operator boundary. Tenant bearer callers cannot activate organizations or operate whole-database backups.
/metrics Separate installation-operator token file, compared in constant time. Tenant system:read grants no access to raw shared metrics.

Legacy identities remain only on adopted records. Lookups use tenant natural keys so updates retain adopted ObjectIds, revisions, actors, and identity version. New identities include the organization. Migrated empty project/profile lists become explicit all_in_org using the adoption manifest; none is distinct. An administrative action narrowed to resources cannot mint broader all_in_org authority. No key grants all organizations.

Content/reference candidate compilation is bounded at 10,000 records/IDs and refuses larger envelopes. This is a safety bound, not a performance result. Large installations must measure representative workloads before raising it. MongoDB documents the candidate-filter semantics in compound filter and Vector Search filtering. This phase adds no third-party dependency.

Run the repeatable disposable gate with Docker and the existing development virtual environment:

scripts/test-v6-isolation.sh

The runner uses the repository's pinned MongoDB/mongot images, generated temporary credentials, tmpfs database storage, an isolated network, and a loopback-only random port. It never reads the deployment .env. It runs the full Python unit suite, then the real three-module selector, including actual stdio and Streamable HTTP MCP. Both organizations reuse logical identifiers and carry distinct private sentinel content. Reports include a fingerprint of the public runtime/test sources; credentials and .private planning are excluded. Only the runner's own containers/network are removed. Set V6_REPORT_DIR to retain reports at a chosen location.

A deployment remains sealed until an explicit operator cutover. Complete Phase 1 adoption first. Stop all existing writers and MCP/API workers, fence/rotate their database credentials, and deploy only schema-37 binaries. The worker version declaration is an operator attestation; it does not discover running processes. Older binaries fail the migration/version gate, and the Phase 1 middleware continues to seal its domain routes. Database credentials themselves remain trusted installation authority.

contextctl --org-id ADOPTED_ORG organizations prepare-isolation \
  --writers-stopped --worker-schema-version 37

# Enable the scoped runtime for subsequent startup/operator operations:
# V6_TENANT_FOUNDATION=true
# V6_TENANT_ISOLATION=true
# API_AUTH_ENABLED=true

contextctl --org-id ADOPTED_ORG organizations activate-isolation \
  --writers-stopped --worker-schema-version 37 \
  --evidence /path/to/unit.xml --evidence /path/to/real.xml

Activation refuses failed/skipped/stale-source evidence, mixed worker declarations, unresolved quarantine, unclassified collections/owners, invalid records, and unresolved/foreign references. It activates only the explicitly named organization; additional organizations stay sealed until separately activated. Reports are local operator evidence and must come from the actual disposable run, not fabricated XML. There is no HTTP activation endpoint.

For metrics, mount a separate operator credential file with at least 32 random characters, set OPERATOR_METRICS_TOKEN_FILE to its container path, and have the installation scraper present it as a bearer token. An unset path disables access. Keep this file outside the repository and separate from all tenant API keys.

Third-party software and material

The repository's MIT License applies to its original source, documentation, skills, and examples. It does not relicense dependencies, container images, model weights, retrieved material, or vendor trademarks.

Database, search, and model artifacts

Component License boundary Upstream source
MongoDB Community Server SSPL-1.0; separate from this application's MIT license MongoDB licensing, SSPL text
MongoDB Community Search / mongot SSPL-1.0; retains its own third-party notices Official mongot repository, license
Default sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights Model card identifies Apache-2.0; downloaded into the local model cache Publisher model card

MongoDB's SSPL is source-available and has not been approved by the Open Source Initiative. Publishing this application under MIT does not make its MongoDB and search dependencies MIT-licensed or OSI-approved. See MongoDB's SSPL FAQ for its distinction between an application using MongoDB and offering MongoDB's functionality as a service.

Changing the configured embedding model changes the model license boundary. Check the exact publisher, revision, license, and required attribution before redistributing model weights. The source release does not include the downloaded model cache or container images.

Python packages and container images

Direct runtime dependencies are declared in pyproject.toml. Runtime and development transitive dependencies are pinned in requirements.lock and requirements-dev.lock. Their installed distributions retain their own license and notice files; installing them does not place them under this project's MIT License.

The stack also uses the pinned upstream Python and MongoDB container images and their operating-system packages. The optional introduction website uses the upstream Nginx unprivileged Alpine image specified in its Compose file. Publishing a combined binary or container image requires retaining the license/notice material for the exact included packages. The application image copies mongodump and mongorestore from the MongoDB image; their upstream license and third-party notices are included in the release notice directory and preserved under /usr/share/doc/mongodb-database-tools/ in the runtime image. This document is a source-release inventory, not a replacement for the complete notices required by a redistributed image.

Before distributing binaries, record the installed dependency versions and preserve the license files shipped with their wheels/packages. Consult the official Database Tools source and license. Do not substitute a list of package names for their required notices.

Skills, examples, and ingested sources

Skills contain original guidance with links to supporting documentation. Those links do not include or transfer the linked publishers' license rights. The payment example describes fictional systems and incidents for demonstration. It is not a record of an organization or financial production guidance.

Documents, code, web pages, and citations you ingest keep their existing ownership and license. Retain source attribution and respect the rights that apply to storage, excerpts, exports, and publication. Access to a source and approval inside the platform do not grant redistribution rights.

Product and vendor names identify compatibility or dependencies; their trademark rights remain with their respective owners.

Console ingress and optional identity provider

The console uses the committed dashboard/package-lock.json, dependency inventory, MIT license and complete frontend notices. The static image retains the notices and supplemental license files. Node is a pinned build stage, not a production JavaScript server. nginx is BSD-licensed; its official image retains its upstream component notices.

The pinned optional Keycloak image is Apache-2.0, with its own bundled JVM and third-party notices; PostgreSQL uses the PostgreSQL license. These images do not become part of this repository's MIT code license. When redistributing container binaries, retain their full upstream notices and meet their corresponding-source obligations, including Git (GPL-2.0) and its Debian runtime libraries. The API image copies Debian package copyright files and common licenses with Git/GSSAPI/CA runtime files from a pinned matching Debian image; build tools are excluded from the final image. Use the exact package versions in that image to obtain corresponding Debian source, rather than assuming a moving package mirror matches a binary.

docs/verification.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Verification and known limits

The implementation and its acceptance evidence are separate. Release readiness is not approved. Full release reconciliation remains open. An earlier complete attempt had blocking failures; later focused evidence resolves individual issues without approving the current public source as a release. Do not deploy a management console on the strength of component tests or documentation builds.

Required evidence

Gate Required proof Current status
Tenant adoption/isolation Real MongoDB/mongot; preserved pre-V6 IDs/references, repeated logical IDs in two orgs, all REST/MCP/jobs/search/export boundaries Focused evidence exists; final complete-source reconciliation remains required
Identity and authority Real local/MFA/session flows and supported Keycloak; provider substitution, account linking, coupled grants, independent review, concurrent revoke/issue and owner protection Full final-source acceptance remains open
Distribution and recovery Real same-origin TLS images, local and OIDC setup, materialized all-collection backup and isolated recovery including encryption keys Focused rehearsals do not substitute for the final release gate
Browser and accessibility All committed journeys plus keyboard/focus/true 200% zoom, light/dark, 360/768/1440px, conflict/empty/error/coverage states Manual review exists with limitations; the final complete browser run remains required
Performance Declared hardware/corpus/sample counts and successful response latency, including skew and concurrent authorization changes Focused measurements include passing and failing results; final complete-source reconciliation remains required
Documentation/artifacts Focused tests, rebuilt guide/site, reproducible archives, extracted source/license/secret audit Must be recorded against the final reviewed source

Observed blockers and measurement limits

A real persisted report test reproduced an authorization-expiry race at the final policy fence. The fix is applied: current grants are evaluated synchronously after the last database await. Four focused real MongoDB cases pass, covering export/activity expiry during rendering and the final CAS. Complete final-source regression reconciliation remains required.

An earlier complete attempt ran 3,333 unit tests and eleven isolation rehearsal tests successfully, with no skips. All 68 integration modules completed, with three failed tests and two errors. The browser suite passed 49 of 50 journeys; its failed journey is the directory latency measurement. A local-only hosting case failed during API startup, and an organization-switch case had a disposable database teardown replication timeout after its assertions passed. Both errors were retained as failed outcomes, including the teardown error after assertions.

Later genuine reports pass the exact affected hosting and org-switch nodes, including clean teardown. Their runtime and test fingerprints match the committed baseline before the focused runner was added; the relevant org-switch sources are unchanged. A fresh focused check also passes the original local-only TLS-routing/startup case and its nearby local MFA/session/bearer regression after the focused hosted-fixture cleanup changes. Its API image verifies the current runtime fingerprint. These are scoped resolutions, not a new full release run.

A subsequent run passed 3,347 unit tests and all eleven real isolation rehearsal tests, then exposed a recovery-fixture readiness gap: restored records passed their count checks, but the lexical probe reached a newly created search index still in INITIAL_SYNC. That attempt was stopped and retained as incomplete. The fixture now explicitly waits for both real search indexes to report READY and queryable before recovery work. All six focused backup/recovery cases pass with the wait; their original restore, count, lexical and vector assertions remain required. A fresh complete-source run must still pass all modules.

The million-event overview workload failed at 1,111 ms warm p95 for the 90/10 tenant distribution, exceeding its 1,000 ms limit. The 50/50 distribution passed at 588 ms. All twenty responses in each distribution succeeded; cold fills took 3.8 seconds and 2.4 seconds. These are one authenticated subject's twenty concurrent identical requests after a cold fill, not twenty distinct people or a continuous-write capacity claim. The tenant/time covering index and bounded, source-invalidated aggregate cache preserve separate current-authority checks; real late-insert/update/delete, foreign-insert and revocation checks pass. Refusals are never successful latency samples.

Measurements used a shared four-physical-core/eight-logical-CPU laptop with about 16 GiB RAM, rather than a dedicated reference host. Real hybrid retrieval passed a focused 100,000-matching-chunk-ID-per-org workload using the local 384-dimensional model, with repeated synthetic text prototypes. That establishes neither relevance quality nor the entire mixed reference corpus. A new full background fixture includes context, all memory scopes, drafts/candidates, people, teams, clients and projects. The real mixed-corpus run passes at 307 ms warm p95, including all six skill/context/shared-memory lexical/vector paths. It uses twenty serial samples paced within the session POST limit and verifies reviewed all_in_org skill access above the ID-preselection ceiling. Repeated synthetic prototypes establish throughput and isolation, not relevance quality.

Policy p95 in the complete attempt passed at 26.1 ms for repeated grants and 10.1 ms for distinct-resource grants across one hundred assignments. Sponsor offboarding with five hundred clients passed; dedicated transport tests cover active REST/stdio/HTTP MCP revocation. The clean ingestion-contention workload failed its absolute directory budget: 1,148 ms baseline and 725 ms loaded p95, against a 500 ms limit, despite passing the relative contention limit. Both 8 KiB console jobs completed and persisted six 384-dimensional chunks. The browser's first twenty concurrent HTTPS directory requests also failed at 1,109 ms p95, with all responses successful. Its query plan examined 21 documents for the requested twenty rows and cursor probe. Earlier passing profiled measurements do not replace these clean failures. No capacity or throughput certification is claimed.

Follow-up focused checks pass after reducing fresh policy/session query round trips and aligning integration fixtures with the shipped console's UTC decoding and bounded 50/50 connection pool. First-wave HTTPS directory p95 was 389 ms; million-event overview warm p95 was 604 ms for 90/10 and 558 ms for 50/50. The two-job ingestion workload measured 173 ms baseline and 194 ms loaded directory p95, a 12.1% increase within the 25% limit. Both 8 KiB jobs completed, persisting six real 384-dimensional chunks; all twenty reader starts overlapped ingestion. Connections initialize as configured; current authority is still read from MongoDB on every request, without a cross-request authority cache. Earlier failures and timing variability remain in the review record; focused and instrumented diagnostic runs do not constitute complete release approval.

The focused browser runner now supports the existing production-image fixture with unique owned containers/networks and verified cleanup. A fresh directory attempt against its in-pytest API fixture returned twenty HTTP 200 responses but failed at 859 ms p95 against the unchanged 500 ms limit. That is a different measurement surface from the original production-image journey and is retained as a failure. An earlier attempt failed certificate trust before collecting any latency samples. The focused browser now pins only its freshly generated fixture certificate key in its temporary Chromium profile; Node verifies the fixture CA. No system CA is installed. The original journey and its assertions are unchanged. On the original production API/console image surface, the final focused attempt passed: twenty first-wave HTTP 200 responses, 317 ms p95, 10,000 added fictional members without added assignments, and 21 examined documents for the cursor probe. It used the shared four-core/eight-logical-CPU, approximately 16 GiB host. The in-pytest and production-image measurements are reported separately; they are not pooled or selected as interchangeable repeats. This single passing wave does not establish continuous-load capacity or close full release reconciliation.

Automated frontend checks and an agent-operated real-browser manual review supplement each other. The review covers keyboard/focus, dialog return, true browser zoom, themes, responsive layouts and representative data states. It is not a physical assistive-technology review or a WCAG 2.2 AA conformance claim. Heavy workspace modules are route-split with session-preserving loading/error states. Build gzip budgets and lab Event Timing do not establish field Web Vitals or assistive-technology conformance.

Reproduce and reconcile

Use a disposable environment only. The full runner requires the pinned Node version, a real Chromium executable, the reviewed local embedding model cache, Docker and supported image/tool availability. It refuses inherited development selectors, skipped/missing tests and source changes during the run. Reports and screenshots belong in ignored operator storage, never the public guide registry.

For an individual named blocker, inspect and run the explicit p02-hosting or p02-browser-directory profile described in the focused runner guide. Each selects only its named cases and required services. Keep failed attempts, teardown outcomes and all successful response samples; a later pass does not erase an earlier failure or approve the full release gate below.

python -m pytest tests/unit -q
python -m pytest tests/integration -q
npm --prefix dashboard run lint
npm --prefix dashboard run typecheck
npm --prefix dashboard run test:unit
npm --prefix dashboard run build
npm --prefix dashboard run test:e2e
bash scripts/test-v6-acceptance.sh

The integration and browser commands need the disposable fixture environment; see Contributing and deployment. The runner maps actual test functions in tests/v6_acceptance_matrix.json and retains real JUnit results. A command that exits successfully after skipping required infrastructure is an incomplete gate. MongoDB mocks, prefiltered fake data, first-page lengths and screenshot text cannot establish enforcement or totals.

Documentation-only checks are narrower:

python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_public_release.py tests/unit/test_content_skill_catalog.py tests/unit/test_backup_deployment.py
python scripts/prepare_open_source_release.py --check
python website/build.py
python -m pytest tests/documentation -q

Retain the actual commands, source fingerprints, image IDs, counts, failure/skip results, hardware/corpus, archive hashes and residual limits in the private review record. Approval requires every blocking failure resolved against the final source; a clean archive alone is not approval. No runner publishes, deploys or pushes a release.

docs/website.mdPublic documentation

Public documentation snapshot. Use the generated tool/API reference for contracts in this checkout and live capability discovery for your running deployment.

Host the public introduction and guide

The static website introduces Agent Context Platform and links to the complete self-contained HTML usage guide. It runs independently of the Context API. No platform credential, database connection or model is needed to serve it.

Build the public files

From the repository root, use the project's Python 3.12 environment with its pinned application dependencies installed. Add the documentation-only renderer:

.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r docs/guide/requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python website/build.py

The script rebuilds docs/usage-guide.html from the current contracts and the explicit public documentation inventory in docs/guide/public-sources.json. It writes the introduction, assets, guide, MIT license and reviewed linked examples/source files to dist/site/. It checks local file links and HTML anchors and writes a hash inventory at dist/site/site-manifest.json. The site also bundles downloads/agent-context-platform-source.tar.gz and downloads/SHA256SUMS, produced by the same audited deterministic source exporter. This archive includes frontend source, package/lockfile, Node pin and dependency notices/licenses, not generated bundles, node_modules, browser traces, Git history, secret files or private plans. The site manifest covers its archive/checksum bytes. The download is a review artifact, not an approved release or automatic publication; see verification. The output directory is ignored by Git and can be rebuilt. Exported files use mode 0644 and directories use 0755, independent of your shell's umask, so the unprivileged Nginx process can read the static content.

For a release-specific check, pass a private name or phrase locally with --forbid-text PRIVATE_NAME; repeat the option for additional values. The checker also rejects absolute home-directory paths and excluded source references. Keep audit values local rather than storing them in the repository.

Guide compilation constructs API schemas without starting the application or its lifespan. It does not load a model, contact a database, read secret files or use the network. The site export rejects hidden files, symlinks and files outside its explicit public file rules. The guide embeds only documents in its public-source inventory.

To reuse a guide you have just rebuilt, use .venv/bin/python website/build.py --skip-guide.

Preview locally

You can open website/index.html directly from the checkout. Its guide and license links point to the files in the repository. The build adjusts those links for the exported dist/site/ directory, which is the directory to serve.

.venv/bin/python -m http.server 8765 \
  --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory dist/site

Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/ and http://127.0.0.1:8765/docs/usage-guide.html. Stop the development server with Ctrl+C.

Serve on your public IP

Copy the repository to your host, build the site there, then run the separate website Compose file from the repository root:

docker compose --env-file /dev/null -f deploy/website/compose.yml config --quiet
docker compose --env-file /dev/null -f deploy/website/compose.yml up -d --wait

This publishes host port 80 on all host interfaces. Allow inbound TCP 80 in your host/provider firewall. If the host is behind a router, forward TCP 80 to it. Visit http://YOUR_PUBLIC_IP/, replacing the placeholder with your actual reachable address. This repository does not contain a preselected public IP or GitHub repository URL.

The website container mounts only dist/site/ as its document root and its public Nginx configuration. It has no access to secrets/, .env, .git, database volumes, the application network or the checkout as a whole. Missing build output fails the mount instead of silently creating an empty directory. Directory listing is disabled, unknown paths return 404, and the server never proxies /mcp or /api to a live backend. The --env-file /dev/null option keeps the documentation server independent of the platform's private .env.

If port 80 is occupied, choose a different port:

WEBSITE_PORT=8088 docker compose --env-file /dev/null \
  -f deploy/website/compose.yml up -d --wait

Then visit http://YOUR_PUBLIC_IP:8088/. Bind only to loopback when placing the site behind a reverse proxy:

WEBSITE_BIND_IP=127.0.0.1 WEBSITE_PORT=8088 \
  docker compose --env-file /dev/null -f deploy/website/compose.yml up -d --wait

For a domain, point its DNS record to your host and terminate HTTPS at your chosen reverse proxy. If you later expose the actual MCP service, follow the deployment guide for its separate authenticated HTTPS endpoint. The public documentation server does not expose that service.

Update or stop

Rebuild dist/site/ after changing public documentation, skills, contracts or the landing page. The read-only directory mount serves the new files. Verify the introduction and guide after rebuilding.

curl --fail http://127.0.0.1/
curl --fail --head http://127.0.0.1/docs/usage-guide.html
docker compose --env-file /dev/null -f deploy/website/compose.yml ps
docker compose --env-file /dev/null -f deploy/website/compose.yml logs --tail 30
docker compose --env-file /dev/null -f deploy/website/compose.yml down

The static site works without JavaScript. JavaScript adds accessible workflow tabs and copy buttons; examples are illustrative and never execute tool calls. Clipboard access may be unavailable over plain HTTP on an IP, so copy buttons select the commands for manual copying when necessary. The guide remains downloadable as one HTML file with its existing offline search and examples.

Application and test map#

app/__init__.py

Agent Context Platform application package.

app/api/__init__.py

HTTP API package.

app/api/concurrency.py

One stable HTTP response for optimistic-concurrency conflicts.

RevisionConflict, revision_conflict_handler

CHAPTER 16 / 16
About 2 min read

From zero to a project and reviewed content

This is the extended organization workflow. For the shortest useful evaluation, complete the two-agent handoff first. Research, creator and monitoring workflows can be adopted when your team needs them.

Start only after the operator's staged cutover and real acceptance gates pass. The sequence below uses implemented human APIs through the console; it does not mint a superuser bearer for a human or reuse the old unmanaged walkthrough's single-author approval shortcut.

  1. Owner: accept the operator-provisioned invitation, verify/enroll MFA or use the approved required provider, then inspect effective access. Initial ownership alone supplies no corpus bypass. An independent approver/operator records necessary bounded root/data policy.
  2. Owner → lead: create the permitted team, invite a lead with reviewed NONE/selected/all-in-org policy, expiry and current issuer generation.
  3. Lead → worker: invite within the delegated team. Worker verifies identity and membership; equal emails never merge global identities. Requests need an independent authorized approver and exact current revision.
  4. Agent setup: approve a verified client/sponsor policy. The authenticated recipient generates/copies their token once into a private file. Use Codex, Claude or Gemini instructions and make a permitted test call.
  5. Knowledge: create/read the authorized project, verify the repository's actual behavior, save a bounded fact and retrieve it with another permitted client. Keep private agent memories private.
  6. Research: register bounded local evidence, ingest, inspect snapshots and citations, request independent revision-bound review and separately promote only to authorized same-org targets.
  7. Creator: author an evidence-backed brief/draft, compare immutable versions, request independent review, export and post manually if separately authorized. Record the exact approved publication receipt; no outbound publishing occurs.
  8. Monitor/offboard: use permitted own/team/org summaries and coverage, then suspend/revoke with expected revisions and step-up. Human sessions and future machine/job access recheck current authority. Preserve authored history; reinstatement does not restore revoked descendants.

My security covers own local password/MFA/recovery, verified identity linking and human-session inspection/revocation. SSO-required policy still applies. Switching org rechecks membership/provider, rotates session/CSRF, clears cached queries and selections, offers an explicit unsaved-work choice and guards late responses. Browser Back cannot revive the old policy context. Server checks remain mandatory if a user unhides a disabled button or calls an API directly.

See dashboard, organization management, deployment and verification for complete maintained contracts and the current unresolved release gates.
